entries.heading: Early notification
entries.note: Use for a complete record issued earlier than approximately six months before publication

entries.heading: Advance notification (confirmed)
entries.note: Use for a complete record issued to confirm advance information approximately six months before publication; or for a complete record issued after that date and before information has been confirmed from the book-in-hand

entries.heading: Notification confirmed on publication
entries.note: Use for a complete record issued to confirm advance information at or just before actual publication date, usually from the book-in-hand, or for a complete record issued at any later date

entries.heading: Update (partial)
entries.note: In ONIX 3.0 or later only, use when sending a ‘block update’ record. A block update implies using the supplied block(s) to update the existing record for the product, replacing only the blocks included in the block update, and leaving other blocks unchanged – for example, replacing old information from Blocks 4 and 6 with the newly-received data while retaining information from Blocks 1–3, 5 and 7–8 untouched. In previous ONIX releases, and for ONIX 3.0 or later using other notification types, updating is by replacing the complete record with the newly-received data

entries.heading: Delete
entries.note: Use when sending an instruction to delete a record which was previously issued. Note that a Delete instruction should NOT be used when a product is cancelled, put out of print, or otherwise withdrawn from sale: this should be handled as a change of Publishing status, leaving the receiver to decide whether to retain or delete the record. A Delete instruction is used ONLY when there is a particular reason to withdraw a record completely, eg because it was issued in error

entries.heading: Notice of sale
entries.note: Notice of sale of a product, from one publisher to another: sent by the publisher disposing of the product

entries.heading: Notice of acquisition
entries.note: Notice of acquisition of a product, by one publisher from another: sent by the acquiring publisher

entries.heading: Test update (partial)
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. Record may be processed for test purposes, but data should be discarded when testing is complete. Sender must ensure the <RecordReference> matches a previously-sent Test record

entries.heading: Test record
entries.note: Record may be processed for test purposes, but data should be discarded when testing is complete. Sender must ensure the <RecordReference> does not match any previously-sent live product record

entries.heading: Single-component, not available separately
entries.note: Used only when an ONIX record is required for a component-as-an-item, even though it is not currently available as such

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product
entries.note: Multiple-component product retailed as a whole

entries.heading: Multiple-item collection, retailed as separate parts
entries.note: Used only when an ONIX record is required for a collection-as-a-whole, even though it is not currently retailed as such

entries.heading: Trade-only product
entries.note: Product available to the book trade, but not for retail sale, and not carrying retail items, eg empty dumpbin, empty counterpack, promotional material

entries.heading: Multiple-item trade-only pack
entries.note: Product available to the book trade, but not for general retail sale as a whole. It carries multiple components for retailing as separate items, eg shrink-wrapped trade pack, filled dumpbin, filled counterpack

entries.heading: Multiple-item pack
entries.note: Carrying multiple components, primarily for retailing as separate items. The pack may be split and retailed as separate items OR retailed as a single item. Use instead of Multiple-item trade-only pack (code 30) if the data provider specifically wishes to make explicit that the pack may optionally be retailed as a whole

entries.heading: Publisher’s distributor
entries.note: Use to designate a distributor providing primary warehousing and fulfillment for a publisher or for a publisher’s sales agent, as distinct from a wholesaler

entries.heading: Bibliographic agency
entries.note: Bibliographic data aggregator

entries.heading: Library bookseller
entries.note: Library supplier. Bookseller selling to libraries (including academic libraries)

entries.heading: Publisher’s sales agent
entries.note: Use for a publisher’s sales agent responsible for marketing the publisher’s products within a territory, as opposed to a publisher’s distributor who fulfills orders but does not market

entries.heading: Publisher’s conversion service provider
entries.note: Downstream provider of e-publication format conversion services (who might also be a distributor or retailer of the converted e-publication), supplying metadata on behalf of the publisher. The assigned ISBN is taken from the publisher’s ISBN prefix

entries.heading: Conversion service provider
entries.note: Downstream provider of e-publication format conversion services (who might also be a distributor or retailer of the converted e-publication), supplying metadata on behalf of the publisher. The assigned ISBN is taken from the service provider’s prefix (whether or not the service provider dedicates that prefix to a particular publisher)

entries.heading: ISTC Registration Agency
entries.note: Deprecated: the ISTC was withdrawn as a standard in 2021

entries.heading: Retail bookseller
entries.note: Bookseller selling primarily to consumers

entries.heading: Education bookseller
entries.note: Bookseller selling primarily to educational institutions

entries.heading: Library
entries.note: Library service providing enhanced metadata to publishers or other parties

entries.heading: Proprietary product ID scheme
entries.note: For example, a publisher’s or wholesaler’s product number or SKU. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required with proprietary identifiers

entries.heading: ISBN-10
entries.note: International Standard Book Number, pre-2007 (10 digits, or 9 digits plus X, without spaces or hyphens) – now Deprecated in ONIX for Books, except where providing historical information for compatibility with legacy systems. It should only be used in relation to products published before 2007 – when ISBN-13 superseded it – and should never be used as the ONLY identifier (it should always be accompanied by the correct GTIN-13 / ISBN-13)

entries.heading: GTIN-13
entries.note: GS1 Global Trade Item Number, formerly known as EAN article number (13 digits, without spaces or hyphens)

entries.heading: UPC
entries.note: UPC product number (12 digits, without spaces or hyphens)

entries.heading: ISMN-10
entries.note: International Standard Music Number, pre-2008 (M plus nine digits, without spaces or hyphens) – now Deprecated in ONIX for Books, except where providing historical information for compatibility with legacy systems. It should only be used in relation to products published before 2008 – when ISMN-13 superseded it – and should never be used as the ONLY identifier (it should always be accompanied by the correct GTIN-12 / ISMN-13)

entries.heading: DOI
entries.note: Digital Object Identifier (variable length and character set, beginning ‘10.’ and without https://doi.org/ or the older http://dx.doi.org/)

entries.heading: LCCN
entries.note: Library of Congress Control Number in normalized form (up to 12 characters, alphanumeric)

entries.heading: GTIN-14
entries.note: GS1 Global Trade Item Number (14 digits, without spaces or hyphens)

entries.heading: ISBN-13
entries.note: International Standard Book Number, from 2007 (13 digits starting 978 or 9791–9799, without spaces or hyphens)

entries.heading: Legal deposit number
entries.note: The number assigned to a publication as part of a national legal deposit process

entries.heading: URN
entries.note: Uniform Resource Name: note that in trade applications an ISBN must be sent as a GTIN-13 and, where required, as an ISBN-13 – it should not be sent as a URN

entries.heading: OCLC number
entries.note: A unique number assigned to a bibliographic item by OCLC

entries.heading: Co-publisher’s ISBN-13
entries.note: An ISBN-13 assigned by a co-publisher. The ‘main’ ISBN sent with <ProductIDType> codes 03 and/or 15 should always be the ISBN that is used for ordering from the supplier identified in <SupplyDetail>. However, ISBN rules allow a co-published title to carry more than one ISBN. The co-publisher should be identified in an instance of the <Publisher> composite, with the applicable <PublishingRole> code

entries.heading: ISMN-13
entries.note: International Standard Music Number, from 2008 (13-digit number starting 9790, without spaces or hyphens)

entries.heading: ISBN-A
entries.note: Actionable ISBN, in fact a special DOI incorporating the ISBN-13 within the DOI syntax. Begins ‘10.978.’ or ‘10.979.’ and includes a / character between the registrant element (publisher prefix) and publication element of the ISBN, eg 10.978.000/1234567. Note the ISBN-A should always be accompanied by the ISBN itself, using <ProductIDType> codes 03 and/or 15

entries.heading: JP e-code
entries.note: E-publication identifier controlled by JPOIID’s Committee for Research and Management of Electronic Publishing Codes. 20 alphanumeric characters, without spaces, beginning with the ISBN ‘registrant element’

entries.heading: OLCC number
entries.note: Unique number assigned by the Chinese Online Library Cataloging Center (see http://olcc.nlc.gov.cn)

entries.heading: JP Magazine ID
entries.note: Japanese magazine identifier, similar in scope to ISSN but identifying a specific issue of a serial publication. Five digits to identify the periodical, plus a hyphen and two digits to identify the issue

entries.heading: UPC-12+5
entries.note: Used only with comic books and other products which use the UPC extension to identify individual issues or products. Do not use where the UPC-12 itself identifies the specific product, irrespective of any 5-digit extension – use code 04 instead

entries.heading: BNF Control number
entries.note: Numéro de la notice bibliographique BNF

entries.heading: ISSN-13
entries.note: International Standard Serial Number expressed as a GTIN-13, with optional 2- or 5-digit barcode extension (ie 13, 15 or 18 digits starting 977, without spaces or hyphens, with <BarcodeType> codes 02, 12 or 05), and only when the extended ISSN is used specifically as a product identifier (ie when the two publisher-defined ‘variant’ digits within the ISSN-13 itself and/or the 2- or 5-digit barcode extension are used to identify a single issue of a serial publication for separate sale). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: ARK
entries.note: Archival Resource Key, as a URL (including the address of the ARK resolver provided by eg a national library)

entries.heading: Digital file internal version number
entries.note: Identifier for a specific revision of a particular product file or package of files, changed each time the file or package is modified in any way (eg to correct errors, update the content, or rebuild the package), whether the change is visible to the reader or not). For example, the ‘release identifier’ within an EPUB package such as ‘urn:uuid:a1b0d67e-2e81-4df5-9e67-a64cbe366809@2011-01-01T12:00:00Z’. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WCO Harmonized System
entries.note: World Customs Organization Harmonized Commodity Coding and Description System, the basis of most other commodity code schemes. Use 6 digits, without punctuation. See https://www.wcoomd.org/en/topics/nomenclature/instrument-and-tools/hs-nomenclature-2022-edition.aspx and https://www.wcotradetools.org/en/harmonized-system

entries.heading: UNSPSC
entries.note: UN Standard Product and Service Classification, including national versions adopted without any additions or changes to the codes or their meaning. Use 8 (or occasionally 10) digits, without punctuation

entries.heading: HMRC
entries.note: UK Revenue and Customs classifications, based on the Harmonized System (8 or 10 digits, without punctuation, for exports from and imports into the UK respectively). See https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff

entries.heading: Warenverzeichnis für die Außenhandelsstatistik
entries.note: German export trade classification, based on the Harmonised System

entries.heading: TARIC
entries.note: EU TARIC codes, an extended version of the Harmonized System primarily for imports into the EU. Use 10 digits (very occasionally 11), without punctuation. See https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/customs-4/calculation-customs-duties/customs-tariff/eu-customs-tariff-taric_en

entries.heading: Fondsgroep
entries.note: Centraal Boekhuis free classification field for publishers

entries.heading: Sender’s product category
entries.note: A product category (not a subject classification) assigned by the sender

entries.heading: GAPP Product Class
entries.note: Product classification maintained by the Chinese General Administration of Press and Publication (http://www.gapp.gov.cn)

entries.heading: CPA
entries.note: Statistical Classification of Products by Activity in the European Economic Community, see http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/ramon/nomenclatures/index.cfm?TargetUrl=LST_NOM_DTL&StrNom=CPA_2008. Use 6 digits, without punctuation. For example, printed children’s books are ‘58.11.13’, but the periods are normally ommited in ONIX

entries.heading: NCM
entries.note: Mercosur / Mercosul Common Nomenclature, based on the Harmonised System. Use 8 digits, without punctuation

entries.heading: CPV
entries.note: Common Procurement Vocabulary (2008), used to describe products and services for public tendering and procurement within the EU. Code is a nine digit number (including the check digit), and may also include a space plus an alphanumeric code of two letters and three digits (including the supplementary check digit) from the Supplementary Vocabulary. See https://simap.ted.europa.eu/web/simap/cpv

entries.heading: PKWiU
entries.note: Polish Classification of Products and Services (2015). Use a single letter followed by 2 to 7 digits, without punctuation. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: HTSUS
entries.note: US HTS (or HTSA) commodity codes for import of goods into USA (10 digits including the ‘statistical suffix’, and without punctuation). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://hts.usitc.gov/current

entries.heading: US Schedule B
entries.note: US Schedule B commodity codes for export from USA (10 digits, without punctuation). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See http://uscensus.prod.3ceonline.com

entries.heading: Clave SAT
entries.note: Mexican SAT classification, based on UN SPSC with later modifications (8 digits, without punctuation). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.sat.gob.mx/consultas/53693/catalogo-de-productos-y-servicios

entries.heading: CN (EU Combined Nomenclature)
entries.note: EU Combined Nomenclature commodity codes, an extended version of the Harmonized System primarily for exports from the EU. Use 8 digits, without punctuation. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/content/combined-nomenclature-0

entries.heading: CCT
entries.note: Canadian Customs Tariff scheme, 8 or 10 digits for imports into and exports from Canada. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/trade-commerce/tariff-tarif/menu-eng.html

entries.heading: CACT
entries.note: Australian ‘Working tariff’. Combined Australian Customs Tariff Nomenclature and Statistical Classification. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.abf.gov.au/importing-exporting-and-manufacturing/tariff-classification

entries.heading: NICO
entries.note: Mexican Número de Identificación Comercial, 10 digits for imports into and exports from Mexico. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.snice.gob.mx/cs/avi/snice/nico.ligie.html

entries.heading: TARIC additional code
entries.note: EU TARIC Document codes, 4 alphanumeric characters (usually 1 letter, 3 digits), eg Y129 (for goods outside the scope of EUDR). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: HTSUS additional code
entries.note: HTSUS code for special classification provisions, or temporary legislation and restrictions, particularly from HTSUS chapters 98 and 99 (8 digits, or 10 where a statistical suffix is appropriate), and without punctuation). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://hts.usitc.gov/current

entries.heading: CPPAP
entries.note: Commission paritaire des publications et agences de presse, identifier used in France (mostly for serial publications). 10 characters (4 digits, one letter, then five digits). The initial four digits indicate the month and year of expiry of the CPPAP registration. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Electre genre
entries.note: Typologie de marché géré par Electre (Market segment code maintained by Electre)

entries.heading: UK open market edition
entries.note: An edition from a UK publisher sold only in territories where exclusive rights are not held. Rights details should be carried in PR.21 (in ONIX 2.1) OR P.21 (in ONIX 3.0 or later) as usual

entries.heading: Airport edition
entries.note: In UK, an edition intended primarily for airside sales in UK airports, though it may be available for sale in other territories where exclusive rights are not held. Rights details should be carried in PR.21 (in ONIX 2.1) OR P.21 (in ONIX 3.0 or later) as usual

entries.heading: Sonderausgabe
entries.note: In Germany, a special printing sold at a lower price than the regular hardback

entries.heading: Pocket book
entries.note: In countries where recognized as a distinct trade category, eg France « livre de poche », Germany ,Taschenbuch‘, Italy «tascabile», Spain «libro de bolsillo»

entries.heading: International edition (US)
entries.note: Edition produced solely for sale in designated export markets

entries.heading: Library audio edition
entries.note: Audio product sold in special durable packaging and with a replacement guarantee for the contained cassettes or CDs for a specified shelf-life

entries.heading: US open market edition
entries.note: An edition from a US publisher sold only in territories where exclusive rights are not held. Rights details should be carried in PR.21 (in ONIX 2.1) OR P.21 (in ONIX 3.0 or later) as usual

entries.heading: Livre scolaire, déclaré par l’éditeur
entries.note: In France, a category of book that has a particular legal status, claimed by the publisher

entries.heading: Livre scolaire (non spécifié)
entries.note: In France, a category of book that has a particular legal status, designated independently of the publisher

entries.heading: Supplement to newspaper
entries.note: Edition published for sale only with a newspaper or periodical

entries.heading: Precio libre textbook
entries.note: In Spain, a school textbook for which there is no fixed or suggested retail price and which is supplied by the publisher on terms individually agreed with the bookseller

entries.heading: News outlet edition
entries.note: For editions sold only through newsstands / newsagents

entries.heading: US textbook
entries.note: In the US and Canada, a book that is published primarily for use by students in school or college education as a basis for study. Textbooks published for the elementary and secondary school markets are generally purchased by school districts for the use of students. Textbooks published for the higher education market are generally adopted for use in particular classes by the instructors of those classes. Textbooks are usually not marketed to the general public, which distinguishes them from trade books. Note that trade books adopted for course use are not considered to be textbooks (though a specific education edition of a trade title may be)

entries.heading: E-book short
entries.note: ‘Short’ e-book (sometimes also called a ‘single’), typically containing a single short story, an essay or piece of long-form journalism

entries.heading: Superpocket book
entries.note: In countries where recognized as a distinct trade category, eg Italy «supertascabile». Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Beau-livre
entries.note: Category of books, usually hardcover and of a large format (A4 or larger) and printed on high-quality paper, where the primary features are illustrations, and these are more important than text. Sometimes called ‘coffee-table books’ or ‘art books’ in English. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Podcast
entries.note: Category of audio products typically distinguished by being free of charge (but which may be monetized through advertising content) and episodic. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Periodical
entries.note: Category of books or e-books which are single issues of a periodical publication, sold as independent products. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Catalog
entries.note: Publisher’s or supplier’s catalog (when treated as a product in its own right). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Atlas
entries.note: Category of books containing a linked group of plates, tables, diagrams, lists, often but not always combined with maps or a geographical theme or approach. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Newspaper
entries.note: Daily or weekly. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Proprietary collection ID scheme
entries.note: For example, publisher’s own series ID scheme. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required with proprietary identifiers

entries.heading: ISSN
entries.note: International Standard Serial Number, unhyphenated, 8 digits

entries.heading: German National Bibliography series ID
entries.note: Maintained by the Deutsche Nationalbibliothek

entries.heading: German Books in Print series ID
entries.note: Maintained by VLB

entries.heading: Electre series ID
entries.note: Maintained by Electre Information, France

entries.heading: DOI
entries.note: Digital Object Identifier (variable length and character set, beginning ‘10.’ and without https://doi.org/ or the older http://dx.doi.org/)

entries.heading: ISBN-13
entries.note: Use only where the collection (series or set) is available as a single product

entries.heading: URN
entries.note: Uniform Resource Name using full URN syntax, eg urn:issn:1476-4687 – though where a specific code for the identifier type is available, use of that code (ie code 02 for ISSN) is preferred

entries.heading: JP Magazine ID
entries.note: Japanese magazine identifier, similar in scope to ISSN. Five digits to identify the periodical, without any hyphen or two digit extension. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: BNF Control number
entries.note: French National Bibliography series ID. Identifiant des publications en série maintenu par la Bibliothèque Nationale de France

entries.heading: ARK
entries.note: Archival Resource Key, as a URL (including the address of the ARK resolver provided by eg a national library)

entries.heading: ISSN-L
entries.note: International Standard Serial Number ‘linking ISSN’, used when distinct from the serial ISSN. Unhyphenated, 8 digits. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Undefined
entries.note: Default

entries.heading: Sentence case
entries.note: Initial capitals on first word and subsequently on proper names only, eg ‘The conquest of Mexico’

entries.heading: Title case
entries.note: Initial capitals on first word and subsequently on all significant words (nouns, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, subordinate conjunctions) thereafter. Unless they appear as the first word, articles, prepositions and coordinating conjunctions remain lower case, eg ‘The Conquest of Mexico’

entries.heading: All capitals
entries.note: For example, ‘THE CONQUEST OF MEXICO’. Use only when Sentence or Title case are not possible (for example because of system limitations). Do NOT use simply because title is (correctly) in all caps (eg ‘BBQ USA’)

entries.heading: Distinctive title (book); Cover title (serial); Title of content item, collection, or resource
entries.note: The full text of the distinctive title of the item, without abbreviation or abridgement. For books, generally taken from the title page (see codes 11–15 where an alternative title is provided on cover or spine). Where the item is an omnibus edition containing two or more works by the same author, and there is no separate combined title, a distinctive title may be constructed (by the sender) by concatenating the individual titles, with suitable punctuation, as in ‘Pride and prejudice / Sense and sensibility / Northanger Abbey’. Where the title alone is not distinctive, recipients may add elements taken from a collection title and part number etc to create a distinctive title – but these elements should be provided separately by the sender

entries.heading: ISSN key title of serial
entries.note: Serials only

entries.heading: Title in original language
entries.note: Where the subject of the ONIX record is a translated item

entries.heading: Title acronym or initialism
entries.note: For serials: an acronym or initialism of Title Type 01, eg ‘JAMA’, ‘JACM’

entries.heading: Abbreviated title
entries.note: An abbreviated form of Title Type 01

entries.heading: Title in other language
entries.note: A translation of Title Type 01 or 03, or an independent title, used when the work is translated into another language, sometimes termed a ‘parallel title’

entries.heading: Thematic title of journal issue
entries.note: Serials only: when a journal issue is explicitly devoted to a specified topic

entries.heading: Former title
entries.note: Books or serials: when an item was previously published under another title

entries.heading: Distributor’s title
entries.note: For books: the title carried in a book distributor’s title file: frequently incomplete, and may include elements not properly part of the title. Usually limited in length and character set (eg to about 30 ASCII characters) for use on other e-commerce documentation

entries.heading: Alternative title on cover
entries.note: An alternative title that appears on the cover of a book

entries.heading: Alternative title on back
entries.note: An alternative title that appears on the back of a book

entries.heading: Expanded title
entries.note: An expanded form of the title, eg the title of a school text book with grade and type and other details added to make the title meaningful, where otherwise it would comprise only the curriculum subject. This title type is required for submissions to the Spanish ISBN Agency

entries.heading: Alternative title
entries.note: An alternative title that the book is widely known by, whether it appears on the book or not (including a title used in another market – but see code 06 for translations – or a working title previously used in metadata but replaced before publication)

entries.heading: Alternative title on spine
entries.note: An alternative title that appears on the spine of a book. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Translated from title
entries.note: Where the subject of the ONIX record is a translated item, but has been translated via some intermediate language. Title type 16 is distinct from title type 03. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Proprietary work ID scheme
entries.note: For example, a publisher’s own work ID scheme. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required with proprietary identifiers

entries.heading: ISBN-10
entries.note: 10-character ISBN of manifestation of work, when this is the only work identifier available – now Deprecated in ONIX for Books, except where providing historical information for compatibility with legacy systems. It should only be used in relation to products published before 2007 – when ISBN-13 superseded it – and should never be used as the ONLY identifier (it should always be accompanied by the correct GTIN-13 / ISBN-13 of the manifestation of the work)

entries.heading: DOI
entries.note: Digital Object Identifier (variable length and character set, beginning ‘10.’ and without https://doi.org/ or the older http://dx.doi.org/)

entries.heading: ISTC
entries.note: International Standard Text Code (16 characters: numerals and letters A–F, unhyphenated). Deprecated: the ISTC was withdrawn as a standard in 2021

entries.heading: ISBN-13
entries.note: 13-character ISBN of a manifestation of work, when this is the only work identifier available (13 digits, without spaces or hyphens)

entries.heading: ISRC
entries.note: International Standard Recording Code

entries.heading: ISAN
entries.note: International Standard Audiovisual Number (17 or 26 characters – 16 or 24 hexadecimal digits, plus one or two alphanumeric check characters, and without spaces or hyphens)

entries.heading: EIDR Content ID
entries.note: Entertainment Identifier Registry identifier for an audiovisual work, eg a movie, TV series (a DOI beginning ‘10.5240/’ with a suffix of 21 hexadecimal digits and five hyphens, and without https://doi.org/ or the older http://dx.doi.org/). See ui.eidr.org/search. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: GLIMIR
entries.note: Global Library Manifestation Identifier, OCLC’s ‘manifestation cluster’ ID

entries.heading: OWI
entries.note: OCLC Work Identifier

entries.heading: ISCC
entries.note: International Standard Content Code, a ‘similarity hash’ derived algorithmically from the content itself (see https://iscc.codes). <IDValue> is a sequence comprising the Meta-Code and Content-Code ISCC-UNITSs generated from a digital manifestation of the work, as a variable-length case-insensitive alphanumeric string (or 27 characters including one hyphen if using ISCC v1.0, but this is deprecated). Note alphabetic characters in v1.x ISCCs use Base32 encoding and are conventionally upper case. The ‘ISCC:’ prefix is omitted. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: By (author)
entries.note: Author of a textual work

entries.heading: With
entries.note: With or as told to: ‘ghost’ or secondary author of a literary work (for clarity, should not be used for true ‘ghost’ authors who are not credited on the book and whose existence is secret)

entries.heading: Screenplay by
entries.note: Writer of screenplay or script (film or video)

entries.heading: Libretto by
entries.note: Writer of libretto (opera): see also A31

entries.heading: Lyrics by
entries.note: Author of lyrics (song): see also A31

entries.heading: By (composer)
entries.note: Composer of music

entries.heading: By (artist)
entries.note: Visual artist when named as the primary creator of, eg, a book of reproductions of artworks

entries.heading: By (photographer)
entries.note: Photographer when named as the primary creator of, eg, a book of photographs

entries.heading: Created by
entries.note: For example of an editorial concept, of a board game, etc

entries.heading: From an idea by
entries.note: For example of a plot idea. Implies a less direct association or active participation than ‘created by’

entries.heading: Designed by
entries.note: Use for interior graphic design. See code A36 for cover design, code A12, A35 for interior illustrations or drawings

entries.heading: Illustrated by
entries.note: Artist when named as the creator of artwork which illustrates a text, or the originator (sometimes ‘penciller’ for collaborative art) of the artwork of a graphic novel or comic book

entries.heading: Photographs by
entries.note: Photographer when named as the creator of photographs which illustrate a text

entries.heading: Text by
entries.note: Author of text which accompanies art reproductions or photographs, or which is part of a graphic novel or comic book

entries.heading: Preface by
entries.note: Author of preface

entries.heading: Prologue by
entries.note: Author of prologue

entries.heading: Summary by
entries.note: Author of summary

entries.heading: Supplement by
entries.note: Author of supplement

entries.heading: Afterword by
entries.note: Author of afterword

entries.heading: Notes by
entries.note: Author of notes or annotations: see also A29

entries.heading: Commentaries by
entries.note: Author of commentaries on the main text

entries.heading: Epilogue by
entries.note: Author of epilogue

entries.heading: Foreword by
entries.note: Author of foreword

entries.heading: Introduction by
entries.note: Author of introduction: see also A29

entries.heading: Footnotes by
entries.note: Author / compiler of footnotes

entries.heading: Memoir by
entries.note: Author of memoir accompanying main text

entries.heading: Experiments by
entries.note: Person who carried out experiments reported in the text

entries.heading: Interpreted through
entries.note: Use with narratives drawn from an oral tradition, where no ‘ownership’ of the narrative is claimed. See also B33. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Introduction and notes by
entries.note: Author of introduction and notes: see also A20 and A24

entries.heading: Software written by
entries.note: Writer of computer programs ancillary to the text

entries.heading: Book and lyrics by
entries.note: Author of the textual content of a musical drama: see also A04 and A05

entries.heading: Contributions by
entries.note: Author of additional contributions to the text

entries.heading: Appendix by
entries.note: Author of appendix

entries.heading: Index by
entries.note: Compiler of index

entries.heading: Cover design or artwork by
entries.note: Use also for the cover artist of a graphic novel or comic book if named separately. Prefer code A56 to credit a graphic designer separately from the creator of the cover artwork

entries.heading: Preliminary work by
entries.note: Responsible for preliminary work on which the work is based

entries.heading: Original author
entries.note: Author of the first edition (usually of a standard work) who is not an author of the current edition

entries.heading: Maps by
entries.note: Maps drawn or otherwise contributed by

entries.heading: Inked or colored by
entries.note: Use for secondary creators when separate persons are named as having respectively drawn and inked / colored / finished artwork, eg for a graphic novel or comic book. Use with A12 for ‘drawn by’. Use A40 for ‘finished by’, but prefer more specific codes A46 to A48 instead of A40 unless the more specific secondary roles are inappropriate, unclear or unavailable

entries.heading: Paper engineering by
entries.note: Designer or paper engineer of die-cuts, press-outs or of pop-ups in a pop-up book, who may be different from the illustrator

entries.heading: Continued by
entries.note: Use where a standard work is being continued by somebody other than the original author

entries.heading: Comic script by
entries.note: Writer of dialogue, captions in a comic book (following an outline by the primary writer)

entries.heading: Inker
entries.note: Renders final comic book line art based on work of the illustrator or penciller (code A12). Preferred to code A40

entries.heading: Colorist
entries.note: Provides comic book color art and effects. Preferred to code A40

entries.heading: Letterer
entries.note: Creates comic book text balloons and other text elements (where this is a distinct role from script writer and/or illustrator), or creates calligraphy in non-comic products

entries.heading: Cover inker
entries.note: Renders final comic book cover line art based on work of the cover designer (code A36), where different from the inker of the interior line art. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Cover colorist
entries.note: Provides comic book cover color art and effects, where different from the colorist of the interior art and effects. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Research by
entries.note: Person or organization responsible for performing research on which the work is based. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Original character design
entries.note: (for comic books). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Cover graphic design by
entries.note: Use where the overall graphic designer of the cover is credited separately from the creator of the cover artwork. Use code A36 for the creator of the cover artwork (who could be a photographer, illustrator etc), or where only a single cover creator is credited. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Other primary creator
entries.note: Other type of primary creator not specified above

entries.heading: Adapted by
entries.note: See also B22 (Dramatized by)

entries.heading: Translated with commentary by
entries.note: This code applies where a translator has provided a commentary on issues relating to the translation. If the translator has also provided a commentary on the work itself, codes B06 and A21 should be used

entries.heading: Series edited by
entries.note: Name of a series editor when the product belongs to a series

entries.heading: Founded by
entries.note: Usually the founder editor of a serial publication (de: Begruendet von)

entries.heading: Consultant editor
entries.note: Use also for ‘advisory editor’, ‘series advisor’, ‘editorial consultant’ etc

entries.heading: Dramatized by
entries.note: See also B05 (Adapted by)

entries.heading: General rapporteur
entries.note: In Europe, an expert editor who takes responsibility for the legal content of a collaborative law volume

entries.heading: Literary editor
entries.note: Editor who is responsible for establishing the text used in an edition of a literary work, where this is recognized as a distinctive role (es: editor literario)

entries.heading: Technical editor
entries.note: Responsible for the technical accuracy and language, may also be involved in coordinating and preparing technical material for publication

entries.heading: Scientific editor
entries.note: Responsible overall for the scientific content of the publication

entries.heading: Historical advisor
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Original editor
entries.note: Editor of the first edition (usually of a standard work) who is not an editor of the current edition. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Translation revised by
entries.note: Where possible, use with B06 for the original translator. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Transcribed by
entries.note: As told to. Use with narratives drawn from an oral tradition, and with B03 (Retold by), B07 (As told by) or A28 (Interpreted through). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Sensitivity reader / editor
entries.note: Reader or editor responsible for ensuring the text is free of offensive, potentially offensive or insensitive language, is inclusive and free from bias, and avoids stereotypical characterization. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Image descriptions by
entries.note: Creator of alternative image descriptions for accessibility purposes. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Text modernized or updated by
entries.note: Use for modernization or minor updating of language, but not for original contributions to the text. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Other adaptation by
entries.note: Other type of adaptation or editing not specified above

entries.heading: Compiled by
entries.note: For puzzles, directories, statistics, etc

entries.heading: Selected by
entries.note: For textual material (eg for an anthology)

entries.heading: Non-text material selected by
entries.note: Eg for a collection of photographs etc

entries.heading: Curated by
entries.note: Eg for an exhibition

entries.heading: Other compilation by
entries.note: Other type of compilation not specified above

entries.heading: Producer
entries.note: Of a film, of a theatrical or multimedia production, of dramatized audio etc

entries.heading: Director
entries.note: Of a film, of a theatrical or multimedia production, of dramatized audio etc

entries.heading: Conductor
entries.note: Conductor of a musical performance

entries.heading: Choreographer
entries.note: Of a dance performance. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Other direction by
entries.note: Other type of direction not specified above

entries.heading: Actor
entries.note: Performer in a dramatized production (including a voice actor in an audio production)

entries.heading: Narrator
entries.note: Where the narrator is a character in a dramatized production (including a voice actor in an audio production). For the ‘narrator’ of a non-dramatized audiobook, use code E07

entries.heading: Vocal soloist
entries.note: Singer etc

entries.heading: Read by
entries.note: Reader of recorded text, as in an audiobook

entries.heading: Performed by (orchestra, band, ensemble)
entries.note: Name of a musical group in a performing role

entries.heading: Speaker
entries.note: Of a speech, lecture etc

entries.heading: Presenter
entries.note: Introduces and links other contributors and material, eg within a documentary

entries.heading: Introduction read by
entries.note: Reader of recorded introduction (or other ‘front matter’) in an audiobook. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Performed by
entries.note: Other type of performer not specified above: use for a recorded performance which does not fit a category above, eg a performance by a stand-up comedian

entries.heading: Filmed / photographed by
entries.note: Cinematographer, etc

entries.heading: Other recording by
entries.note: Other type of recording not specified above

entries.heading: Assisted by
entries.note: Contributor must follow another contributor with any contributor role, and placement should therefore be controlled by contributor sequence numbering to ensure the correct association

entries.heading: Enacting jurisdiction
entries.note: For publication of laws, regulations, rulings etc. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Peer reviewed
entries.note: Use with <UnnamedPersons> code 02 as a ‘flag’ to indicate the publication is anonymously peer-reviewed. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Posthumously completed by
entries.note: Contributor must follow another (posthumous) contributor with any contributor role, and placement should therefore be controlled by contributor sequence numbering to ensure the correct association. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: In association with
entries.note: Contributor must follow another contributor with any contributor role, and placement should therefore be controlled by contributor sequence numbering to ensure the correct association. See also ‘published in association with’ in List 45. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: (Various roles)
entries.note: For use ONLY with ‘et al’ or ‘Various’ within <UnnamedPersons>, where the roles of the multiple contributors vary

entries.heading: Other
entries.note: Other creative responsibility not falling within A to F above

entries.heading: Unspecified
entries.note: Usually the name as it is presented on the book

entries.heading: Pseudonym
entries.note: ‘Pen name’, usually adopted for anonymity, semi-anonymity or for ‘branding’ purposes. May be used to give a well-known pseudonym, where another name is a ‘real’ name

entries.heading: Earlier name
entries.note: Use only within <AlternativeName>

entries.heading: ‘Real’ name
entries.note: May be used to identify a ‘real’ name, where another name is a pseudonym, professional name or is unnamed

entries.heading: Transliterated / translated form of primary name
entries.note: Use only within <AlternativeName>, when the primary name type is unspecified, for names in a different script or language

entries.heading: Later name
entries.note: Use only within <AlternativeName>

entries.heading: Fictional character name
entries.note: Use only within <NameAsSubject> to indicate the subject is fictional, or in <AlternativeName> alongside <UnnamedPersons> to indicate a human-like name for a synthetic voice or AI. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Acronym / initialism
entries.note: Use only within <AlternativeName> with a corporate name to indicate the name is an acronym, initialism or short abbreviation for the full name. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Professional name
entries.note: Name other than a ‘pen name’ adopted for professional purposes (eg a ‘stage name’). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Anonymous
entries.note: Note that Anonymous can be interpreted as singular or plural. A real name can be provided using <AlternativeName> where it is generally known

entries.heading: et al
entries.note: And others. Use when some but not all contributors are listed individually, perhaps because the complete contributor list is impractically long

entries.heading: Various
entries.note: When there are multiple contributors, and none are listed individually. Use for example when the product is a pack of books by different authors

entries.heading: Synthesized voice – male
entries.note: Use for example with Contributor role code E07 ‘read by’ for audio books with digital narration having a male-inflected tone. ‘Brand name’ of voice may be provided in <AlternativeName>

entries.heading: Synthesized voice – female
entries.note: Use for example with Contributor role code E07 ‘read by’ for audio books with digital narration having a female-inflected tone. ‘Brand name’ of voice may be provided in <AlternativeName>

entries.heading: Synthesized voice – unspecified
entries.note: Use for example with Contributor role code E07 ‘read by’ for audio books with digital narration

entries.heading: Synthesized voice – based on real voice actor
entries.note: Sometimes termed an ‘Authorized Voice Replica’. Use for example with Contributor role code E07 ‘read by’ for audio books with digital narration, and provide name of voice actor in <AlternativeName>. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: AI (Artificial intelligence)
entries.note: Use when the creator (of text, of images etc) is a generative AI model or technique. Note, can also be combined with the role ‘assisted by’. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Publication linked to conference
entries.note: For example an academic, professional or political conference

entries.heading: Publication linked to sporting event
entries.note: For example a competitive match, fixture series or championship

entries.heading: Programme or guide for sporting event
Publication linked to artistic event
entries.note: For example a theatrical or musical event or performance, a season of events or performances, or an exhibition of art

entries.heading: Programme or guide for artistic event
Publication linked to exposition
entries.note: For example a commercial exposition

entries.heading: Abridged edition
entries.note: Content has been shortened: use for abridged, shortened, concise, condensed

entries.heading: Acting edition
entries.note: Version of a play or script intended for use of those directly involved in a production, usually including full stage directions in addition to the text of the script

entries.heading: Adapted edition
entries.note: Content has been adapted to serve a different purpose or audience, or from one medium to another: use for dramatization, novelization etc. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the exact nature of the adaptation

entries.heading: Alternate
entries.note: Do not use. Deprecated, but retained in the list for reasons of backwards compatibility. Not for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Annotated edition
entries.note: Content is augmented by the addition of notes

entries.heading: Anniversary edition
entries.note: Edition published to mark a special anniversary of first publication of the content. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the nature of the anniversary. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Bilingual edition
entries.note: Both languages should be specified in the <Language> group. Use MLL for an edition in more than two languages

entries.heading: Bilingual ‘facing page’ edition
entries.note: Use only where the two languages are presented in parallel on facing pages, or in parallel columns of text on a single page (otherwise use BLL). Both languages should be specified in the <Language> group

entries.heading: Braille edition
entries.note: Braille edition

entries.heading: Budget edition
entries.note: Product sold at lower price than other editions, usually with lower quality paper or binding to reduce production costs. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Combined volume
entries.note: An edition in which two or more works also published separately are combined in a single volume; AKA ‘omnibus edition’ or occasionally ‘bind-up’, or in comic books a ‘trade paperback’ (fr: ‘intégrale’)

entries.heading: Critical edition
entries.note: Content includes critical commentary on the text

entries.heading: Coursepack
entries.note: Content was compiled for a specified educational course

entries.heading: Digital original
entries.note: A digital product that, at the time of publication, has or had no physical counterpart and that is or was not expected to have a physical counterpart for a reasonable time (recommended at least 30 days following publication)

entries.heading: Enhanced edition
entries.note: Use for e-publications that have been enhanced with additional text, speech, other audio, video, interactive or other content

entries.heading: Enlarged edition
entries.note: Content has been enlarged or expanded from that of a previous edition, with significant additions to the original content – for example additional chapters. Do not use where the only additions are not a part of the original work (eg ‘teaser chapters’ from another work)

entries.heading: Easy-to-read edition
entries.note: Book which uses highly simplified wording, clear page layout and typography to ensure the content can be understood by those with intellectual disabilities. See https://www.inclusion-europe.eu/easy-to-read for guidelines. See also SMP for editions with simplified language. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Expurgated edition
entries.note: ‘Offensive’ content has been removed

entries.heading: Facsimile edition
entries.note: Exact reproduction of the content and format of a previous edition

entries.heading: Festschrift
entries.note: A collection of writings published in honor of a person, an institution or a society

entries.heading: High readability edition
entries.note: Edition optimized for high readability, typically featuring colored or tinted page backgrounds to reduce contrast, extra letter, word and line spacing to reduce crowding and isolate individual words, simplified page layouts and an open, sans serif font (or occasionally, an unusual font design) intended to aid readability. Sometimes labelled ‘dyslexia-friendly’. See also code SMP if the text itself is simplified, and codes LTE or ULP if the type size is significantly larger than normal. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Illustrated edition
entries.note: Content includes extensive illustrations which are not part of other editions

entries.heading: International edition
entries.note: A product aimed specifically at markets other than the country of original publication, usually titled as an ‘International edition’ and with specification and/or content changes

entries.heading: Large type / large print edition
entries.note: Large print edition, print sizes 14 to 19pt – see also ULP

entries.heading: Microprint edition
entries.note: A printed edition in a type size too small to be read without a magnifying glass

entries.heading: Media tie-in
entries.note: An edition published to coincide with the release of a film, TV program, or electronic game based on the same work. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the exact nature of the tie-in

entries.heading: Multilingual edition
entries.note: All languages should be specified in the ‘Language’ group. Use BLL for a bilingual edition

entries.heading: New edition
entries.note: Where no other information is given, or no other coded type or edition numbering is applicable

entries.heading: Edition with numbered copies
entries.note: A limited or collectors’ edition in which each copy is individually numbered, and the actual number of copies is strictly limited. Note that the supplier may limit the number of orders fulfilled per retail outlet. Use <EditionStatement> to give details of the number of copies printed

entries.heading: Paperback original
entries.note: A product published in any form of soft cover, that at the time of publication, has or had no counterpart in any other format, and that is or was not expected to have such a counterpart for a reasonable time (recommended at least 30 days following publication). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Prebound edition
entries.note: Book that was previously bound, normally as a paperback, and has been rebound with, for example, a library-quality hardcover binding, or a lay-flat binding, by a supplier other than the original publisher. See also the <Publisher> and <RelatedProduct> composites for other aspects of the treatment of prebound editions in ONIX

entries.heading: Revised edition
entries.note: Content has been revised from that of a previous edition (often used when there has been no corresponding increment in the edition number, or no edition numbering is available)

entries.heading: School edition
entries.note: An edition intended specifically for use in schools

entries.heading: Signed edition
entries.note: Individually autographed by the author(s)

entries.heading: Simplified language edition
entries.note: An edition that uses simplified language, usually for second or additional language learners. See ETR for highly simplified editions for readers with intellectual disabilities

entries.heading: Special edition
entries.note: Use for anniversary, collectors’, de luxe, gift, limited, signed, commemorative or celebratory, tie-in, special variant cover or otherwise special editions, but prefer more specific codes AVS, FST, MDT, NUM, SIG, UNN whenever appropriate. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the exact nature of the special edition

entries.heading: Student edition
entries.note: Where a text is available in both student and teacher’s editions

entries.heading: Teacher’s edition
entries.note: Where a text is available in both student and teacher’s editions; use also for instructor’s or leader’s editions, and for editions intended exclusively for educators where no specific student edition is available

entries.heading: Unabridged edition
entries.note: Where a title has also been published in an abridged edition; also for audiobooks, regardless of whether an abridged audio version also exists

entries.heading: Ultra large print edition
entries.note: For print sizes 20pt and above, and with typefaces designed for the visually impaired – see also LTE

entries.heading: Edition with unnumbered copies
entries.note: A limited or collectors’ edition in which each copy is not individually numbered – but where the actual number of copies is strictly limited. Note that the supplier may limit the number of orders fulfilled per retail outlet. Use <EditionStatement> to give details of the number of copies printed

entries.heading: Unexpurgated edition
entries.note: Content previously considered ‘offensive’ has been restored

entries.heading: Variorum edition
entries.note: Content includes notes by various commentators, and/or includes and compares several variant texts of the same work

entries.heading: Readaloud edition
entries.note: (de: Vorlesebücher) Edition specifically intended and designed for reading aloud (to children). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Original language of a translated text
entries.note: Where the text in the original language is NOT part of the current product

entries.heading: Language of abstracts
entries.note: Where different from language of text: used mainly for serials

entries.heading: Original language in a multilingual edition
entries.note: Where the text in the original language is part of a bilingual or multilingual product

entries.heading: Translated language in a multilingual edition
entries.note: Where the text in a translated language is part of a bilingual or multilingual product

entries.heading: Language of audio track
entries.note: For example, on an audiobook or video product. Use for the only available audio track, or where there are multiple tracks (eg on a DVD), for an alternate language audio track that is NOT the original. (In the latter case, use code 11 for the original language audio if it is included in the product, or code 10 to identify an original language that is not present in the product)

entries.heading: Language of subtitles
entries.note: For example, on a DVD or digital video with closed or open captions / subtitles

entries.heading: Language of original audio track
entries.note: Where the audio in the original language is NOT part of the current product

entries.heading: Original language audio track in a multilingual product
entries.note: Where the audio in the original language is part of a multilingual product with multiple audio tracks

entries.heading: Language of notes
entries.note: Use for the language of footnotes, endnotes, annotations or commentary, instructions or guidance for use etc, where it is different from the language of the main text

entries.heading: Language of introduction / end matter
entries.note: Use for the language of any introductory text, prologue, etc, or epilogue, end matter, etc, where it is different from the language of the main text. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Target language of teaching / learning
entries.note: Eg for the book ‘Ingles para latinos’, English. For phrasebooks and language teaching, learning or study material. Wherever possible, the language should also be listed as the subject of the book. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Additional vocabulary / text in this language
entries.note: Use of significant words, phrases, quotations or short passages from a language other than the main language of the text, as an integral part of the text. This does not include ‘loanwords’, academic Latin, etc. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Main content page count
entries.note: The highest-numbered page in a single numbered sequence of main content, usually the highest Arabic-numbered page in a book; or, for books without page numbers or (rarely) with multiple numbered sequences of main content, the total number of pages that carry the main content of the book. Note that this may include numbered but otherwise blank pages (eg pages inserted to ensure chapters start on a recto page) and may exclude unnumbered (but contentful) pages such as those in inserts / plate sections. It should exclude pages of back matter (eg any index) even when their numbering sequence continues from the main content. Either this or the Content Page count is the preferred page count for most books for the general reader. For books with substantial front and/or back matter, include also Front matter (03) and Back matter (04) page counts, or Total numbered pages (05). For books with inserts (plate sections), also include Total unnumbered insert page count whenever possible

entries.heading: Total text length
entries.note: Number of words or characters of natural language text

entries.heading: Front matter page count
entries.note: The total number of numbered (usually Roman-numbered) pages that precede the main content of a book. This usually consists of various title and imprint pages, table of contents, an introduction, preface, foreword, etc

entries.heading: Back matter page count
entries.note: The total number of numbered (often Roman-numbered) pages that follow the main content of a book. This usually consists of an afterword, appendices, endnotes, index, etc. It excludes extracts or ‘teaser’ material from other works, and blank (or advertising) pages that are present only for convenience of printing and binding

entries.heading: Total numbered pages
entries.note: The sum of all Roman- and Arabic-numbered pages. Note that this may include numbered but otherwise blank pages (eg pages inserted to ensure chapters start on a recto page) and may exclude unnumbered (but contentful) pages such as those in inserts / plate sections. It is the sum of the main content (00), front matter (03) and back matter (04) page counts

entries.heading: Production page count
entries.note: The total number of pages in a book, including unnumbered pages, front matter, back matter, etc. This includes any extracts or ‘teaser’ material from other works, and blank pages at the back that carry no content and are present only for convenience of printing and binding

entries.heading: Absolute page count
entries.note: The total number of pages of the book counting the cover as page 1. This page count type should be used only for digital publications delivered with fixed pagination

entries.heading: Number of pages in print counterpart
entries.note: The total number of pages (equivalent to the Content page count, code 11) in the print counterpart of a digital product delivered without fixed pagination, or of an audio product

entries.heading: Duration
entries.note: Total duration in time, expressed in the specified extent unit. This is the ‘running time’ equivalent of code 11

entries.heading: Notional number of pages in digital product
entries.note: An estimate of the number of ‘pages’ in a digital product delivered without fixed pagination, and with no print counterpart, given as an indication of the size of the work. Equivalent to code 08, but exclusively for digital or audio products

entries.heading: Content page count
entries.note: The sum of all Roman- and Arabic-numbered and contentful unnumbered pages. Sum of page counts with codes 00, 03, 04 and 12, and also the sum of 05 and 12

entries.heading: Total unnumbered insert page count
entries.note: The total number of unnumbered pages with content inserted within the main content of a book – for example inserts / plate sections that are not numbered

entries.heading: Duration of introductory matter
entries.note: Duration in time, expressed in the specified extent units, of introductory matter. This is the ‘running time’ equivalent of code 03, and comprises any significant amount of running time represented by a musical intro, announcements, titles, introduction or other material prefacing the main content

entries.heading: Duration of main content
entries.note: Duration in time, expressed in the specified extent units, of the main content. This is the ‘running time’ equivalent of code 00, and excludes time represented by announcements, titles, introduction or other prefatory material or ‘back matter’

entries.heading: Duration of back matter
entries.note: Duration in time, expressed in the specified extent units, of any content that follows the main content of a book. This may consist of an afterword, appendices, endnotes, end music etc. It excludes extracts or ‘teaser’ material from other works. This is the ‘running time’ equivalent of code 04

entries.heading: Production duration
entries.note: Duration in time, expressed in the specified extent units, of the complete content of a book. This is the ‘running time’ equivalent of code 06, and includes time represented by musical themes, announcements, titles, introductory and other prefatory material, plus ‘back matter’ such as any afterword, appendices, plus any extracts or ‘teaser’ material from other works

entries.heading: Number of cards
entries.note: In a pack of educational flash cards, playing cards, postcards, greeting cards etc. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Number of write-in pages
entries.note: Count of the number of pages within the main content page count that are blank or substantially blank, intended for the reader to fill in (eg in a journal). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Filesize
entries.note: Approximate size of a digital file or package (in the form it is downloaded), expressed in the specified extent unit

entries.heading: Storage filesize
entries.note: Approximate size of storage space required for a digital file or package in the form in which it is usually stored for use on a device, where this is different from the download filesize (see code 22), and expressed in the specified extent unit. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Physical pieces
entries.note: Unbound sheets or leaves, where ‘pages’ is not appropriate. For example a count of the individual number of cards in a pack. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. For number of pieces in eg a jigsaw, kit, board game, see <ProductFormFeature> and code 22 from list 79

entries.heading: Characters
entries.note: Approximate number of characters (including spaces) of natural language text. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Words
entries.note: Approximate number of words of natural language text

entries.heading: Tracks
entries.note: Of an audiobook on CD (or a similarly divided selection of audio files). Conventionally, each track is 3–6 minutes of running time, and track counts are misleading and inappropriate if the average track duration is significantly more or less than this. Note that track breaks are not necessarily aligned with structural breaks in the text (eg chapter breaks)

entries.heading: Discs
entries.note: Of an audiobook on multiple Red Book audio CDs. Conventionally, each disc is 60–70 minutes of running time, and disc counts are misleading and inappropriate if the average disc duration is significantly more or less than this (for example if the discs are Yellow Book CDs containing mp3 files). Note that disc breaks are not necessarily aligned with structural breaks in the text (eg chapter breaks). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Hours HHH
entries.note: Fill with leading zeroes if any elements are missing

entries.heading: Hours and minutes HHHMM
entries.note: Fill with leading zeroes if any elements are missing

entries.heading: Hours minutes seconds HHHMMSS
entries.note: Fill with leading zeroes if any elements are missing. If centisecond precision is required, use HHHMMSScc. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Chapters
entries.note: Number of chapters (or other similar subdivisions) of the content. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unspecified, see description
entries.note: See description in the <AncillaryContentDescription> element

entries.heading: Halftones, black and white

entries.heading: ISIC
entries.note: International Standard Industry Classification, a classification of economic activities. Use for books that are about a particular industry or economic activity. <SubjectCode> should be a single letter denoting an ISIC section OR a 2-, 3- or 4-digit number denoting an ISIC division, group or class. See http://unstats.un.org/unsd/cr/registry/isic-4.asp

entries.heading: LC Children’s Subject Headings

entries.heading: EuroVoc
entries.note: EuroVoc multilingual thesaurus. <SubjectCode> should be a EuroVoc concept dc:identifier (for example, 2777, ‘refrigerated products’). See http://eurovoc.europa.eu

entries.heading: BISG Educational Taxonomy
entries.note: Controlled vocabulary for educational objectives. See https://www.bisg.org/products/recommendations-for-citing-educational-standards-and-objectives-in-metadata

entries.heading: Keywords (not for display)
entries.note: For indexing and search purposes, MUST not be displayed. Where multiple keywords or keyword phrases are sent, this should be in a single instance of the <SubjectHeadingText> element, and it is recommended that they should be separated by semi-colons. Use of code B2 should be very rare: use B2 in preference to code 20 only where it is important to show the keyword list is specifically NOT for display to purchasers (eg some keywords for a medical textbook may appear offensive if displayed out of context)

entries.heading: Nomenclature Diplôme
entries.note: French higher and vocational educational subject classification, URI http://data.education.fr/voc/scolomfr/scolomfr-voc-029

entries.heading: Key character names
entries.note: For fiction and non-fiction, one or more key names, provided – like keywords – for indexing and search purposes. Where multiple character names are sent, this should be in a single instance of <SubjectHeadingText>, and multiple names should be separated by semi-colons. Note <NameAsSubject> should be used for people who are the central subject of the book. Code B4 may be used for names of lesser importance

entries.heading: Key place names
entries.note: For fiction and non-fiction, one or more key names, provided – like keywords – for indexing and search purposes. Where multiple place names are sent, this should in a single instance of <SubjectHeadingText>, and multiple names should be separated by semi-colons. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: FAST
entries.note: Faceted Application of Subject Terminology, OCLC subject scheme derived from LCSH (see code 04). See https://fast.oclc.org/fast/. Codes are up to 8 digits, for example 1726640 for Historical fiction (see https://id.worldcat.org/fast/1726640). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: NGSS
entries.note: Next Generation Science Standards for K-12 education in the USA (https://www.nextgenscience.org). <SubjectCode> is a code such as 4-PS3-2. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: MVB-Lesemotive
entries.note: MVB classification of ‘reading rationales’, which classify unconscious motives that lead to a book purchase. Categories are assigned and maintained by MVB. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://vlb.de/lesemotive

entries.heading: LOPS21 Subject module
entries.note: Finnish Suomalainen oppiaineluokitus. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Læreplaner-LK20
entries.note: Codes for Norwegian curriculum for primary and secondary education. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See Læreplaner-LK20 at https://www.udir.no/om-udir/data/kl06-grep/

entries.heading: Kompetansemål-LK20
entries.note: Codes for competency aims in the Norwegian curriculum for primary and secondary education. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See Kompetansemål-LK20 at https://www.udir.no/om-udir/data/kl06-grep/

entries.heading: Kompetansemålsett-LK20
entries.note: Codes for sets of competency aims in the Norwegian curriculum for primary and secondary education. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See Kompetansemålsett-LK20 at https://www.udir.no/om-udir/data/kl06-grep/

entries.heading: Tverrfaglige temaer-LK20
entries.note: Codes for interdisciplinary topics in the Norwegian curriculum for primary and secondary education. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See Tverrfaglige temaer-LK20 at https://www.udir.no/om-udir/data/kl06-grep/

entries.heading: CLIL – Type d’article scolaire
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: GAR – Type pédagogique

entries.heading: ISCED-F

See http://uis.unesco.org/sites/default/files/documents/international-standard-classification-of-education-fields-of-education-and-training-2013-detailed-field-descriptions-2015-en.pdf

entries.heading: Klassifikationen von Spielen, Puzzles und Spielwaren
entries.note: German category scheme for games, puzzles and toys. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.ludologie.de/fileadmin/user_upload/PDFs/211126_Kategorisierung_von_Spielen_Puzzles_und_Spielwaren.pdf

entries.heading: NBVok NTSF
entries.note: National Library of Norway genre and form thesaurus. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.nb.no/nbvok/ntsf

entries.heading: JPRO Genre

entries.heading: KAUNO
entries.note: Finnish Ontology for fiction (Finnish: Fiktiivisen aineiston ontologia). See https://finto.fi/kauno/fi/ (in Finnish), https://finto.fi/kauno/sv/ (in Swedish), https://finto.fi/kauno/en/ (in English). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: SLM
entries.note: Finnish genre and form vocabulary (Finnish: Suomalainen lajityyppi ja muotosanasto). See https://finto.fi/slm/fi/ (in Finnish), https://finto.fi/slm/sv/ (in Swedish), https://finto.fi/slm/en/ (in English). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: YSO-places

entries.heading: Norske emneord
entries.note: See https://www.nb.no/nbvok/nb/. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Austlang

Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang

entries.heading: German Tropes list
entries.note: Used for tropes (recurring themes, motifs, patterns of behavior and/or character traits of the main character(s) that run through a work) in German-speaking countries. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.boersenverein.de/interessengruppen/ig-produktmetadaten/best-practices/

entries.heading: General / adult
entries.note: For a non-specialist or ‘popular’ adult audience. Consider also adding an ONIX Adult audience rating

entries.heading: Children
entries.note: For a young audience typically up to about the age of 12, not specifically for any educational purpose. An audience range should also be included

entries.heading: Teenage
entries.note: For a teenage or ‘young adult’ audience typically from about the age of 12 to the late teens, not specifically for any educational purpose. An audience range should also be included

entries.heading: Primary and secondary education
entries.note: Kindergarten, pre-school, primary / elementary or secondary / high school education. Note ‘secondary’ includes both level 2 and level 3 secondary education as defined in UNESCO’s ISCED 2011 (see https://www.uis.unesco.org/en/methods-and-tools/isced). An audience range should also be included

entries.heading: Pre-primary education
entries.note: Equivalent to UNESCO’s ISCED Level 0 – see https://www.uis.unesco.org/en/methods-and-tools/isced (note codes 11–14 are specific subsets of the Primary and secondary education audience, code 04). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Primary education
entries.note: Equivalent to ISCED Level 1. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Lower secondary education
entries.note: Equivalent to ISCED Level 2 (general and vocational). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Upper secondary education
entries.note: Equivalent to ISCED Level 3 (general and vocational). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Tertiary education
entries.note: For tertiary education typically in universities and colleges of higher education, equivalent to ISCED Levels 5–7

entries.heading: Professional and scholarly
entries.note: For an expert adult audience, including professional development and academic research

entries.heading: Adult education
entries.note: For any adult audience in a formal or semi-formal learning setting, eg vocational training and apprenticeships (collectively, equivalent to ISCED Level 4), or practical or recreational learning for adults

entries.heading: EFL / TEFL / TESOL
entries.note: Intended for use in teaching and learning English as a second, non-native or additional language. Indication of the language level (eg CEFR) should be included where possible. An audience range should also be included if the product is (also) suitable for use in primary and secondary education

entries.heading: Second / additional language teaching
entries.note: Intended for use in teaching and learning second, non-native or additional languages (other than English), for example teaching German to Spanish speakers. Indication of the language level (eg CEFR) should be included where possible. An audience range should also be included if the product is (also) suitable for use in primary and secondary education. Prefer code 07 for products specific to teaching English

entries.heading: ONIX audience codes
entries.note: Using a code from List 28

entries.heading: Proprietary audience scheme
entries.note: For example, a publisher’s or retailer’s own audience coding scheme. Note that a distinctive <AudienceCodeTypeName> is required with proprietary coding schemes

entries.heading: MPAA rating
entries.note: Motion Picture Association of America rating applied to movies

entries.heading: BBFC rating
entries.note: British Board of Film Classification rating applied to movies

entries.heading: FSK rating
entries.note: German FSK (Freiwillige Selbstkontrolle der Filmwirtschaft) rating applied to movies

entries.heading: BTLF audience code
entries.note: French Canadian audience code list, used by BTLF for Memento

entries.heading: Electre audience code
entries.note: Audience code used by Electre (France)

entries.heading: ANELE Tipo
entries.note: Spain: educational audience and material type code of the Asociación Nacional de Editores de Libros y Material de Enseñanza

entries.heading: AVI
entries.note: Code list used to specify reading levels for children’s books, used in Flanders, and formerly in the Netherlands – see also code 18

entries.heading: USK rating
entries.note: German USK (Unterhaltungssoftware Selbstkontrolle) rating applied to video or computer games

entries.heading: AWS
entries.note: Audience code used in Flanders

entries.heading: Schulform
