Deprecated – use Thema educational purpose qualifier (eg 4Z-DE-BA – for German Elementary School) in <Subject> instead

entries.heading: Bundesland
entries.note: School region: codelist maintained by VdS Bildungsmedien eV, the German association of educational media publishers, indicating where products are licensed to be used in schools. See http://www.bildungsmedien.de/service/onixlisten/bundesland_onix_codelist29_value13_0408.pdf. Deprecated

entries.heading: Ausbildungsberuf
entries.note: Occupation: codelist for vocational training materials formerly maintained by VdS Bildungsmedien eV, the German association of educational media publishers at http://www.bildungsmedien.de/service/onixlisten/ausbildungsberufe_onix_codelist29_value14_0408.pdf. Deprecated – use Thema educational purpose qualifier (eg 4Z-DE-UH – for specific German professional/vocational qualifications and degrees) in <Subject> instead

entries.heading: Suomalainen kouluasteluokitus
entries.note: Finnish school or college level

entries.heading: CBG age guidance
entries.note: UK Publishers Association, Children’s Book Group, coded indication of intended reader age, carried on book covers

entries.heading: BookData audience code
entries.note: Audience code used in NielsenIQ BookData services

entries.heading: AVI (revised)
entries.note: Code list used to specify reading levels for children’s books, used in the Netherlands – see also code 09

entries.heading: Lexile measure
entries.note: Lexile measure (the Lexile measure in <AudienceCodeValue> may optionally be prefixed by the Lexile code). Examples might be ‘880L’, ‘AD0L’ or ‘HL600L’. Deprecated – use <Complexity> instead

entries.heading: Fry Readability score
entries.note: Fry readability metric based on number of sentences and syllables per 100 words. Expressed as a number from 1 to 15 in <AudienceCodeValue>. Deprecated – use <Complexity> instead

entries.heading: Japanese Children’s audience code
entries.note: Children’s audience code (対象読者), two-digit encoding of intended target readership from 0–2 years up to High School level

entries.heading: ONIX Adult audience rating
entries.note: Publisher’s rating indicating suitability for a particular adult audience, using an <AudienceCodeValue> from List 203. Should only be used when the ONIX Audience code indicates a general adult audience (code 01 from List 28)

entries.heading: Common European Framework of Reference for Language Learning (CEFR)
entries.note: Codes A1 to C2 indicating standardized level of language learning or teaching material, from beginner to advanced, defined by the Council of Europe (see http://www.coe.int/lang-CEFR)

entries.heading: Korean Publication Ethics Commission rating
entries.note: Rating used in Korea to control selling of books and e-books to minors. Current values are 0 (suitable for all) and 19 (only for sale to ages 19+). See http://www.kpec.or.kr/english/

entries.heading: IoE Book Band
entries.note: UK Institute of Education Book Bands for Guided Reading scheme (see http://www.ioe.ac.uk/research/4664.html). <AudienceCodeValue> is a color, eg ‘Pink A’ or ‘Copper’. Deprecated – use <Complexity> instead

entries.heading: FSK Lehr-/Infoprogramm
entries.note: Used for German videos / DVDs with educational or informative content; value for <AudienceCodeValue> must be either ‘Infoprogramm gemäß § 14 JuSchG’ or ‘Lehrprogramm gemäß § 14 JuSchG’

entries.heading: Intended audience language
entries.note: Where this is different from the language of the text of the book recorded in <Language>. <AudienceCodeValue> should be a value from List 74

entries.heading: PEGI rating
entries.note: Pan European Game Information rating used primarily for video games

entries.heading: Gymnasieprogram
entries.note: Code indicating the intended curriculum (eg Naturvetenskapsprogrammet, Estetica programmet) in Swedish higher secondary education

entries.heading: ISCED 2011
entries.note: International Standard Classification of Education levels (2011), eg <AudienceCodeValue> 253 is ‘Lower secondary vocational education, level completion without direct access to upper secondary education’. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See http://uis.unesco.org/en/topic/international-standard-classification-education-isced

entries.heading: US school grade range
entries.note: Values for <AudienceRangeValue> are specified in List 77

entries.heading: UK school grade
entries.note: Values are to be defined by BIC for England and Wales, Scotland and N Ireland

entries.heading: Reading speed, words per minute
entries.note: Values in <AudienceRangeValue> must be integers

entries.heading: Interest age, months
entries.note: For use up to 36 months only, or up to 42 months in Audience range value (2) only: values in <AudienceRangeValue> must be integers. Should not be used when an Audience range with qualifier code 17 is present

entries.heading: Interest age, years
entries.note: Values in <AudienceRangeValue> must be integers

entries.heading: Reading age, years
entries.note: Values in <AudienceRangeValue> must be integers

entries.heading: Spanish school grade
entries.note: Spain: combined grade and region code, maintained by the Ministerio de Educación

entries.heading: Skoletrinn
entries.note: Bokbasen educational level for primary and secondary education

entries.heading: Nivå
entries.note: Swedish educational qualifier (code)

entries.heading: Schulform
entries.note: Deprecated – assigned in error: see List 29

entries.heading: Bundesland
entries.note: Deprecated – assigned in error: see List 29

entries.heading: Ausbildungsberuf
entries.note: Deprecated – assigned in error: see List 29

entries.heading: Canadian school grade range
entries.note: Values for <AudienceRangeValue> are specified in List 77

entries.heading: Finnish Upper secondary school course
entries.note: Lukion kurssi

entries.heading: Chinese School Grade range
entries.note: Values are P, K, 1–17 (including college-level audiences), see List 227

entries.heading: French school cycles / classes
entries.note: Detailed French educational level classification. Values are defined by ScoLOMFR, see http://data.education.fr/voc/scolomfr/scolomfr-voc-022 – Cycles de l’enseignement scolaire. See also code 34

entries.heading: Brazil Education level
entries.note: Nível de Educação do Brasil, see List 238. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: French educational levels
entries.note: Basic French educational level classification. Values are defined by ScoLOMFR. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See http://data.education.fr/voc/scolomfr/scolomfr-voc-012

entries.heading: Finnish Upper secondary school course (2021+)
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Detailed French educational levels
entries.note: Detailed French educational level classification. Values are defined by ScoLOMFR. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See http://data.education.fr/voc/scolomfr/scolomfr-voc-022 – Niveau éducatif détaillé. See also code 30

entries.heading: GREP Aarstrinn
entries.note: Norwegian educational level for primary and secondary education. See https://www.udir.no/ and https://data.udir.no/kl06/v201906/aarstrinn/

entries.heading: Exact
entries.note: May only be used in Audience range precision (1), and when no Audience range precision (2) is present

entries.heading: From
entries.note: May only be used in Audience range precision (1)

entries.heading: To
entries.note: May be used in Audience range precision (1) when no Audience range precision (2) is present, or in Audience range precision (2) when Audience range precision (1) is code 03

entries.heading: Lexile code
entries.note: For example AD or HL. Deprecated in ONIX 3 – use code 06 instead

entries.heading: Lexile number
entries.note: For example 880L. Deprecated in ONIX 3 – use code 06 instead

entries.heading: Fry Readability score
entries.note: Fry readability metric based on number of sentences and syllables per 100 words. Expressed as an integer from 1 to 15 in <ComplexityCode>

entries.heading: IoE Book Band
entries.note: UK Institute of Education Book Bands for Guided Reading scheme (see https://www.ucl.ac.uk/reading-recovery-europe/ilc/publications/which-book-why). <ComplexityCode> is a color, eg ‘Pink A’ or ‘Copper’

entries.heading: Fountas & Pinnell Text Level Gradient
entries.note: <ComplexityCode> is a code from ‘A’ to Z+’. See http://www.fountasandpinnellleveledbooks.com/aboutLeveledTexts.aspx

entries.heading: Lexile measure
entries.note: The Lexile measure in <ComplexityCode> combines MetaMetrics’ Lexile number (for example 620L or 880L) and optionally the Lexile code (for example AD or HL). Examples might be ‘880L’, ‘AD0L’ or ‘HL600L’. Applies to English text. See https://lexile.com/about-lexile/lexile-overview/

entries.heading: ATOS for Books
entries.note: Advantage-TASA Open Standard book readability score, used for example within the Renaissance Learning Accelerated Reader scheme. <ComplexityCode> is the ‘Book Level’, a real number between 0 and 17. See http://www.renaissance.com/products/accelerated-reader/atos-analyzer

entries.heading: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level
entries.note: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level Formula, a standard readability measure based on the weighted number of syllables per word and words per sentence. <ComplexityCode> is a real number typically between about -1 and 20

entries.heading: Guided Reading Level
entries.note: Use this code for books levelled by the publisher or a third party using the Fountas and Pinnell Guided Reading methodology

entries.heading: Reading Recovery Level
entries.note: Used for books aimed at K-2 literacy intervention. <ComplexityCode> is an integer between 1 and 20

entries.heading: LIX
entries.note: Swedish ‘läsbarhetsindex’ readability index used in Scandinavia. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Lexile Audio measure
entries.note: Lexile Audio measure from MetaMetrics’ Framework for Listening. The code in <ComplexityCode> indicates the difficulty of comprehension of audio material (for example 600L or 1030L). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://lexile.global/the-lexile-framework-for-listening/

entries.heading: Lexile measure (Spanish)
entries.note: Metametrics’ Lexile measure for Spanish text. See https://lexile.com/educators/understanding-lexile-measures/lexile-measures-spanish/ Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: HTML
entries.note: Other than XHTML

entries.heading: XML
entries.note: Other than XHTML

entries.heading: Default text format
entries.note: Default: plain text containing no markup tags of any kind, except for the character entities & and < that XML insists must be used to represent ampersand and less-than characters in textual data, and in the encoding declared at the head of the message or in the XML default (UTF-8 or UTF-16) if there is no explicit declaration

entries.heading: Basic ASCII text
entries.note: Plain text containing no markup tags of any kind, except for the character entities & and < that XML insists must be used to represent ampersand and less-than characters in textual data, and with the character set limited to the ASCII range, i.e. valid characters whose Unicode character numbers lie between 32 (space) and 126 (tilde)

entries.heading: Runner-up
entries.note: Named as being in second place

entries.heading: Commended
entries.note: Cited as being worthy of special attention at the final stage of the judging process, but not named specifically as winner or runner-up. Possible terminology used by a particular prize includes ‘specially commended’ or ‘honored’

entries.heading: Short-listed
entries.note: Title named by the judging process to be one of the final list of candidates, such as a ‘short-list’ from which the winner is selected, or a title named as ‘finalist’

entries.heading: Long-listed
entries.note: Title named by the judging process to be one of the preliminary list of candidates, such as a ‘long-list’ from which first a shorter list or set of finalists is selected, and then the winner is announced

entries.heading: Joint winner
entries.note: Or co-winner

entries.heading: Nominated
entries.note: Selected by judging panel or an official nominating process for final consideration for a prize, award or honor for which no ‘short-list’ or ‘long list’ exists

entries.heading: Textual work
entries.note: A complete work which is published as a content item in a product which carries two or more such works, eg when two or three novels are published in a single omnibus volume

entries.heading: Front matter
entries.note: Text components such as Preface, Introduction etc which appear as preliminaries to the main body of text content in a product

entries.heading: Body matter
entries.note: Text components such as Part, Chapter, Section etc which appear as part of the main body of text content in a product

entries.heading: Back matter
entries.note: Text components such as Index which appear after the main body of text in a product

entries.heading: Proprietary text item ID scheme
entries.note: For example, a publisher’s own identifier scheme for a textual content item. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required with proprietary identifiers

entries.heading: GTIN-13
entries.note: Formerly known as the EAN-13 (unhyphenated)

entries.heading: DOI
entries.note: Digital Object Identifier (variable length and character set, beginning ‘10.’ and without https://doi.org/ or the older http://dx.doi.org/)

entries.heading: PII
entries.note: Publisher item identifier, 17 characters, without punctuation, beginning with B (for book) or S (for serial publications). Deprecated

entries.heading: SICI
entries.note: Serial Item and Contribution Identifier, for serial items only. Deprecated: the SICI was withdrawn as a standard in 2012

entries.heading: ISTC
entries.note: International Standard Text Code (16 characters: numerals and letters A–F, unhyphenated). Deprecated: the ISTC was withdrawn as a standard in 2021

entries.heading: ISBN-13
entries.note: (Unhyphenated)

entries.heading: ISCC
entries.note: International Standard Content Code, a ‘similarity hash’ derived algorithmically from the content itself (see https://iscc.codes). <IDValue> is a sequence comprising the Meta-Code and Content-Code ISCC-UNITSs generated from a digital manifestation of the work, as a variable-length case-insensitive alphanumeric string (or 27 characters including one hyphen if using ISCC v1.0, but this is deprecated). Note alphabetic characters in v1.x ISCCs use Base32 encoding and are conventionally upper case. The ‘ISCC:’ prefix is omitted. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Proprietary name ID scheme
entries.note: For example, a publisher’s own name, contributor or imprint ID scheme. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required with proprietary identifiers

entries.heading: Proprietary
entries.note: Deprecated – use code 01

entries.heading: DNB publisher identifier
entries.note: Deutsche Nationalbibliothek publisher identifier

entries.heading: Börsenverein Verkehrsnummer
entries.note: (de: Verkehrsnummer ded Börsenverein des deutschen Buchhandels)

entries.heading: German ISBN Agency publisher identifier
entries.note: (de: MVB-Kennnummer)

entries.heading: GLN
entries.note: GS1 global location number (formerly EAN location number)

entries.heading: SAN
entries.note: Book trade Standard Address Number – US, UK etc

entries.heading: MARC organization code
entries.note: MARC code list for organizations – see http://www.loc.gov/marc/organizations/orgshome.html

entries.heading: Centraal Boekhuis Relatie ID
entries.note: Trading party identifier used in the Netherlands

entries.heading: Distributeurscode Boekenbank
entries.note: Flemish supplier code. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Fondscode Boekenbank
entries.note: Flemish publisher code

entries.heading: Y-tunnus
entries.note: Business Identity Code (Finland). See http://www.ytj.fi/ (in Finnish)

entries.heading: ISNI
entries.note: International Standard Name Identifier. A sixteen digit number. Usually presented with spaces or hyphens dividing the number into four groups of four digits, but in ONIX the spaces or hyphens should be omitted. See https://isni.org/

entries.heading: PND
entries.note: Personennamendatei – person name authority file used by Deutsche Nationalbibliothek and in other German-speaking countries. See http://www.dnb.de/standardisierung/normdateien/pnd.htm (German) or http://www.dnb.de/eng/standardisierung/normdateien/pnd.htm (English). Deprecated in favor of the GND

entries.heading: NACO
entries.note: A control number assigned to a Library of Congress Control Number (LCCN) Name Authority / NACO record

entries.heading: Japanese Publisher identifier
entries.note: Publisher identifier administered by Japanese ISBN Agency

entries.heading: GKD
entries.note: Gemeinsame Körperschaftsdatei – Corporate Body Authority File in the German-speaking countries. See http://www.dnb.de/standardisierung/normdateien/gkd.htm (German) or http://www.dnb.de/eng/standardisierung/normdateien/gkd.htm (English). Deprecated in favor of the GND

entries.heading: ORCID
entries.note: Open Researcher and Contributor ID. A sixteen digit number. Usually presented with hyphens dividing the number into four groups of four digits, but in ONIX the hyphens should be omitted. See http://www.orcid.org/

entries.heading: GAPP Publisher Identifier
entries.note: Publisher identifier maintained by the Chinese ISBN Agency (GAPP)

entries.heading: VAT Identity Number
entries.note: Identifier for a business organization for VAT purposes, eg within the EU’s VIES system. See http://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/faqvies.do for EU VAT ID formats, which vary from country to country. Generally these consist of a two-letter country code followed by the 8–12 digits of the national VAT ID. Some countries include one or two letters within their VAT ID. See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VAT_identification_number for non-EU countries that maintain similar identifiers. Spaces, dashes etc should be omitted

entries.heading: JP Distribution Identifier
entries.note: 4-digit business organization identifier controlled by the Japanese Publication Wholesalers Association

entries.heading: GND
entries.note: Gemeinsame Normdatei – Joint Authority File in the German-speaking countries. See http://www.dnb.de/EN/gnd (English). Combines the PND, SWD and GKD into a single authority file, and should be used in preference

entries.heading: DUNS
entries.note: Dunn and Bradstreet Universal Numbering System, see http://www.dnb.co.uk/dandb-duns-number

entries.heading: Ringgold ID
entries.note: Ringgold organizational identifier, see http://www.ringgold.com/identify.html

entries.heading: Identifiant Editeur Electre
entries.note: French Electre publisher identifier

entries.heading: EIDR Party ID
entries.note: Entertainment Identifier Registry party identifier (a DOI beginning ‘10.5237/’ with a suffix of 8 hexadecimal digits and one hyphen, and without the https://doi.org/ or the older http://dx.doi.org/), for example ‘10.5237/C9F6-F41F’ (Sam Raimi). See http://eidr.org

entries.heading: Identifiant Marque Electre
entries.note: French Electre imprint Identifier

entries.heading: VIAF ID
entries.note: Virtual Internet Authority File. <IDValue> should be a number. The URI form of the identifier can be created by prefixing the number with ‘https://viaf.org/viaf/’. See https://viaf.org

entries.heading: FundRef DOI
entries.note: DOI used in CrossRef’s Open Funder Registry list of academic research funding bodies, for example ‘10.13039/100010269’ (Wellcome Trust). Use of RORs for funder identifiers is now preferred. See https://www.crossref.org/services/funder-registry/

entries.heading: BNE CN
entries.note: Control number assigned to a Name Authority record by the Biblioteca Nacional de España

entries.heading: BNF Control Number
entries.note: Numéro de la notice de personne BNF

entries.heading: ARK
entries.note: Archival Resource Key, as a URL (including the address of the ARK resolver provided by eg a national library)

entries.heading: Nasjonalt autoritetsregister
entries.note: Nasjonalt autoritetsregister for navn – Norwegian national authority file for personal and corporate names. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: GRID
entries.note: Global Research Identifier Database ID (see https://www.grid.ac). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. Deprecated – ROR is now generally preferred

entries.heading: IDRef
entries.note: Party ID from Identifiers and Standards for Higher Education and Research (fr: Identifiants et Référentiels pour l’enseignement supérieur et la recherche). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://www.idref.fr

entries.heading: IPI
entries.note: Party ID from CISAC’s proprietary Interested Party Information scheme, used primarily in rights and royalties administration. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: ROR
entries.note: Research organization registry identifier (see https://ror.org), leading 0 followed by 8 alphanumeric characters (including 2-digit checksum). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EORI
entries.note: Economic Operators Registration and Identification, identifier for businesses that import into or export from the EU. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: LEI
entries.note: Legal Entity Identifier, administered by the Global LEI Foundation, as 20 alphanumeric characters without spaces or hyphens. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: SIREN
entries.note: French business identifier, issued by the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE). 9 digits, without spaces. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: SIRET
entries.note: French business and location identifier, issued by the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE). 14 digits (the SIREN plus a further five digits), without spaces, or occasionally an alphanumeric code. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Chinese Participant identifier
entries.note: Chinese Participant identifier on the Publishing and distribution public service platform. 12-digits (or 11 digits plus X), usually presented with a / and hyphens dividing the number into groups of three, four and four digits plus a check digit, but in ONIX the / and hyphens should be omitted. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Co-publisher
entries.note: Use where two or more publishers co-publish the exact same product, either under a single ISBN (in which case both publishers are co-publishers), or under different ISBNs (in which case the publisher of THIS ISBN is the publisher and the publishers of OTHER ISBNs are co-publishers. Note this is different from publication of ‘co-editions’

entries.heading: Publisher of original-language version
entries.note: Of a translated work

entries.heading: Published in association with
entries.note: Use also for ‘Published in cooperation with’

entries.heading: New or acquiring publisher
entries.note: When ownership of a product is transferred from one publisher to another

entries.heading: Publishing group
entries.note: The group to which a publisher (publishing role 01) belongs: use only if a publisher has been identified with role code 01

entries.heading: Publisher of facsimile original
entries.note: The publisher of the edition of which a product is a facsimile

entries.heading: Repackager of prebound edition
entries.note: The repackager of a prebound edition that has been assigned its own identifier. (In the US, a ‘prebound edition’ is a book that was previously bound, normally as a paperback, and has been rebound with a library-quality hardcover binding by a supplier other than the original publisher.) Required when the <EditionType> is coded PRB. The original publisher should be named as the ‘publisher’

entries.heading: Former publisher
entries.note: When ownership of a product is transferred from one publisher to another (complement of code 09)

entries.heading: Publication funder
entries.note: Body funding publication fees, if different from the body funding the underlying research. Intended primarily for use with open access publications

entries.heading: Research funder
entries.note: Body funding the research on which publication is based, if different from the body funding the publication. Intended primarily for use with open access publications

entries.heading: Funding body
entries.note: Body funding research and publication. Intended primarily for use with open access publications

entries.heading: Printer
entries.note: Organization responsible for printing a printed product. Supplied primarily to meet legal deposit requirements, and may apply only to the first impression. The organization may also be responsible for binding, when a separate binder is not specified

entries.heading: Binder
entries.note: Organization responsible for binding a printed product (where distinct from the printer). Supplied primarily to meet legal deposit requirements, and may apply only to the first impression

entries.heading: Manufacturer
entries.note: Organization primarily responsible for physical manufacture of a product, when neither Printer nor Binder is directly appropriate (for example, with disc or tape products, or digital products on a physical carrier)

entries.heading: Previous publisher
entries.note: Use for the publisher of earlier manifestations of the work. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Sales rights unknown or unstated for any reason
entries.note: May only be used with the <ROWSalesRightsType> element

entries.heading: For sale, based on publisher’s exclusive publishing rights in the specified territory
For sale, based on publisher’s non-exclusive publishing rights in the specified territory
entries.note: It is possible that a different publisher offers the same content under another ISBN

entries.heading: Not for sale in the specified territory (reason unspecified)
entries.note: Publisher may or may not hold publishing rights – use codes 04–06 instead to provide greater detail

entries.heading: Not for sale in the specified territory (but publisher holds exclusive publishing rights in that territory)
Not for sale in the specified territory (but publisher holds non-exclusive publishing rights in that territory)
Not for sale in the specified territory (because publisher does not hold publishing rights in that territory)
For sale with exclusive rights in the specified countries or territories (sales restriction applies)
entries.note: Only for use with ONIX 3.0. Deprecated

entries.heading: For sale with non-exclusive rights in the specified countries or territories (sales restriction applies)
entries.note: Only for use with ONIX 3.0. Deprecated

entries.heading: Height
entries.note: For a book, the overall height when standing on a shelf. For a folded map, the height when folded. For packaged products, the height of the retail packaging, and for trade-only products, the height of the trade packaging. In general, the height of a product in the form in which it is presented or packaged for retail sale

entries.heading: Width
entries.note: For a book, the overall horizontal dimension of the cover when standing upright. For a folded map, the width when folded. For packaged products, the width of the retail packaging, and for trade-only products, the width of the trade packaging. In general, the width of a product in the form in which it is presented or packaged for retail sale

entries.heading: Thickness
entries.note: For a book, the overall thickness of the spine. For a folded map, the thickness when folded. For packaged products, the depth of the retail packaging, and for trade-only products, the depth of the trade packaging. In general, the thickness or depth of a product in the form in which it is presented or packaged for retail sale

entries.heading: Page trim height
entries.note: Overall height (code 01) is preferred for general use, as it includes the board overhang for hardbacks

entries.heading: Page trim width
entries.note: Overall width (code 02) is preferred for general use, as it includes the board overhang and spine thickness for hardbacks

entries.heading: Unit volume
entries.note: The volume of the product, including any retail packaging. Note the <MeasureUnit> is interpreted as a volumetric unit – for example code cm = cubic centimetres (ie millilitres), and code oz = (US) fluid ounces. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unit capacity
entries.note: Volume of the internal (fluid) contents of a product (eg of paint in a can). Note the <MeasureUnit> is interpreted as a volumetric unit – for example code cm = cubic centimetres (ie millilitres), and code oz = (US) fluid ounces. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unit weight
entries.note: The overall weight of the product, including any retail packaging

entries.heading: Diameter (sphere)
entries.note: Of a globe, for example

entries.heading: Unfolded / unrolled sheet height
entries.note: The height of a folded or rolled sheet map, poster etc when unfolded

entries.heading: Unfolded / unrolled sheet width
entries.note: The width of a folded or rolled sheet map, poster etc when unfolded

entries.heading: Diameter (tube or cylinder)
entries.note: The diameter of the cross-section of a tube or cylinder, usually carrying a rolled sheet product. Use 01 ‘Height’ for the height or length of the tube

entries.heading: Rolled sheet package side measure
entries.note: The length of a side of the cross-section of a long triangular or square package, usually carrying a rolled sheet product. Use 01 ‘Height’ for the height or length of the package

entries.heading: Unpackaged height
entries.note: As height, but of the product without packaging (use only for products supplied in retail packaging, must also supply overall size when packaged using code 01). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unpackaged width
entries.note: As width, but of the product without packaging (use only for products supplied in retail packaging, must also supply overall size when packaged using code 02). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unpackaged thickness
entries.note: As thickness, but of the product without packaging (use only for products supplied in retail packaging, must also supply overall size when packaged using code 03). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Total battery weight
entries.note: Weight of batteries built-in, pre-installed or supplied with the product. Details of the batteries should be provided using <ProductFormFeature>. A per-battery unit weight may be calculated from the number of batteries if required. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Total weight of Lithium
entries.note: Mass or equivalent mass of elemental Lithium within the batteries built-in, pre-installed or supplied with the product (eg a Lithium Iron phosphate battery with 160g of cathode material would have a total of around 7g of Lithium). Details of the batteries must be provided using <ProductFormFeature>. A per-battery unit mass of Lithium may be calculated from the number of batteries if required. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Assembled length
entries.note: For use where product or part of product requires assembly, for example the size of a completed kit, puzzle or assembled display piece. The assembled dimensions may be larger than the product size as supplied. Use only when the unassembled dimensions as supplied (including any retail or trade packaging) are also provided using codes 01, 02 and 03. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unpackaged unit weight
entries.note: Overall unit weight (code 08) is preferred for general use, as it includes the weight of any packaging. Use Unpackaged unit weight only for products supplied in retail packaging, and must also supply overall unit weight. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Carton length
entries.note: Includes packaging. See <PackQuantity> for number of copies of the product per pack, and used only when dimensions of individual copies (codes 01, 02, 03) AND <PackQuantity> are supplied. Note that neither orders nor deliveries have to be aligned with multiples of the pack quantity, but such orders and deliveries may be more convenient to handle. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Carton weight
entries.note: Includes the weight of product(s) within the carton. See <PackQuantity> for number of copies per pack, and used only when the weight of individual copies (code 08) AND <PackQuantity> are supplied. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Pallet length
entries.note: Includes pallet and packaging. See <PalletQuantity> for number of copies of the product per pallet, and used only when dimensions of individual copies (codes 01, 02, 03) AND <PalletQuantity> are supplied. Note that neither orders nor deliveries have to be aligned with multiples of the pallet quantity, but such orders and deliveries may be more convenient to handle. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Pallet weight
entries.note: Includes the weight of product(s) and cartons stacked on the pallet. See <PalletQuantity> for the number of copies per pallet, and used only when the weight of individual copies (code 08) AND <PalletQuantity> are supplied. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later
