entries.heading: Color of cover
entries.note: For Product Form Feature values see code list 98

entries.heading: Color of spine
entries.note: Where it is different from the overall color of the cover (see code 01). For Product Form Feature values see code list 98. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Color of foil (on cover)
entries.note: On cover or spine. For Product form feature values see metallic colors from code list 98. If further detail is required, also use Product form feature description. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Color of foil (on jacket)
entries.note: On dustjacket. For Product Form Feature values see metallic colors from code list 98. If further detail is required, also use Product form feature description. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Color of page edges
entries.note: Sprayed / stained / gilded edges. For Product form feature values see code list 98. For patterned and illustrated page edges, also use Product form feature description or see List 158 code 54

entries.heading: Color of endpapers
entries.note: Or of inside front and back covers. For Product form feature values see Codelist 98. For patterned and illustrated endpapers, also use Product form feature description or see List 158 code 55. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Color of ribbon marker(s)
entries.note: Use also for color of elasticated strap. For Product Form Feature Values see Codelist 98, and with multicolored or multiple ribbons, also use Product Form Feature Description. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Color of head and tail bands
entries.note: Capital bands. For Product form feature values see codelist 98, and with multicolored (eg striped) bands, also use Product form feature description. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Text font
entries.note: The principal font used for body text, when this is a significant aspect of product description, eg for some Bibles, and for large print product. The accompanying <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is text specifying the typeface name. The font size may be specified with the font name, but is preferred separately (in points) in <ProductFormFeatureValue>

entries.heading: Special cover material
entries.note: For Product Form Feature values see code list 99

entries.heading: DVD region
entries.note: For Product Form Feature values see code list 76

entries.heading: Operating system requirements
entries.note: A computer or handheld device operating system required to use a digital product, with version detail if applicable. The accompanying Product Form Feature Value is a code from List 176. Version detail, when applicable, is carried in Product Form Feature Description

entries.heading: Other system requirements
entries.note: Other system requirements for a digital product, described by free text in Product Form Feature Description

entries.heading: ‘Point and listen’ device compatibility
entries.note: Indicates compatibility with proprietary ‘point and listen’ devices such as Ting Pen (http://www.ting.eu), the iSmart Touch and Read Pen. These devices scan invisible codes specially printed on the page to identify the book and position of the word, and the word is then read aloud by the device. The name of the compatible device (or range of devices) should be given in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>

entries.heading: E-publication accessibility detail
entries.note: For <ProductFormFeatureValue> codes, see Codelist 196

entries.heading: E-publication format version
entries.note: For versioned e-book file formats (or in some cases, devices). <ProductFormFeatureValue> should contain the version number as a period-separated list of numbers (eg ‘7’, ‘1.5’ or ‘3.10.7’). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later – in ONIX 2.1, use <EpubTypeVersion> instead. For the most common file formats, code 15 and List 220 is strongly preferred

entries.heading: US CPSIA or other international hazard warning
entries.note: Hazard warning required by US Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act (CPSIA) of 2008 or other US or international legislation. Required, when applicable, for products sold in the US. The Product Form Feature Value is a code from List 143. Further explanation may be given in Product Form Feature Description

entries.heading: EU General Product Safety Regulation and Toy Safety Directive hazard warning
entries.note: Product carries hazard warning, conformity notice or other text required by EU General Product Safety Regulation or Toy Safety Directive. The Product Form Feature Value is a code from List 184, and (for some codes) the exact wording of the warning or text may be given in Product Form Feature Description

entries.heading: IATA Dangerous Goods warning
entries.note: Product Form Feature Description must give further details of the warning

entries.heading: E-publication format version code
entries.note: For common versioned e-book formats (or in some cases, devices) – for example EPUB 2.0.1 or EPUB 3.0. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a code from list 220. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: E-publication format validator version
entries.note: For common versioned e-book formats, the name and version of the validator used to check conformance. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the common name of the validator used (eg EpubCheck, Flightdeck), and <ProductFormFeatureValue> is the version number of the validator (eg 4.0.0a). Use with code 15 (or possibly code 10), or with <EpubTypeVersion>, to specify the version the e-publication conforms with

entries.heading: ‘Point and watch’ device / app compatibility
entries.note: Indicates compatibility with proprietary ‘point and watch‘ devices or apps. These scan invisible codes specially printed on the page, or the whole page image, to identify the book and page position. Scanning can trigger display of (for example) an augmented reality view of the page. The name of the compatible app or device (or range of apps / devices) should be given in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: E-publication authentication and access control
entries.note: Requirement for user authentication prior to use, with detail of authentication method (user enrolment, and login passwords, location- or device-based recognition, authentication via third-party identity service etc) given in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Battery type and safety
entries.note: Use to describe battery requirements, types, hazards and battery safety warnings. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a code from List 242. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Battery capacity
entries.note: Total capacity (of batteries in the product) in Watt hours. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is an integer or decimal number (eg ‘45’, not ‘45Wh’). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Dangerous goods
entries.note: Use to describe regulation of the product for various purposes. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a code from List 243. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Game pieces
entries.note: Number of pieces, eg for jigsaws, puzzles, kits, board games. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is an integer. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. For pieces like cards in a pack, see <Extent> and code 00 from List 24

entries.heading: Game players
entries.note: Number of players, for board games, card games, videogames etc. <ProductFormFeatureValue> must be a required (exact) number as an integer OR a range (eg ‘2–6’), optionally accompanied by the number of players as text (eg ‘suitable for 2–6 players’) in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Game play time
entries.note: Typical time to complete a game, for board games, card games, videogames etc, stated as an integer (in minutes) OR range (eg ‘60–90’) in <ProductFormFeatureValue>, optionally accompanied by the playing time as text (eg ‘typically 60–90 minutes’) in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Personal data requirements
entries.note: Personal data required for registration or use of the product. This can be coded in <ProductFormFeatureValue> (for example using a URI from SCOLOM list 044 – see http://data.education.fr/voc/scolomfr/scolomfr-voc-044) – and/or described in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Not FSC or PEFC certified
entries.note: Product does not carry FSC or PEFC logo. The Product Form Feature Value element is not used. The Product Form Feature Description element may carry free text indicating the grade or type of paper. The product record may also still carry a claimed Pre- and Post-Consumer Waste (PCW) percentage value (type code 37) in a separate repeat of the Product Form Feature composite

entries.heading: FSC certified – pure
entries.note: Product carries FSC logo (Pure, 100%). <ProductFormFeatureValue> is the Certification number (ie either a Chain Of Custody (COC) number or a Trademark License number) printed on the book. Format: Chain of Custody number is two to five letters-COC-six digits (the digits should include leading zeros if necessary), eg ‘AB-COC-001234’ or ‘ABCDE-COC-123456’; Trademark License number is C followed by six digits, eg ‘C005678’ (this would normally be prefixed by ‘FSC®’ when displayed). The Product Form Feature Description element may carry free text indicating the grade or type of paper. By definition, a product certified Pure does not contain Pre- or Post-Consumer-Waste (PCW), so type code 31 can only occur on its own. Certification numbers may be checked at https://info.fsc.org/

entries.heading: FSC certified – mixed sources
entries.note: Product carries FSC logo (Mixed sources, Mix). <ProductFormFeatureValue> is the Certification number (ie either a Chain Of Custody (COC) number or a Trademark License number) printed on the book. Format: Chain of Custody number is two to five letters-COC-six digits (the digits should include leading zeros if necessary), eg ‘AB-COC-001234’ or ‘ABCDE-COC-123456’; Trademark License number is C followed by six digits, eg ‘C005678’ (this would normally be prefixed by ‘FSC®’ when displayed). The Product Form Feature Description element may carry free text indicating the grade or type of paper. May be accompanied by a Pre- and Post-Consumer-Waste (PCW) percentage value, to be reported in another instance of <ProductFormFeature> with type code 36. Certification numbers may be checked at https://info.fsc.org/

entries.heading: FSC certified – recycled
entries.note: Product carries FSC logo (Recycled). <ProductFormFeatureValue> is the Certification number (ie either a Chain Of Custody (COC) number or a Trademark License number) printed on the book. Format: Chain of Custody number is two to five letters-COC-six digits (the digits should include leading zeroes if necessary), eg ‘AB-COC-001234’ or ‘ABCDE-COC-123456’; Trademark License number is C followed by six digits, eg ‘C005678’ (this would normally be prefixed by ‘FSC®’ when displayed). The Product Form Feature Description element may carry free text indicating the grade or type of paper. May be accompanied by a Pre- and Post-Consumer-Waste (PCW) percentage value, to be reported in another instance of <ProductFormFeature> with type code 36, but otherwise assumed to be 100% recycled. Certification numbers may be checked at https://info.fsc.org/

entries.heading: PEFC certified
entries.note: Product carries PEFC logo (certified) or equivalent from PEFC-endorsed national scheme. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is the Chain Of Custody (COC) number printed on the book. The Product Form Feature Description element may carry free text indicating the grade or type of paper. May be accompanied by a Post-Consumer Waste (PCW) percentage value, to be reported in another instance of <ProductFormFeature> with type code 36

entries.heading: PEFC recycled
entries.note: Product carries PEFC logo (recycled) or equivalent from PEFC-endorsed national scheme. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is the Chain Of Custody (COC) number printed on the book. The Product Form Feature Description element may carry free text indicating the grade or type of paper. Should be accompanied by a Post-Consumer-Waste (PCW) percentage value, to be reported in another instance of <ProductFormFeature> with type code 36

entries.heading: FSC or PEFC certified Pre- and Post-Consumer Waste (PCW) percentage
entries.note: The percentage of recycled Pre- and Post-Consumer-Waste (PCW) used in a product where the composition is certified by FSC, PEFC or PEFC-endorsed scheme. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is an integer. May occur together with type code 32, 33, 34 or 35

entries.heading: Claimed Pre- and Post-Consumer Waste (PCW) percentage
entries.note: The percentage of recycled Pre- and Post-Consumer Waste (PCW) claimed to be used in a product where the composition is not certified by FSC or PEFC. <Product FormFeatureValue> is an integer. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry free text supporting the claim. Must be accompanied by type code 30

entries.heading: ‘Green’ inks
entries.note: Vegetable-based or other environmentally-conscious inks and varnishes. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry free text with a more detailed statement. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: ‘Green’ adhesives
entries.note: Product binding uses environmentally-conscious adhesives and other binding materials. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry free text with a more detailed statement. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Paper produced by ‘green’ technology
entries.note: Product made from paper produced using environmentally-conscious technology. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry free text with a more detailed statement

entries.heading: Carbon / GHG emission certification scheme
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a code from List 262 identifying the particular certification scheme. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may be a descriptor for some part, schedule or annex of the certification scheme, where necessary. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Carbon / GHG emission certification / license number
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a code from List 262 identifying a particular certification scheme. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is a certificate or license number used to certify compliance with the scheme. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Carbon / GHG emission certification URL
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a code from List 262 identifying a particular certification scheme. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is a URL linking to a web page certifying compliance with the scheme. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Carbon / GHG Scope 3 certified Carbon dioxide equivalent emission
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a code from List 262 identifying a particular certification scheme. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is a number specifying certified GHG emissions per copy of the product, measured in kilograms of Carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) using the Scope 3 methodology of the scheme. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Carbon / GHG Scope 2 certified Carbon dioxide equivalent emission
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Carbon / GHG Scope 1 certified Carbon dioxide equivalent emission
entries.note: Scope 1 emission certifications are not recommended for use. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (interior or full product)
entries.note: For EU Deforestation regulations, location of raw material source plot (‘where the tree grew’) for the interior or main body of the product (or for the entire product, if the raw material source for the binding and other parts of the product cannot be differentiated). If there are multiple sources for the same raw material, repeat <ProductFormFeature> for each plot or use the ‘list of plots’ option below. Further repeats of <ProductFormFeature> may be used for multiple paper, card and board types. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a country code from List 91 indicating the country in which the source plot is, optionally followed by a space and the name of the species, and optionally followed by a space and the date of harvest of the source plot (YYYY, YYYYMM or YYYYMMDD). A species name may itself consist of the binomial Latin name (the ‘scientific name’), or the binomial Latin name followed by a space plus the common name in parentheses. The common name may only be included if the Latin name is also present. Alternatively, a list of multiple species names from the same source plot may be listed, separated by commas. In such a list, all species names must include both scientific and common name, or all must include a scientific name only. Note there can be up to four types of data (country, a Latin name and a common name, or a comma-separated list of Latin names and common names, and a date), each space separated, but only the country is mandatory. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is a list of points defining one or more plots from which the raw material was harvested, using GPS coordinates with 6 decimal places of precision (these are real numbers, ±90 for latitude [negative numbers indicate a latitude south of the equator], ±180 excluding -180 itself for longitude [negative numbers indicate a longitude west of the Prime Greenwich meridian]). Latitude and Longitude for each point are space-separated, and multiple points are comma-separated. Multiple plots are semicolon separated, and must be in the same country. (Any supplied species name and date must also apply to all plots in the list.) (Note these GPS coordinates use decimal parts of a degree, not minutes and seconds.) ONE point defines the center of a 4 hectare plot (200m × 200m). TWO points define a line joining opposite corners of a ‘square’ plot bounded by two lines of latitude and two of longitude. THREE or more points define a simple polygon outlining the plot. Plot types with one, two or multiple points must not be mixed in a list of multiple plots. Lines and polygon edges may not cross a national boundary or the 180° line of longitude. Polygon edges may not intersect. It is good practice to ensure the polygon is drawn clockwise and is ‘closed’ (that is, that the first and last points are identical, so that for example four points define a triangle). If not closed, the closing polygon edge is implied, and to avoid ambiguity, trailing zeros in the latitude and longitude should be explicit. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (binding)
entries.note: As code 47, but for endpaper, cover card or board, any other binding or covering material and any jacket (but not including any slipcase or other packaging). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (other)
entries.note: As code 47, but for any slipcase or box, retail packaging, supplementary material (but not including any packaging discarded before retail sale). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR due diligence reference
entries.note: For EU Deforestation Regulations, <ProductFormFeatureValue> is the ‘Due Diligence Statement’ (DDS) document reference recorded by the publisher or other organization responsible for the product when a due diligence statement is uploaded to the EU’s portal, expected to be in a format like ‘24FRXVV3VOS991’ (with an optional suffix ‘+’ and a ‘verification code’ expected to be in a format like ‘A4B3C2D1’). This reference is the DDS for the product as a whole. There may also be a UUID acting as an internal or proprietary document reference, for which use <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. <ProductFormFeature> should be repeated if multiple DDSs apply to the product as a whole. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. See https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en

entries.heading: EUDR associated due diligence references
entries.note: For EU Deforestation Regulation, <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a space-separated list of document references for DDSs (including optional verification code) created by upstream operators that are or may be referred to in the DDS for the product as a whole (ie the DDS specified using code 50)) – for example DDSs for the paper types used to manufacture the product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR compliant with national law attestation
entries.note: For EU Deforestation regulations, a ‘flag’ indicating that all raw materials were produced in accordance with legal requirements of one or more countries within each of which there are one or more source plots, and that documentation to verify this is available upon request. <ProductFormFeatureValue> is a space-separated list of country codes from List 91. Presence of code 52 and a country code acts as an positive attestation that the product’s raw materials sourced from the specified country are compliant with the national laws of that country, but the attestation is meaningful only if there is no pre-existing DDS for the product as a whole (presence of a DDS reference already attests the product is compliant with all national laws and that documentation is available). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR deforestation-free attestation
entries.note: For EU Deforestation regulations, a ‘flag’ indicating that all raw materials used for the product are ‘deforestation-free’, and that documentation to verify this is available upon request. Presence of code 53 acts as a positive attestation that the product’s raw materials are deforestation-free, but the attestation is meaningful only if there is no pre-existing DDS for the product as a whole (presence of a DDS reference already attests the product is deforestation-free and that documentation is available). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR stock present attestation
entries.note: For EU Deforestation regulations, a ‘flag’ indicating that no (in-EU) supplier has stock that was not physically present within the EU prior to the enforcement date of the Regulation, and that documentation to verify this is available upon request. Presence of code 54 acts as a positive attestation that all copies of the product held at distributors and wholesalers within the EU pre-dates the enforcement date, but the attestation is meaningful only if there is no pre-existing DDS for the product as a whole (presence of a DDS reference already attests the product is compliant with the regulation and that documentation is available). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR beyond scope attestation
entries.note: For EU Deforestation regulations, a ‘flag’ indicating that the raw materials for the product are entirely outside the scope of the regulations for any reason, for example because a map – that would otherwise be required to conform – is printed on plastic rather than paper, or a book is made wholly of recycled raw materials (including the cover). <ProductClassification> may contain an additional TARIC exemption code. Ensure other Product form features agree, and that documentation is available. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. No other EUDR metadata need be included

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (interior or full product) URL
entries.note: As code 47, but <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the URL of a GeoJSON file outlining the source plot. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (binding) URL
entries.note: As code 48, but <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the URL of a GeoJSON file outlining the source plot. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (other) URL
entries.note: As code 49, but <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the URL of a GeoJSON file outlining the source plot. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (interior or full product) Postal address
entries.note: As code 47, but <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the country and postcode or full postal address of a source plot or of the paper manufacturer or printer (eg GB M10 9KC). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (binding) Postal address
entries.note: As code 48, but <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the country and postcode or full postal address of a source plot or of the paper manufacturer or printer. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EUDR raw material location (other) Postal address
entries.note: As code 49, but <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the country and postcode or full postal address of a source plot or of the paper manufacturer or printer. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Map projection
entries.note: The primary projection used for a cartographic product. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> is the name of the projection, eg Mercator, Winkel tripel projection

entries.heading: No outer packaging
entries.note: No packaging, or all smaller items enclosed inside largest item

entries.heading: Slip-sleeve
entries.note: Thin card or soft plastic sleeve, much less rigid than a slip case

entries.heading: Clamshell
entries.note: Packaging consisting of formed plastic sealed around each side of the product. Not to be confused with single-sided Blister pack

entries.heading: Keep case
entries.note: Typical DVD-style packaging, sometimes known as an ‘Amaray’ case

entries.heading: Jewel case
entries.note: Typical CD-style packaging

entries.heading: Digipak
entries.note: Common CD-style packaging, a card folder with one or more panels incorporating a tray, hub or pocket to hold the disc(s)

entries.heading: Shrink-wrapped (biodegradable)
entries.note: Use for products or product bundles supplied for retail sale in shrink-wrapped packaging, where the shrink-wrap film is biodegradable. For non-degradable film, see code 21. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: In box (with lid)
entries.note: Individual item, items or set in card box with separate or hinged lid: not to be confused with the commonly-used ‘boxed set’ which is more likely to be packaged in a slip case

entries.heading: Slip-cased
entries.note: Slip-case for single item only (de: ‘Schuber’)

entries.heading: Slip-cased set
entries.note: Slip-case for multi-volume set, also commonly referred to as ‘boxed set’ (de: ‘Kassette’)

entries.heading: Tube
entries.note: Rolled in tube or cylinder: eg sheet map or poster

entries.heading: Binder
entries.note: Use for miscellaneous items such as slides, microfiche, when presented in a binder

entries.heading: In wallet or folder
entries.note: Use for miscellaneous items such as slides, microfiche, when presented in a wallet or folder

entries.heading: Long triangular package
entries.note: Long package with triangular cross-section used for rolled sheet maps, posters etc

entries.heading: Long square package
entries.note: Long package with square cross-section used for rolled sheet maps, posters, etc

entries.heading: Pouch
entries.note: In pouch, eg teaching materials in a plastic bag or pouch

entries.heading: Rigid plastic case
entries.note: In duroplastic or other rigid plastic case, eg for a class set

entries.heading: Cardboard case
entries.note: In cardboard case, eg for a class set

entries.heading: Shrink-wrapped
entries.note: Use for products or product bundles supplied for retail sale in shrink-wrapped packaging. For biodegradable shrink-wrap film, prefer code 08. For shrink-wrapped packs of multiple products for trade supply only, see code XL in List 7

entries.heading: Blister pack
entries.note: A pack comprising a pre-formed plastic blister and a printed card with a heat-seal coating

entries.heading: Carry case
entries.note: A case with carrying handle, typically for a set of educational books and/or learning materials

entries.heading: In tin
entries.note: Individual item, items or set in metal box or can with separate or hinged lid

entries.heading: With browse-prevention tape
entries.note: (ja: koguchi tome) Peelable sticker or tape sealing the foredge of a book to prevent pre-purchase reading of the content. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Text
entries.note: Readable text of the main content: this value is required, together with applicable <ProductForm> and <ProductFormDetail> values, to designate an e-book or other digital or physical product whose primary content is text. Note ‘text’ is ‘text as text’, not ‘text as an image’. To indicate the accessibility of this text, this code should be used with relevant values from list 196

entries.heading: Extensive links between internal content
entries.note: E-publication contains a significant number of actionable (clickable) cross-references, hyperlinked notes and annotations, or with other actionable links between largely textual elements (eg quiz / test questions, ‘choose your own ending’ etc)

entries.heading: Extensive links to external content
entries.note: E-publication contains a significant number of actionable (clickable) web links to external content, downloadable resources, supplementary material, etc

entries.heading: Links to external interactive content
entries.note: Publication contains actionable (clickable) links to external interactive content. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Additional text not part of main content
entries.note: Publication contains additional textual content such as an interview, feature article, essay, bibliography, quiz / test, other background material, or text that is not included in a primary or ‘unenhanced’ version. Note ‘text’ is ‘text-as-text’, not ‘text as an image’ or images of text

entries.heading: Text within images
entries.note: Including text-as-text embedded in diagrams, charts, or within images containing speech balloons, thought bubbles, captions etc. Note this does not include ‘text as an image’ or images of text (for which see code 49). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Additional eye-readable links to external content
entries.note: Publication contains a significant number of web links (printed URLs, QR codes etc). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Promotional text for other book product
entries.note: Publication contains supplementary text as promotional content such as, for example, a teaser chapter

entries.heading: Still images / graphics
entries.note: Includes any type of illustrations. To indicate accessibility of the images, use with codes 14, 15, 16, 25, 26 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate. Use only when no more detailed specification is provided

entries.heading: Photographs
entries.note: Whether in a plate section / insert, or not. To indicate accessibility of the images, use with codes 14, 15, 16, 25, 26 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate

entries.heading: Figures, diagrams, charts, graphs
entries.note: Including other ‘mechanical’ (ie non-photographic) illustrations. To indicate accessibility of the images, use with codes 14, 15, 16,25, 26 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate

entries.heading: Additional images / graphics not part of main work
entries.note: Publication is enhanced with additional images or graphical content such as supplementary photographs that are not included in a primary or ‘unenhanced’ version. To indicate accessibility of the images, use with codes 14, 15, and other codes from list 196 as appropriate

entries.heading: Maps and / or other cartographic content
Chemical content
entries.note: Indicates that the publication contains chemical notations, formulae. To indicate accessibility of the images, use with codes 18, 34 or 54, and other codes from list 196 as appropriate. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Mathematical content
entries.note: Indicates that the publication contains mathematical notation, equations, formulae. To indicate accessibility of the images, use with codes 17, 35 or 53 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Decorative images or graphics
entries.note: Publication contains visual content that is purely decorative and are not necessary to understanding of the content. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Assessment material
entries.note: eg Questions or student exercises, problems, quizzes or tests (as an integral part of the work). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Audiobook
entries.note: Audio recording of a reading of a book or other text – typically single voice. To indicate the accessibility of the audio, use with codes 11, 15, 27, 39, and other codes from list 196 as appropriate, and with code V212 from list 175 to indicate availability of a transcript

entries.heading: Audiobook – dual
entries.note: Audio recording of a reading of a book or other text – typically two or multiple voices. Not dramatized: each voice reads a chapter or section written from that character’s point of view. To indicate the accessibility of the audio, use with codes 11, 15, 27, 39 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate, and with code V212 from list 175 to indicate availability of a transcript

entries.heading: Audiobook – duet
entries.note: Audio recording of a reading of a book or other text – typically two or multiple voices. Not fully dramatized: each voice reads a chapter or section written from that character’s point of view, but dialogue is ‘performed’ by alternating voices. To indicate the accessibility of the audio, use with codes 11, 15, 27, 39 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate, and with code V212 from list 175 to indicate availability of a transcript

entries.heading: Performance – spoken word
entries.note: Audio recording of a drama performed by a multi-voice cast, or other spoken word performance. To indicate the accessibility of the audio, use with codes 11, 15, 27, 39 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate, and with code V212 from list 175 to indicate availability of a transcript

entries.heading: Other speech content
entries.note: eg an interview, speech, lecture or commentary / discussion, not a ‘reading’ or ‘performance’). To indicate the accessibility of the audio, use with codes 11, 15, 27, 39 and other codes from list 196 as appropriate, and with code V212 from list 175 to indicate availability of a transcript

entries.heading: Music recording
entries.note: Audio recording of a music performance, including musical drama and opera

entries.heading: Other audio
entries.note: Audio recording of other sound, eg birdsong, sound effects, ASMR material

entries.heading: Images of text
entries.note: At least some text – including text within other images – is ‘text as an image’ (ie a picture of text). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Partial performance – spoken word
entries.note: Audio recording of a reading, performance or dramatization of part of the work

entries.heading: Additional audio content not part of main content
entries.note: Product includes additional pre-recorded audio of any supplementary material such as full or partial reading, lecture, performance, dramatization, interview, background documentary or other audio content not included in the primary or ‘unenhanced’ version

entries.heading: Promotional audio for other book product
entries.note: eg Reading of teaser chapter

entries.heading: Video
entries.note: Includes film, video, animation etc, with or without audio. Use only when no more detailed specification is provided. To indicate the accessibility of the moving images and any accompanying audio, use with code 27, 28, and other codes from list 196, and codes V210, V211, V212, V213, V214 or V215 from list 175 as appropriate

entries.heading: Video content without audio
entries.note: Publication contains video material with no audio recording or narration (but may have music or textual subtitles). To indicate the accessibility of the moving images, use with code 28 and other codes from list 196. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Performance – visual
entries.note: Video recording of a drama or other performance, including musical performance. To indicate the accessibility of the moving images, use with code 28 and other codes from list 196

entries.heading: Animated / interactive illustrations
entries.note: eg animated diagrams, charts, graphs or other illustrations (usually without sound). To indicate accessibility features, use with codes 14, 15, 16, 25, 26, 28 or other codes from list 196 or list 175 as appropriate

entries.heading: Narrative animation
entries.note: eg cartoon, animatic or CGI animation (usually includes sound). To indicate accessibility features, use with code 28 from list 196, and codes V210, V211, V212, V213, V214 or V215 from list 175 as appropriate

entries.heading: Other video
entries.note: Other video content eg interview, not a reading or performance

entries.heading: Partial performance – video
entries.note: Video recording of a reading, performance or dramatization of part of the work

entries.heading: Additional video content not part of main work
entries.note: E-publication is enhanced with video recording of full or partial reading, performance, dramatization, interview, background documentary or other content not included in the primary or ‘unenhanced’ version

entries.heading: Promotional video for other book product
entries.note: eg Book trailer

entries.heading: Game / Puzzle
entries.note: No multi-user functionality. Formerly just ‘Game’

entries.heading: Contest
entries.note: Includes some degree of multi-user functionality

entries.heading: Software
entries.note: Largely ‘content free’

entries.heading: Data
entries.note: Data files

entries.heading: Blank pages or spaces
entries.note: Entire pages or blank spaces, forms, boxes, write-in pages etc, intended to be filled in by the reader

entries.heading: Advertising content
entries.note: Use only where type of advertising content is not stated

entries.heading: Advertising – first party
entries.note: ‘Back ads’ – promotional content for other books (that does not include sample content of those books, cf codes 17, 23)

entries.heading: Advertising – coupons
entries.note: Eg to obtain discounts on other products

entries.heading: Scripting
entries.note: E-publication contains microprograms written (eg) in JavaScript and executed within the reading system. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Scripted pop-ups
entries.note: E-publication contains pop-ups or other functionality offering (eg) term definitions, cross-links or glossary entries [Note this should not include (eg) dictionary functionality that is part of the reading system.] Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Sequential art
entries.note: Or pictorial narrative, usually panel-based. Images displayed in a specific order for the purpose of graphic storytelling or giving information (eg graphic novels, comics and manga). May include text integrated into the image (as speech and thought bubbles, textual ‘sound’ effects, captions etc). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Apocrypha (Catholic canon)
entries.note: The seven portions of the Apocrypha added to the Catholic canon at the Council of Trent in 1546: Tobit; Judith; Wisdom of Solomon; Sirach (Ecclesiasticus); Baruch, including the Letter of Jeremiah; I and II Maccabees; Extra portions of Esther and Daniel (Additions to Esther; the Prayer of Azariah; Song of the Three Jews; Susannah; Bel and the Dragon). These are not generally included in the Protestant canon

entries.heading: Apocrypha (canon unspecified)
entries.note: A collection of Apocryphal texts, canon not specified

entries.heading: Additional Apocryphal texts: Greek Orthodox canon
entries.note: I Esdras; Prayer of Manasseh; Psalm 151; III Maccabees

entries.heading: Additional Apocryphal texts: Slavonic Orthodox canon
entries.note: I and II Esdras; Prayer of Manasseh; Psalm 151; III and IV Maccabees

entries.heading: Additional Apocryphal texts
entries.note: Additional Apocryphal texts included in some Bible versions: I and II Esdras; Prayer of Manasseh

entries.heading: General canon with Apocrypha (Catholic canon)
entries.note: The 66 books included in the Protestant, Catholic and Orthodox canons, together with the seven portions of the Apocrypha included in the Catholic canon. (Equivalent to OT plus NT plus AP)

entries.heading: General canon with Apocryphal texts (canon unspecified)
entries.note: The 66 books included in the Protestant, Catholic and Orthodox canons, together with Apocryphal texts, canon not specified. (Equivalent to OT plus NT plus AQ, 77 books in all)

entries.heading: General canon
entries.note: The 66 books included in the Protestant, Catholic and Orthodox canons, 39 from the Old Testament and 27 from the New Testament. The sequence of books may differ in different canons. (Equivalent to OT plus NT)

entries.heading: Gospels
entries.note: The books of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John

entries.heading: Old Testament
entries.note: Those 39 books which were included in the Jewish canon by the rabbinical academy established at Jamma in 90 CE. Also known as the Jewish or Hebrew scriptures

entries.heading: New Testament
entries.note: The 27 books included in the Christian canon through the Easter Letter of Athanasius, Bishop of Alexandria and also by a general council of the Christian church held near the end of the 4th century CE

entries.heading: New Testament with Psalms and Proverbs
entries.note: Includes the 27 books of the New Testament plus Psalms and Proverbs from the Old Testament. Equivalent to NT plus PP)

entries.heading: Paul’s Epistles
entries.note: The books containing the letters of Paul to the various early Christian churches

entries.heading: Psalms and Proverbs
entries.note: The book of Psalms and the book of Proverbs combined

entries.heading: Psalms
entries.note: The book of Psalms

entries.heading: Pentateuch
entries.note: The first five books of the Bible: Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Leviticus, Deuteronomy. Also applied to the Torah

entries.heading: Other portions
entries.note: Selected books of either the OT or NT not otherwise noted

entries.heading: Alberto Vaccari
entries.note: Alberto Vaccari – Pontificio Istituto Biblico

entries.heading: Amplified
entries.note: (AMP) A translation based on the American Standard Version and showing multiple options for the translation of ancient text. Published in full in 1965. Sponsored by the Lockman Foundation

entries.heading: Antonio Martini
entries.note: Most popular Catholic Bible translation in Italian prior to the CEI translation in 1971

entries.heading: American Standard
entries.note: (ASV) A 1901 translation using verbal equivalence techniques with the purpose of Americanizing the REV

entries.heading: Biblia de las Americas
entries.note: (LBLA) Spanish translation by the Lockman Foundation, first published in 1986 and updated in 1995, 1997. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Nueva Biblia de las Americas
entries.note: (NBLA) Updated Spanish translation by the Lockman Foundation, first published in 2005. Also known as Nueva Biblia Latinoamericana de Hoy (NBLH), Nueva Biblia de los Hispanos (NBH), and Nueva Biblia Latinoamericana (NBL). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Biblia de América
entries.note: A 1994 Spanish translation of the complete Catholic Bible by La Casa de la Biblia (representing the Spanish Episcopal Conference) and approved by the Episcopal Conferences of Mexico, Colombia and Chile. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Common English Bible
entries.note: (CEB) 2011 contemporary English translation of the Bible sponsored by the US-based Christian Resources Development Corporation. The translation includes Old Testament, Apocrypha and New Testament, and is aimed to be accessible to most English readers (minimum 7th grade reading age)

entries.heading: Conferenza Episcopale Italiana
entries.note: Italian Episcopal Conference 1971 translation suitable for Italian Catholic liturgy. (Includes minor 1974 revision)

entries.heading: Conferenza Episcopale Italiana 2008
entries.note: New translation of the C.E.I. first published in 2008 – the version most widely used by the Italian Catholic Church

entries.heading: Contemporary English
entries.note: (CEV) A translation completed in 1995 and sponsored by the American Bible Society under the leadership of Barclay Newman

entries.heading: Concordata
entries.note: 1968 Interfaith version promoted by the Italian Bible Society. Has a Catholic ‘imprimateur’, but its ecumenical approach has Jewish, Protestant and Christian Orthodox approval

entries.heading: Diodati
entries.note: Version based on original documents, edited by Giovanni Diodati in 1607, revised by Diodati in 1641 and again in 1894. It is the reference version for many Italian Protestants

entries.heading: Nuova Diodati
entries.note: (LND) Revision of the Diodati Bible dating to the 1990s, aiming at highest fidelity to original ancient Greek (New Testament) and Hebrew (Old Testament) texts

entries.heading: Douay–Rheims
entries.note: (DRB) An early (1580–1609) English translation from the Latin Vulgate designed for Catholics and performed by George Martin

entries.heading: Einheitsübersetzung
entries.note: A German translation of the Bible for use in Roman Catholic churches

entries.heading: English Standard
entries.note: (ESV) An update of the Revised Standard Version that makes ‘modest’ use of gender-free terminology

entries.heading: Biblia (1776)
entries.note: Finnish Bible translation

entries.heading: Raamattu (1933/1938)
entries.note: Finnish Bible translation

entries.heading: Raamattu kansalle
entries.note: Finnish Bible translation

entries.heading: Raamattu (1992)
entries.note: Finnish Bible translation

entries.heading: God’s Word
entries.note: (GW) A 1995 translation by the World Bible Publishing Company using the English language in a manner to communicate to the late 20th century American

entries.heading: Geneva
entries.note: (GEN) An early (1560) English version of the Bible translated by William Whittingham with strong Protestant leanings

entries.heading: Good News
entries.note: (GNB, GNT) A translation sponsored by the American Bible Society. The New Testament was first published (as ‘Today’s English Version’ TEV) in 1966. The Old Testament was completed in 1976, and the whole was published as the ‘Good News Bible’

entries.heading: Galbiati, Penna, Rossano – UTET
entries.note: Version edited by E. Galbiati, A. Penna and P. Rossano, and published by UTET. This version, based on original texts, is rich in notes and has been used as the basis for CEI translation

entries.heading: Original Greek
entries.note: (GNT) New Testament text in an original Greek version

entries.heading: Garofano, Rinaldi – Marietti
entries.note: Richly annotated 1963 version edited by S. Garofano and S. Rinaldi, and published by Marietti

entries.heading: Original Hebrew
entries.note: Old Testament text in an original Hebrew version

entries.heading: Christian Standard
entries.note: (HCSB, CSB) Published by Broadman and Holman as the Holman Christian Standard Bible (HCSB) in 2004, this translation rejects all forms of gender-neutral wording and is written with strong influences from the Southern Baptist perspective of biblical scholarship. The revised and updated version was first published in 2017 as the Christian Standard Bible (CSB)

entries.heading: International Children’s
entries.note: (ICB) A translation completed in 1986 targeting readability at the US third grade level

entries.heading: Traduzione Interconfessionale in Lingua Corrente
entries.note: (TILC) Interconfessional translation resulting from 1985 effort by Catholic and Protestant scholars, aimed at delivering an easy-to-understand message

entries.heading: Jerusalem
entries.note: (JB) A translation designed for English speaking Catholics based on the original languages. It is based on French as well as ancient texts and was first published in 1966. See also code NJR, NJB

entries.heading: King James
entries.note: (KJV) A translation commissioned by King James I of England and first published in 1611, with revisions in 1769

entries.heading: 21st Century King James
entries.note: (KJ21) A verbal translation led by William Prindele. Published in 1994, it was designed to modernize the language of the King James Version based on Webster’s New International Dictionary, 2nd edition, unabridged

entries.heading: King James Clássica
entries.note: (KJC) 2024 Portuguese translation of the KJV by Editoria Hagnos, preserving the style of the KJV. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Living Bible
entries.note: (TLB) A paraphrase translation led by Kenneth N Taylor and first published in 1972

entries.heading: Luzzi
entries.note: 1924 translation by Giovanni Luzzi, Professor at the Waldensian Faculty of Theology in Rome, who revised the 17th Century Diodati version

entries.heading: Message Bible
entries.note: (MSG) A paraphrase translation of the New Testament by Eugene Peterson first published in 1993. Old Testament added by 2002

entries.heading: New American
entries.note: (NAB) A translation aimed at Catholic readers first published in its entirety in 1970. A revised New Testament was issued in 1986 as the 2nd Edition. The 3rd Edtion was published in 1991 with a revision to Psalms. The 4th Edition (also known as the New American Bible Revised Edition) was published in 2011, incorporating revisions to the Old Testament (prefer code NAR for 4th Edition)

entries.heading: New American Revised
entries.note: (NABRE) 2011 update (4th Edition) of the New American Bible, with revisions to the Old Testament. Approved by the US Conference of Bishops. Use code NAB for earlier editions. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: New American Standard
entries.note: (NASB) A translation commissioned by the Lockman Foundation. The New Testament was published in 1960 followed by the entire Bible in 1971. Use code NAU for later revisions

entries.heading: New American Standard, Updated
entries.note: (NASB-U) A 1995 translation using more modern language than the NASB, with revision in 2020

entries.heading: CTS New Catholic Bible
entries.note: (CTS, NCB) 2007 revision of the 1966 Jerusalem Bible, with new textual and liturgical notes and changes to the Psalms, published by the Catholic Truth Society. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: St. Joseph New Catholic Bible
entries.note: (St Joseph NCB). A 2019 translation by the Catholic Book Publishing Company (CBP), marketed as Saint Joseph Editions. The New Testament (2015) and Psalms (2002) originally published under the name New Catholic Version. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Bibelen 1895
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen 1930
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen 1938
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen 1978-85
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen 1978
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen 1985
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Norsk Bibel 88
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen 1978-85 / rev. 2005
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen 2011
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: Norsk Bibel 88 / rev. 2007
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Fauskanger 2015
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation with commentary. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Bibelen 2011 / rev. 2024
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation, 2024 update of Bibelen 2011. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Pollestad 2023
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: New Century
entries.note: (NCV) A translation inspired by the International Children’s version. First published by World Publishing in 1991

entries.heading: New English
entries.note: (NEB) A translation first issued in 1961 (New Testament) and 1970 (complete Bible) as a result of a proposal at the 1946 General Assembly of the Church of Scotland

entries.heading: Bibelen Guds ord
entries.note: Norwegian Bible translation

entries.heading: New International
entries.note: (NIV) A translation underwritten by Biblica (formerly the International Bible Society, and previously the New York Bible Society). The New Testament was published in 1973 followed by the entire Bible in 1978. The NIV text was revised in 1984 and again in 2011

entries.heading: New International Reader’s
entries.note: (NIrV) A 1996 translation designed for people with limited literacy in English and based on the NIV

entries.heading: New Jerusalem
entries.note: (NJB) A revision of the Jerusalem Bible. First published in 1986. See also code NJR

entries.heading: New Jerusalem Revised
entries.note: (RNJB) 2019 successor to Jerusalem and New Jerusalem Bibles. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: New King James
entries.note: (NKJV) A version issued by Thomas Nelson Publishers in 1982–83 designed to update the language of the King James Version while maintaining the phrasing and rhythm and using the same sources as its predecessor

entries.heading: Bibelen, nynorsk
entries.note: Norwegian ‘nynorsk’ Bible translation

entries.heading: New Living
entries.note: (NLT) A translation sponsored by Tyndale House and first released in 1996. It is considered a revision and updating of the Living Bible

entries.heading: New Revised Standard
entries.note: (NRSV) A revision of the Revised Standard based on ancient texts but updating language to American usage of the 1980s

entries.heading: Nueva Traducción Viviente
entries.note: (NTV) A 2010 Spanish translation from the original Greek and Hebrew, sponsored by Tyndale House

entries.heading: Novissima Versione della Bibbia
entries.note: Nuovissima version – a Catholic-oriented translation in modern Italian, edited by a group including Carlo Martini, Gianfranco Ravasi and Ugo Vanni and first published (in 48 volumes, 1967–1980) by Edizioni San Paolo

entries.heading: Nueva Biblia al Dia
entries.note: (NBD) A 2008 Spanish translation from the original Greek and Hebrew, sponsored by the International Bible Society / Sociedad Bíblica Internacional

entries.heading: Nueva Version Internacional
entries.note: (NVI) A Spanish translation underwritten by the International Bible Society

entries.heading: New World Translation
entries.note: (NWT) An English translation published by the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: New Testament in Modern English (Phillips)
entries.note: (Phi) An idiomatic translation by J B Phillips, first completed in 1966

entries.heading: Revised English
entries.note: (REB) A 1989 revision of the NEB. A significant effort was made to reduce the British flavor present in the NEB

entries.heading: Revised Version
entries.note: (RV, ERV) The first major revision of the King James Version, the Revised Version incorporates insights from early manuscripts discovered between 1611 and 1870, and corrects readings in the KJV which nineteenth-century scholarship deemed mistaken. The New Testament was published in 1881, the Old Testament in 1885, and the Apocrypha in 1895

entries.heading: Revised Standard
entries.note: (RSV) A translation authorized by the National Council of Churches of Christ in the USA. The New Testament was published in 1946 followed by a complete Protestant canon in 1951

entries.heading: Revised Standard Catholic
entries.note: (RSV-CE, RSV-2CE) Version of the RSV Catholic canon published 1966, with slight updates in 2006. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Reina–Valera
entries.note: A Spanish translation based on the original texts

entries.heading: Bibel 2000
entries.note: Swedish Bible translation

entries.heading: Bibelen, samisk
entries.note: Norwegian ‘samisk’ Bible translation

entries.heading: Today’s English
entries.note: (TEV) A translation of the New Testament sponsored by the American Bible Society and first published in 1966. It was incorporated into the ‘Good News Bible’ (GNB) in 1976

entries.heading: Today’s New International
entries.note: (TNIV) An updating of the New International Version. The New Testament was published in 2002, and the entire Bible in 2005. Superseded by the 2011 NIV update

entries.heading: Nova Vulgata
entries.note: (NV) Neo-Vulgate or Nova Vulgata Bibliorum Sacrorum Editio, official Latin translation of the Catholic canon, published 1979 with a revised 2nd edition in 1986. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Easy to read version
entries.note: (ERV, EVD) Version in contemporary language, originally published as the Bible for the Deaf by Bible League International to facilitate access to the Biblical text. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Biblia de Jerusalén Latinoamericana
entries.note: 2000 Aprobado por el Consejo Episcopal Latinoamericano y Caribeño (CELAM). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Bíblia do Peregrino
entries.note: (PER) Esta 1999 edición busca reproducir el estilo poético en que fue escrita la Biblia, utilizando la traducción idiomática. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: João Ferreira de Almeida (Primeira Versão)
entries.note: (JFA1) Primeira versão tradução 1753, publicada originalmente em 2 volumes. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: João Ferreira de Almeida (Segunda Versão)
entries.note: (JFA2) Revisão de 1819 publicada originalmente em um único volume. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Emendada
entries.note: (ARE) Revista em 1840 por E. Whitely. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Reformada
entries.note: (ARR) Revisada em 1847 pela Sociedade Bíblica Trinitariana. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Correcta
entries.note: (ARC1) Revisão de 1875 coordenada pelo português João Nunes Chaves

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Corrigida 1898
entries.note: (ARC2) Revisão de 1898 feita em Lisboa, Portugal

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Corrigida na Grafia Simplificada
entries.note: (ARC-SG) Revisão de 1944 da Imprensa Bíblica Brasileira com ajustes ortográficos para facilitar a leitura. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Corrigida 1949
entries.note: (ARC3) Revisão de 1949 pela Sociedade Bíblica do Brasil

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Atualizada
entries.note: (ARA1) Revisão e atualização de 1959 feita pela Sociedade Bíblica do Brasil a partir dos manuscritos originais

entries.heading: Almeida Revisada de Acordo com os Melhores Textos em Hebraico e Grego
entries.note: (AVR) Revisão de 1968 faita pela Imprensa Bíblica Brasileira a partir dos manuscritos originais. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Corrigida 1969
entries.note: (ARC4) Segunda revisão do texto de Almeida ARC3 de 1969 pela Sociedade Bíblica do Brasil

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Atualizada, Segunda Edição
entries.note: (ARA) Revisão de 1993 da primeira edição ARA1 que apresenta importantes mudanças estilísticas e exegéticas. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Revista e Corrigida, Nova Edição
entries.note: (ARC) Revisão de 1995 da primeira edição, feita pela Sociedade Bíblica do Brasil. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Edição Contemporânea
entries.note: (AEC) Revisão de 1999 feita pela Editora Vida, livre de arcaísmos e ambiguidades, preservando o estilo próprio da Almeida Revista e Corrigida. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Almeida Século 21
entries.note: (AS21) Versão de 2008 feita em parceria entre a Imprensa Bíblica Brasileira e a Edições Vida Nova, a qual incorporou avanços na Crítica Textual bíblica, possibilitando um avanço gramatical e ortográfico sobre a Almeida Revisada

entries.heading: Almeida Corrigida e Fiel 1994
entries.note: (ACF1) Revisão dos textos originais de Almeida, feita em 1994 pela Sociedade Bíblica Trinitariana

entries.heading: Almeida Corrigida e Fiel 2011
entries.note: (ACF) Última revisão feita em 2011 pela Sociedade Bíblica Trinitariana. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Nova Almeida Atualizada
entries.note: (NAA) Revisão mais aprofundada da Almeida Revista e Atualizada (ARA) feita em 2021 pela Sociedade Bíblica do Brasil. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Tradução Brasileira
entries.note: (TB) Versão elaborada por uma comissão de especialistas a partir dos originais. É a primeira tradução completa da Bíblia feita no Brasil. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Tradução na Linguagem de Hoje
entries.note: (TLH) Versão feita em 1988 diretamente dos originais, adequada para o nível educacional médio da população brasileira. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Nova Tradução na Linguagem de Hoje
entries.note: (NTLH) Revisão de 2000 da primeira edição da Tradução na Linguagem de Hoje, principalmente sobre o texto do Novo Testamento. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Nova Versão Internacional
entries.note: (NVI) Versão de 2001 feita pela Bíblica Brasil, a partir dos manuscritos mais aceitos, com equipe de profissionais brasileiros com base na NIV americana. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Nova Versão Transformadora
entries.note: Versão de 2016 da Tyndale Fundation feita por exegetas brasileiros a partir dos textos originais, tendo como base a New Living Translation norte-americana. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: King James Atualizada
entries.note: (KJA) Tradução em 2012 para o português brasileiro moderno da Sociedade Bíblica Ibero-Americana do Brasil e da Editora Abba Press da Bíblia King James (KJV)

entries.heading: Bíblia Sagrada Tradução Oficial da CNBB
entries.note: (BCNBB) A tradução oficial católica 2018 se baseia nos textos originais hebraicos, aramaicos e gregos, comparados com a Nova Vulgata. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Bíblia Mensagem de Deus
entries.note: (BMD) Tradução da Bíblia para português de 1983 diretamete dos originais hebraicos e gregos, feita pela Liga de Estudos Bíblicos. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Tradução Ecumênica da Bíblia
entries.note: (TEB) Tradução Ecumênica baseia-se nos textos originais e reproduz fielmente o modelo da mundialmente reconhecida Traduction Oecuménique de la Bible. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: A Bíblia Paulinas
entries.note: 2023 tradução dos textos sagrados feita diretamente das línguas originais (hebraico, aramaico e grego) para o português. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Bible de Maredsous (Bíblia Ave-Maria)
entries.note: (BAM) Translation from the Greek, Hebrew and Aramaic originals by the Benedictine Monks of Maredsous, best known in the 1959 Brazilian Portuguese translation by Missionários do Imaculado Coração de Maria. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Traduction Oecuménique de la Bible
entries.note: (TOB) Ecumenical translation of the Bible, a revision of the Jerusalem Bible by both Catholics and Protestants in 1975. Revised in 1988, 2004, and in 2010 with additional books from the Orthodox canon. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Other
entries.note: Other translations not otherwise noted

entries.heading: Cambridge Annotated
entries.note: Contains the work of Howard Clark Kee including a summary of the development of the canon, introductions to the books, notes and cross references. Originally published in 1993, NRSV

entries.heading: Life Application
entries.note: A project of Tyndale House Publishers and Zondervan intended to help readers apply the Bible to daily living. Living Bible, King James, New International, NASB

entries.heading: Macarthur
entries.note: A King James version study Bible with notes by James Macarthur first published in 1997

entries.heading: Oxford Annotated
entries.note: A study Bible originally published in the 1960s and based on the RSV / NRSV

entries.heading: Studiebibel, Det Nye testamentet
entries.note: Norwegian study Bible, New Testament

entries.heading: New Oxford Annotated
entries.note: Published in 1991 and based on the New Revised Standard version

entries.heading: Norsk studiebibel
entries.note: Norwegian study Bible

entries.heading: Ryrie
entries.note: Based on the work of Charles C. Ryrie. King James, NI, NASB

entries.heading: Scofield
entries.note: A study Bible based on the early 20th century work of C.I. Scofield. Based on the King James version

entries.heading: Spirit Filled
entries.note: A transdenominational study Bible for persons from the Pentecostal / Charismatic traditions

entries.heading: Award
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed for presentation from a religious organization

entries.heading: Baby
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed to be a gift to commemorate a child’s birth

entries.heading: Bride
entries.note: A special gift Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed for the bride on her wedding day. Usually white

entries.heading: Children’s
entries.note: A text Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed in presentation and readability for a child

entries.heading: Christening / Baptism gift
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) specifically intended as a gift or keepsake for a child’s Christening or baptism, often with personalization features like a presentation page, space to record milestones, and sometimes even illustrations or stories tailored for young children. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Compact
entries.note: A small Bible (or selected Biblical text) with a trim height of five inches or less

entries.heading: Confirmation
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed to be used in the confirmation reading or as a gift to a confirmand

entries.heading: Cross-reference
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) which includes text conveying cross-references to related scripture passages

entries.heading: Daily readings
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) laid out to provide readings for each day of the year

entries.heading: Devotional
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) containing devotional content together with the scripture

entries.heading: Family
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) containing family record pages and/or additional study material for family devotion

entries.heading: First communion
entries.note: A Bible or (selected Biblical text) specifically intended as a gift or keepsake for a communicant’s first communion. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: General / Text
entries.note: A standard Bible (or selected Biblical text) of any version with no distinguishing characteristics beyond the canonical text

entries.heading: Gift
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed for gift or presentation, often including a presentation page

entries.heading: Journaling / notetaking
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed with extra space in the margins or on dedicated pages for notes, personal reflections or creative expression. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Lectern / Pulpit
entries.note: A large Bible (or selected Biblical text) with large print designed for use in reading scriptures in public worship from either the pulpit or lectern. Usually in a fine binding and elaborately decorated

entries.heading: Men’s
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) especially designed with helps and study guides oriented to the adult male

entries.heading: Outreach
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed for distribution to those outside of the church, often at a lower cost or in a more accessible format. They are intended to be shared with people who may not already own a Bible, and frequently feature helpful resources like introductions to key concepts, guidance on common questions, and explanations of salvation for those exploring faith or new believers. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Pastoral
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) intended as a practical resource for pastors, offering guidance and tools for various aspects of ministry. It typically includes additional articles, sermon outlines, and special service templates, alongside standard Biblical text. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Pew
entries.note: Usually inexpensive but sturdy, a Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed for use in church pews

entries.heading: Preaching
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) specifically designed with features that are helpful for public speaking and delivering sermons, including a larger font size, wider margins for taking notes, and a layout that makes it easy to locate verses quickly. Smaller and less elaborately-decorated than a Pulpit Bible. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Primary school
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed for use in primary school

entries.heading: Reader’s
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) laid out as single-column text, with no footnotes or verse numbers, like a ‘normal’ book. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Scholarly
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) including texts in Greek and/or Hebrew and designed for scholarly study

entries.heading: Student
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) with study articles and helps especially for use in the classroom

entries.heading: Study
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) with many extra features, e.g. book introductions, dictionary, concordance, references, maps, etc, to help readers better understand the scripture

entries.heading: Wedding gift
entries.note: A special gift Bible (or selected Biblical text) designed as a gift to the couple on their wedding day

entries.heading: Women’s
entries.note: A devotional or study Bible (or selected Biblical text) with helps targeted at the adult woman

entries.heading: Youth / Teen
entries.note: A Bible (or selected Biblical text) containing special study and devotional helps designed specifically for the needs of teenagers or young adults

entries.heading: Chronological
entries.note: A Bible with the text organized in the order in which events are believed to have happened

entries.heading: Chain reference
entries.note: A Bible which explores keywords or themes by referring text to preceding or following text

entries.heading: Interlinear
entries.note: A Bible or other text in which different versions are printed one line above the other, so that the variations can easily be detected

entries.heading: Parallel
entries.note: A Bible with two or more versions printed side by side

entries.heading: Standard
entries.note: A Bible in which the text is presented in the traditional order

entries.heading: Center column
entries.note: References are printed in a narrow column in the center of the page between two columns of text

entries.heading: Page end
entries.note: References are printed at the foot of the page

entries.heading: Side column
entries.note: References are printed in a column to the side of the scripture

entries.heading: Verse end
entries.note: References are printed at the end of the applicable verse

entries.heading: Unknown
entries.note: The person creating the ONIX record does not know where the references are located

entries.heading: Other
entries.note: Other locations not otherwise identified

entries.heading: VAT Identity Number
entries.note: Identifier for a business organization for VAT purposes, eg within the EU’s VIES system. See http://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/faqvies.do for EU VAT ID formats, which vary from country to country. Generally these consist of a two-letter country code followed by the 8–12 digits of the national VAT ID. Some countries include one or two letters within their VAT ID. See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VAT_identification_number for non-EU countries that maintain similar identifiers. Spaces, dashes etc should be omitted

entries.heading: EORI

entries.heading: Chinese participant identifier

entries.heading: Proprietary discount code scheme
entries.note: A publisher’s or supplier’s own code which identifies a trade discount category. Note that a distinctive <DiscountCodeTypeName> is required with proprietary coding schemes. The actual discount for each code is set by trading partner agreement (applies to goods supplied on standard trade discounting terms)

entries.heading: Boeksoort

entries.heading: German terms code

entries.heading: Proprietary commission code scheme
entries.note: A publisher’s or supplier’s own code which identifies a commission rate category. Note that a distinctive <DiscountCodeTypeName> is required with proprietary coding schemes. The actual commission rate for each code is set by trading partner agreement (applies to goods supplied on agency terms)

entries.heading: BIC commission group code
entries.note: UK publisher’s or distributor’s commission group code in format specified by BIC to ensure uniqueness. Format is identical to BIC discount group code, but indicates a commission rather than a discount (applies to goods supplied on agency terms)

entries.heading: ISNI-based discount group code
entries.note: ISNI-based discount group scheme devised initially by the German IG ProduktMetadaten, in a format comprised of the supplier’s 16-digit ISNI, followed by a hyphen and one to three alphanumeric characters – normally digits – chosen by the supplier. These characters are the index to a discount percentage in a table shared in advance by the supplier with individual customers. In this way, a supplier may maintain individual product-specific discount arrangements with each customer. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

heading: US CPSIA or other international hazard warning type

entries.heading: No known hazards or warnings
entries.note: Product assessed but no known hazards or warnings applicable. May be applied to both digital and physical products. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WARNING: CHOKING HAZARD – Small parts | Not for children under 3 yrs.
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US

entries.heading: WARNING: CHOKING HAZARD – Children under 8 yrs. can choke or suffocate on uninflated or broken balloons. Adult supervision required | Keep uninflated balloons from children. Discard broken balloons at once.
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US

entries.heading: WARNING: CHOKING HAZARD – This toy is a small ball | Not for children under 3 yrs.
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US

entries.heading: WARNING: CHOKING HAZARD – Toy contains a small ball | Not for children under 3 yrs.
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US

entries.heading: WARNING: CHOKING HAZARD – This toy is a marble | Not for children under 3 yrs.
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US

entries.heading: WARNING: CHOKING HAZARD – Toy contains a marble | Not for children under 3 yrs.
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US

entries.heading: No choking hazard warning necessary
entries.note: To be used when a supplier wishes to make a clear statement that no such warning is applicable to product

entries.heading: WARNING: STRANGULATION HAZARD – Long cord | Not for children under 3 yrs.
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: No strangulation hazard warning necessary
entries.note: To be used when a supplier wishes to make a clear statement that no such warning is applicable to product, Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: US CPSC Certificate of Conformity available
entries.note: A General Certificate of Conformity (GCC), or for children’s products, a Children’s Product Certificate (CPC), required to certify the product complies with applicable safety rules enforced by the US Consumer Products Safety Commission. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> must carry the URL of the GCC or CPC document

entries.heading: WARNING: MAGNET HAZARD – Product contains (a) small magnet(s)
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in the US. Should be accompanied by additional text: Swallowed magnets can stick together across intestines causing serious infections and death. Seek immediate medical attention if magnet(s) are swallowed or inhaled

entries.heading: No magnet hazard warning necessary
entries.note: To be used when a supplier wishes to make a clear statement that no such warning is applicable to product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WARNING – Flashing hazard
entries.note: Product flashes, flickers or includes high-contrast static or moving patterns which may cause discomfort or seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: No flashing hazard warning necessary
entries.note: To be used when a supplier wishes to make a clear statement that no such warning is applicable to product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WARNING – Sound hazard
entries.note: Product makes loud, sudden, repetitive or other sounds which may trigger seizures in sensitive people. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: No sound hazard warning necessary
entries.note: To be used when a supplier wishes to make a clear statement that no such warning is applicable to product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WARNING – Motion simulation hazard
entries.note: Products simulates (via visual effects) the experience of motion, which may cause nausea in sensitive people. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: No motion simulation hazard warning necessary
entries.note: To be used when a supplier wishes to make a clear statement that no such warning is applicable to product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WARNING – California Proposition 65 carcinogenic, teratogenic or other reproductively harmful chemical hazard
entries.note: Required on applicable products sold in California. Must be accompanied in <ProductFormFeatureDescription> by specific additional text as displayed on product or packaging. For example, “WARNING: This product can expose you to chemicals including [chemical name], which is known to the State of California to cause cancer. For more information, go to www.P65Warnings.ca.gov”. Note long-form warnings should be used here, even if a short form warning is used on the product or packaging. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: No California Proposition 65 hazard warning necessary
entries.note: To be used when a supplier wishes to make a clear statement that no such warning is applicable to product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: California Proposition 65 chemical name
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescripton> carries the name of chemical that is the subject of a warning, taken from the list at www.p65warnings.ca.gov/chemicals Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later
