entries.heading: Flashing risk unknown
entries.note: Flashing present but risk unknown or unassessed. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Sound risk unknown
entries.note: Sound present but risk unknown or unassessed. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Motion simulation risk unknown
entries.note: Motion simulation present but risk unknown or unassessed. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: None
entries.note: Has no technical protection

entries.heading: DRM
entries.note: Has DRM protection

entries.heading: Digital watermarking
entries.note: Has digital watermarking

entries.heading: Adobe DRM
entries.note: Has DRM protection applied by the Adobe CS4 Content Server Package or by the Adobe ADEPT hosted service

entries.heading: Apple DRM
entries.note: Has FairPlay DRM protection applied via Apple proprietary online store

entries.heading: OMA DRM
entries.note: Has OMA v2 DRM protection applied, as used to protect some mobile phone content

entries.heading: Readium LCP DRM
entries.note: Has Licensed Content Protection DRM applied by a Readium License Server. See https://readium.org/lcp-specs/

entries.heading: Sony DRM
entries.note: Has Sony DADC User Rights Management (URMS) DRM protection applied

entries.heading: No constraints
entries.note: Allows positive indication that there are no particular constraints (that can be specified in <EpubUsageConstraint>). By convention, use 01 in <EpubUsageStatus>

entries.heading: Preview
entries.note: Preview before purchase. Allows a retail customer, account holder or patron to view or listen to a proportion of the book before purchase. Also applies to borrowers making use of ‘acquisition on demand’ models in libraries, and to ‘subscription’ models where the purchase is made on behalf of the reader. Note that any Sales embargo date (in <PublishingDate> or <MarketDate>) also applies to provision of previews, unless an explicit date is provided for the preview

entries.heading: Print
entries.note: Make physical copy of extract

entries.heading: Copy / paste
entries.note: Make digital copy of extract

entries.heading: Share
entries.note: Share product across multiple concurrent devices. Allows a retail customer, account holder or patron to read the book across multiple devices linked to the same account. Also applies to readers in library borrowing and ‘subscription’ models

entries.heading: Text to speech
entries.note: ‘Read aloud’ with text to speech functionality

entries.heading: Lend
entries.note: Lendable by the purchaser to another device owner or account holder or patron, eg ‘Lend-to-a-friend’, or library lending (where the library product has a separate <ProductIdentifier> from the consumer product – but for this prefer code 16). The ‘primary’ copy becomes unusable while the secondary copy is ‘lent’ unless a number of concurrent borrowers is also specified

entries.heading: Time-limited license
entries.note: E-publication license is time-limited. Use with code 02 from List 146 and either a time period in days, weeks or months in <EpubUsageLimit>, or a Valid until date in <EpubUsageLimit>. The purchased copy becomes unusable when the license expires. For clarity, a perpetual license is the default, but may be specified explicitly with code 01 from list 146, or with code 02 and a limit <Quantity> of 0 days

entries.heading: Library loan renewal
entries.note: Maximum number of consecutive loans or loan extensions (usually from a library) to a single device owner or account holder or patron. Note that a limit of 1 indicates that a loan cannot be renewed or extended

entries.heading: Multi-user license
entries.note: E-publication license is multi-user. Maximum number of concurrent users licensed to use the product should be given in <EpubUsageLimit>. For clarity, unlimited concurrency is the default, but may be specified explicitly with code 01 from list 146, or with code 02 and a limit <Quantity> of 0 users

entries.heading: Preview on premises
entries.note: Preview locally before purchase. Allows a retail customer, account holder or patron to view a proportion of the book (or the whole book, if no proportion is specified) before purchase, but ONLY while located physically in the retailer’s store (eg while logged on to the store or library wifi). Also applies to patrons making use of ‘acquisition on demand’ models in libraries

entries.heading: Text and data mining
entries.note: Make use of the content of the product (text, images, audio etc) or the product metadata or supporting resources for extraction of useful (and possibly new) information through automated computer analysis, or for training of tools for such analysis (including training of generative AI models). By convention, use 01 or 03 in <EpubUsageStatus>. Note 03 should be regarded as ‘prohibited to the full extent allowed by law’, or otherwise expressly reserved by the rightsholder, as in some jurisdictions, TDM may be subject to copyright exception (eg for not-for-profit purposes), subject to optional reservation, or allowed under ‘fair use’ doctrine

entries.heading: TDM for AI to enhance the private purchase experience
entries.note: Where text and data mining is prohibited or otherwise expressly reserved by the rightsholder, make use of the content of the product (text, images, audio etc) or the product metadata or supporting resources to train or enable a generative AI-enhanced purchase experience for a customer, with no use outside of a private AI instance controlled by the reseller – for example to provide AI-assisted book selection

entries.heading: TDM for AI to enhance the private reading experience
entries.note: Where text and data mining is prohibited or otherwise expressly reserved by the rightsholder, make use of the content of the product (text, images, audio etc) or the product metadata or supporting resources to train or enable a generative AI-enhanced reading experience for the purchaser, with no use outside of a private AI instance controlled by the reseller or embedded in the product itself – for example to provide AI-enhanced reading

entries.heading: Library loan
entries.note: Loanable by the purchaser (usually a library) to other device owner or account holder or patron, eg library lending (whether or not the library product has a separate <ProductIdentifier> from the consumer product). The ‘primary’ copy becomes unusable while the secondary copy is ‘on loan’ unless a number of concurrent borrowers is also specified. Use code 08 to specify any limit on loan renewals

entries.heading: Permitted subject to limit
entries.note: Limit should be specified in <EpubUsageLimit> or <PriceConstraintLimit>

entries.heading: Copies
entries.note: Maximum number of copies that may be made of a permitted extract

entries.heading: Characters
entries.note: Maximum number of characters in a permitted extract for a specified usage

entries.heading: Words
entries.note: Maximum number of words in a permitted extract for a specified usage

entries.heading: Pages
entries.note: Maximum number of pages in a permitted extract for a specified usage

entries.heading: Percentage
entries.note: Maximum percentage of total content in a permitted extract for a specified usage

entries.heading: Devices
entries.note: Maximum number of devices in ‘share group’

entries.heading: Concurrent users
entries.note: Maximum number of concurrent users. NB where the number of concurrent users is specifically not limited, set the number of concurrent users to zero

entries.heading: Users
entries.note: Maximum number of licensed individual users, independent of concurrency of use

entries.heading: Concurrent classes
entries.note: Maximum number of licensed concurrent classes of user. A ‘class’ is a group of learners attending a specific course or lesson and generally taught as a group

entries.heading: Classes
entries.note: Maximum number of licensed classes of learners, independent of concurrency of use and the number of users per class

entries.heading: Institutions
entries.note: Maximum number of licensed institutions, independent of concurrency of use and the number of classes or individuals per institution

entries.heading: Percentage per time period
entries.note: Maximum percentage of total content which may be used in a specified usage per time period; the time period being specified as another <EpubUsageLimit> Quantity

entries.heading: Days
entries.note: Maximum time period in days (beginning from product purchase or activation)

entries.heading: Weeks
entries.note: Maximum time period in weeks

entries.heading: Months
entries.note: Maximum time period in months

entries.heading: Hours minutes and seconds
entries.note: Maximum amount of time in hours, minutes and seconds allowed in a permitted extract for a specified usage, in the format HHHMMSS (7 digits, with leading zeros if necessary)

entries.heading: Days (fixed start)
entries.note: Maximum time period in days (beginning from the product publication date). In effect, this defines a fixed end date for the license independent of the purchase or activation date

entries.heading: Weeks (fixed start)
entries.note: Maximum time period in weeks

entries.heading: Months (fixed start)
entries.note: Maximum time period in months

entries.heading: Times
entries.note: Maximum number of times a specified usage event may occur (in the lifetime of the product)

entries.heading: Times per day
entries.note: Maximum frequency a specified usage event may occur (per day)

entries.heading: Times per month
entries.note: Maximum frequency a specified usage event may occur (per month)

entries.heading: Times per year
entries.note: Maximum frequency a specified usage event may occur (per year)

entries.heading: Dots per inch
entries.note: Maximum resolution of printed or copy / pasted extracts

entries.heading: Dots per cm
entries.note: Maximum resolution of printed or copy / pasted extracts

entries.heading: Allowed usage start page
entries.note: Page number where allowed usage begins. <Quantity> should contain an absolute page number, counting the cover as page 1. (This type of page numbering should not be used where the e-publication has no fixed pagination). Use with (max number of) Pages, Percentage of content, or End page to specify pages allowed in Preview

entries.heading: Allowed usage end page
entries.note: Page number at which allowed usage ends. <Quantity> should contain an absolute page number, counting the cover as page 1. (This type of page numbering should not be used where the e-publication has no fixed pagination). Use with Start page to specify pages allowed in a preview

entries.heading: Allowed usage start time
entries.note: Time at which allowed usage begins. <Quantity> should contain an absolute time, counting from the beginning of an audio or video product, in the format HHHMMSS or HHHMMSScc. Use with Time, Percentage of content, or End time to specify time-based extract allowed in Preview

entries.heading: Allowed usage end time
entries.note: Time at which allowed usage ends. <Quantity> should contain an absolute time, counting from the beginning of an audio or video product, in the format HHHMMSS or HHHMMSScc. Use with Start time to specify time-based extract allowed in Preview

entries.heading: Valid from
entries.note: The date from which the usage constraint applies. <Quantity> is in the format YYYYMMDD

entries.heading: Valid to
entries.note: The date until which the usage constraint applies. <Quantity> is in the format YYYYMMDD

entries.heading: Unspecified (default)
entries.note: Collection type is not determined

entries.heading: Publisher collection
entries.note: The collection is a bibliographic collection (eg a series or set (Fr. série)) defined and identified by a publisher, either on the product itself or in product information supplied by the publisher. The books in the collection generally share a subject, narrative, design style or authorship. They may have a specific order, or the collection may be unordered

entries.heading: Collection éditoriale
entries.note: The collection is a bibliographic collection defined and identified by a publisher, either on the product itself or in product information supplied by the publisher, where the books in the collection have no specific order (other than order of publication), shared subject, narrative, style or shared authorship, and are grouped by the publisher largely for marketing purposes. The collection has many of the characteristics of an imprint or marque. Used primarily in French book publishing, to distinguish between ‘série’ (using the normal code 10) and ‘collection’ (code 11), and where the collection éditoriale is not an imprint

entries.heading: Ascribed collection
entries.note: The collection has been defined and identified by a party in the metadata supply chain other than the publisher, typically an aggregator

entries.heading: Product
entries.note: The title element refers to an individual product

entries.heading: Collection level
entries.note: The title element refers to the top level of a bibliographic collection

entries.heading: Subcollection
entries.note: The title element refers to an intermediate level of a bibliographic collection that comprises two or more ‘sub-collections’

entries.heading: Content item
entries.note: The title element refers to a content item within a product, eg a work included in a combined or ‘omnibus’ edition, or a chapter in a book. Generally used only for titles within <ContentItem> (Block 3)

entries.heading: Master brand
entries.note: The title element names a multimedia franchise, licensed property or master brand where the use of the brand spans multiple collections and product forms, and possibly multiple imprints and publishers. It need not have a hierarchical relationship with title elements at other levels, or with other master brands. Used only for branded media properties carrying, for example, a children’s character brand or film franchise branding

entries.heading: Sub-subcollection
entries.note: The title element refers to an intermediate level of a bibliographic collection that is a subdivision of a sub-collection (a third level of collective identity)

entries.heading: Universe
entries.note: The title element names a ‘universe’, where parallel or intersecting narratives spanning multiple works and multiple characters occur in the same consistent fictional setting. It need not have a hierarchical relationship with title elements at other levels, in particular with master brands. Used primarily for comic books, but applicable to other fiction where appropriate

entries.heading: Audio
entries.note: Audio recording – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer AZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other A* code applies

entries.heading: Audio cassette
entries.note: Audio cassette (analogue)

entries.heading: CD-Audio
entries.note: Audio compact disc: use for ‘Red book’ discs (conventional audio CD) and SACD, and use coding in <ProductFormDetail> to specify the format, if required

entries.heading: DAT
entries.note: Digital audio tape cassette

entries.heading: Audio disc
entries.note: Audio disc (excluding CD-Audio): use for ‘Yellow book’ (CD-Rom-style) discs, including for example mp3 CDs, and use coding in <ProductFormDetail> to specify the format of the data on the disc

entries.heading: Audio tape
entries.note: Audio tape (analogue open reel tape)

entries.heading: MiniDisc
entries.note: Sony MiniDisc format

entries.heading: CD-Extra
entries.note: Audio compact disc with part CD-ROM content, also termed CD-Plus or Enhanced-CD: use for ‘Blue book’ and ‘Yellow / Red book’ two-session discs

entries.heading: Downloadable audio file
entries.note: Digital audio recording downloadable to the purchaser’s own device(s)

entries.heading: Pre-recorded digital audio player
entries.note: For example, Playaway audiobook and player: use coding in <ProductFormDetail> to specify the recording format, if required

entries.heading: Pre-recorded SD card
entries.note: For example, Audiofy audiobook chip

entries.heading: LP
entries.note: ‘Long player’. Vinyl disc (analogue), typically 12 inches diameter and played at 33⅓rpm

entries.heading: Downloadable and online / streamed audio file
entries.note: Digital audio recording available both by download to the purchaser’s own device(s) and by online (eg streamed) access

entries.heading: Online / streamed audio file
entries.note: Digital audio recording available online (eg streamed), not downloadable to the purchaser’s own device(s)

entries.heading: Other audio format
entries.note: Other audio format not specified by AB to AO. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Book
entries.note: Book – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer BZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other B* code applies

entries.heading: Hardback
entries.note: Hardback or cased book

entries.heading: Paperback / softback
entries.note: Paperback or other softback book

entries.heading: Loose-leaf
entries.note: Loose-leaf book

entries.heading: Spiral bound
entries.note: Spiral, comb or coil bound book

entries.heading: Pamphlet
entries.note: Pamphlet, stapled (de: ‘geheftet’). Includes low-extent wire-stitched books bound without a distinct spine (eg many comic book ‘floppies’)

entries.heading: Leather / fine binding
entries.note: Use <ProductFormDetail> to provide additional description

entries.heading: Board book
entries.note: Child’s book with all pages printed on board

entries.heading: Rag book
entries.note: Child’s book with all pages printed on textile

entries.heading: Bath book
entries.note: Child’s book printed on waterproof material

entries.heading: Novelty book
entries.note: A book whose novelty consists wholly or partly in a format which cannot be described by any other available code – a ‘conventional’ format code is always to be preferred; one or more Product Form Detail codes, eg from the B2nn group, should be used whenever possible to provide additional description

entries.heading: Slide bound
entries.note: Slide bound book

entries.heading: Big book
entries.note: Extra-large format for teaching etc; this format and terminology may be specifically UK; required as a top-level differentiator

entries.heading: Part-work (fascículo)
entries.note: A part-work issued with its own ISBN and intended to be collected and bound into a complete book

entries.heading: Fold-out book or chart
entries.note: Concertina-folded booklet or chart, designed to fold to pocket or regular page size, and usually bound within distinct board or card covers (de: Leporello)

entries.heading: Foam book
entries.note: A children’s book whose cover and pages are made of foam

entries.heading: Other book format
entries.note: Other book format or binding not specified by BB to BP. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Sheet map
entries.note: Sheet map – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer CZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other C* code applies

entries.heading: Sheet map, rolled
entries.note: See <ProductPackaging> and Codelist 80 for ‘rolled in tube’

entries.heading: Globe
entries.note: Globe or planisphere

entries.heading: Other cartographic
entries.note: Other cartographic format not specified by CB to CE. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Digital (on physical carrier)
entries.note: Digital content delivered on a physical carrier (detail unspecified). Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer DZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other D* code applies

entries.heading: CD-I
entries.note: CD interactive: use for ‘Green book’ discs

entries.heading: Diskette
entries.note: AKA ‘floppy disc’

entries.heading: Double-sided CD / DVD
entries.note: Double-sided disc, one side Audio CD / CD-ROM, other side DVD

entries.heading: BR-ROM
entries.note: (Blu Ray ROM)

entries.heading: Other digital carrier
entries.note: Other carrier of digital content not specified by DB to DO. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Digital (delivered electronically)
entries.note: Digital content delivered electronically (delivery method unspecified). Use only when the form and delivery method is unknown, or when no other E* code applies and the delivery method is described in <ProductFormDescription>. Note, use <ProductFormDetail> to specify file format

entries.heading: Digital download and online / streamed
entries.note: Digital content available both by download and by online access

entries.heading: Digital online / streamed
entries.note: Digital content accessed online only (eg streamed), not downloadable to the purchaser’s own device(s)

entries.heading: Digital download
entries.note: Digital content delivered by download only

entries.heading: Film or transparency
entries.note: Film or transparency – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer FZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other F* code applies

entries.heading: Slides
entries.note: Photographic transparencies mounted for projection

entries.heading: OHP transparencies
entries.note: Transparencies for overhead projector

entries.heading: Filmstrip
entries.note: Photographic transparencies, unmounted but cut into short multi-frame strips

entries.heading: Film
entries.note: Continuous movie film as opposed to filmstrip

entries.heading: Other film or transparency format
entries.note: Other film or transparency format not specified by FB to FF. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Digital product license
entries.note: Digital product license (delivery method unspecified). Use only when the form is unknown, or when no other L* code applies and the delivery method is described in <ProductFormDescription>

entries.heading: Digital product license key
entries.note: Digital product license delivered through the retail supply chain as a physical ‘key’, typically a card or booklet containing a code enabling the purchaser to download the associated product

entries.heading: Digital product license code
entries.note: Digital product license delivered by email or other electronic distribution, typically providing a code enabling the purchaser to activate, upgrade or extend the license supplied with the associated product

entries.heading: Microform
entries.note: Microform – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer MZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other M* code applies

entries.heading: Microfilm
entries.note: Roll microfilm

entries.heading: Other microform
entries.note: Other microform not specified by MB or MC. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Miscellaneous print
entries.note: Miscellaneous printed material – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer PZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other P* code applies

entries.heading: Address book
entries.note: May use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

entries.heading: Cards
entries.note: Cards, flash cards (eg for teaching reading), revision cards, divination, playing or trading cards

entries.heading: Copymasters
entries.note: Copymasters, photocopiable sheets

entries.heading: Diary or journal
entries.note: May use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

entries.heading: Frieze
entries.note: Narrow strip-shaped printed sheet used mostly for education or children’s products (eg depicting alphabet, number line, procession of illustrated characters etc). Usually intended for horizontal display

entries.heading: Kit
entries.note: Parts for post-purchase assembly, including card, wood or plastic parts or model components, interlocking construction blocks, beads and other crafting materials etc

entries.heading: Sheet music
entries.note: May use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

entries.heading: Postcard book or pack
entries.note: Including greeting cards and packs. For bound books (usually with perforated sheets to remove cards), may use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

entries.heading: Poster
entries.note: Poster for retail sale – see also XF

entries.heading: Record book
entries.note: Record book (eg ‘birthday book’, ‘baby book’): binding unspecified; may use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

entries.heading: Wallet or folder
entries.note: Wallet, folder or box (containing loose sheets etc, or empty): it is preferable to code the contents and treat ‘wallet’ (or folder / box) as packaging in <ProductPackaging> with Codelist 80, but if this is not possible (eg where the product is empty and intended for storing other loose items) the product as a whole may be coded as a ‘wallet’. For binders intended for loose leaf or partwork publications intended to be updateable, see codes BD, BN

entries.heading: Plate (lámina)
entries.note: A book-sized (as opposed to poster-sized) sheet, usually in color or high quality print

entries.heading: Notebook / blank book
entries.note: A book with all pages blank for the buyer’s own use; may use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

entries.heading: Organizer
entries.note: May use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

entries.heading: Leaflet
entries.note: Folded but unbound

entries.heading: Book plates
entries.note: Ex libris’ book labels and packs

entries.heading: Other printed item
entries.note: Other printed item not specified by PB to PQ. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product
entries.note: Presentation unspecified: format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>. Use only when the packaging of the product is unknown, or when no other S* code applies and the presentation is described in <ProductFormDescription>

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product, boxed
entries.note: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product, slip-cased
entries.note: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product, shrink-wrapped
entries.note: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>. Use code XL for a shrink-wrapped pack for trade supply, where the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product, loose
entries.note: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product, part(s) enclosed
entries.note: Multiple component product where subsidiary product part(s) is / are supplied as enclosures to the primary part, eg a book with a CD packaged in a sleeve glued within the back cover. Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product, entirely digital
entries.note: Multiple component product where all parts are digital, and delivered as separate files, eg a group of individual EPUB files, an EPUB with a PDF, an e-book with a license to access a range of online resources, etc. Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Multiple-component retail product, partly digital
entries.note: Multiple component product where some parts are digital, but at least one is physical, eg a physical book with a digital version also included, or an educational product containing a mix of physical and digital material. Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Video
entries.note: Video – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer VZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other V* code applies

entries.heading: Videodisc
entries.note: eg Laserdisc

entries.heading: DVD video
entries.note: DVD video: specify TV standard in <ProductFormDetail>

entries.heading: VHS video
entries.note: VHS videotape: specify TV standard in <ProductFormDetail>

entries.heading: Betamax video
entries.note: Betamax videotape: specify TV standard in <ProductFormDetail>

entries.heading: VCD
entries.note: VideoCD

entries.heading: SVCD
entries.note: Super VideoCD

entries.heading: HD DVD
entries.note: High definition DVD disc, Toshiba HD DVD format

entries.heading: Blu-ray
entries.note: High definition DVD disc, Sony Blu-ray format

entries.heading: UMD Video
entries.note: Sony Universal Media disc

entries.heading: CBHD
entries.note: China Blue High-Definition, derivative of HD-DVD

entries.heading: Other video format
entries.note: Other video format not specified by VB to VQ. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Trade-only material
entries.note: Trade-only material (unspecified). Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer XZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other X* code applies

entries.heading: Dumpbin – filled
entries.note: Dumpbin with contents. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Counterpack – filled
entries.note: Counterpack with contents. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Poster, promotional
entries.note: Promotional poster for display, not for sale – see also PK

entries.heading: Window piece
entries.note: Promotional piece for shop window display

entries.heading: Large book display
entries.note: Large scale facsimile of book for promotional display

entries.heading: Shrink-wrapped pack
entries.note: A quantity pack with its own product code, usually for trade supply only: the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>. For products or product bundles supplied individually shrink-wrapped for retail sale, use code SD

entries.heading: Boxed pack
entries.note: A quantity pack with its own product code, usually for trade supply only: the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>. For products or product bundles boxed individually for retail sale, use code SB

entries.heading: Pack (outer packaging unspecified)
entries.note: A quantity pack with its own product code, usually for trade supply only: the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>. Use only when the pack is neither shrinp-wrapped nor boxed

entries.heading: Spinner – filled
entries.note: Spinner with contents. ISBN(s) (where applicable) and detail of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>

entries.heading: Other point of sale – including retail product
entries.note: Other point of sale material not specified by XB to XO, supplied with included product(s) for retail sale. The retail product(s) must be described in <ProductPart>. Further detail of the POS material is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Other point of sale
entries.note: Other point of sale material not specified by XB to XY, promotional or decorative. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: General merchandise
entries.note: General merchandise, book accessories and non-book products – unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer ZX, ZY or ZZ, plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other Z* code applies

entries.heading: Doll or figure
entries.note: Including action figures, figurines

entries.heading: Soft toy
entries.note: Soft or plush toy

entries.heading: Toy
entries.note: Including educational toys (where no other code is relevant)

entries.heading: Game
entries.note: Board game, or other game (except computer game: see DE and other D* codes)

entries.heading: E-book reader
entries.note: Dedicated e-book reading device, typically with mono screen

entries.heading: Tablet computer
entries.note: General purpose tablet computer, typically with color screen

entries.heading: Audiobook player
entries.note: Dedicated audiobook player device, typically including book-related features like bookmarking

entries.heading: Jigsaw
entries.note: Jigsaw or similar ‘shapes’ puzzle

entries.heading: Mug
entries.note: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in drinking mug, cup etc

entries.heading: Tote bag
entries.note: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in bag

entries.heading: Tableware
entries.note: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in plates, bowls etc (note for mugs and cups, use code ZK)

entries.heading: Umbrella
entries.note: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in umbrella

entries.heading: Paints, crayons, pencils
entries.note: Coloring set, including pens, chalks, etc

entries.heading: Handicraft kit
entries.note: Handicraft kit or set, eg sewing, crochet, weaving, basketry, beadwork, leather, wood or metalworking, pottery and glassworking, candlemaking etc

entries.heading: Other toy / game accessories
entries.note: Other toy, game and puzzle items not specified by ZB to ZQ, generally accessories to other products etc. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Other apparel
entries.note: Other apparel items not specified by ZB to ZQ, including branded, promotional or tie-in scarves, caps, aprons, dress-up costumes etc. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Other merchandise
entries.note: Other branded, promotional or tie-in merchandise not specified by ZB to ZY. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

entries.heading: Associated with
entries.note: To express unknown relationship types (for use when expressing legacy ONIX 2.1 data in ONIX 3.0)

entries.heading: Flourished in
entries.note: (‘Floruit’)

entries.heading: Citizen of
entries.note: Or nationality. For use with country codes only

entries.heading: Registered in
entries.note: The place of legal registration of an organization

entries.heading: Operating from
entries.note: The place an organization or part of an organization is based or operates from

entries.heading: Eligible for geographical marketing programs
entries.note: Contributor is eligible for national, regional or local marketing support. Use with country code, region code or country / region plus location, as appropriate

entries.heading: Indigenous to (Indigenous geographies or territorialities)
entries.note: Use to indicate that an Indigenous contributor has chosen to be publicly identified as an Indigenous person associated with a particular territory or geography. Used with <LocationName> (in addition to country or region) to indicate an Indigenous territoriality or geography

entries.heading: No
entries.note: Not illustrated

entries.heading: Yes
entries.note: Illustrated

entries.heading: Sender-defined text
entries.note: To be used only in circumstances where the parties to an exchange have agreed to include text which (a) is not for general distribution, and (b) cannot be coded elsewhere. If more than one type of text is sent, it must be identified by tagging within the text itself

entries.heading: Short description / annotation
entries.note: Of the product. Limited to a maximum of 350 characters. In ONIX 3.0, this is assumed to include markup characters. In ONIX 3.1 and later, this limit does not include markup

entries.heading: Description
entries.note: Of the product. Length unrestricted

entries.heading: Table of contents
entries.note: Used for a table of contents sent as a single text field, which may or may not carry structure expressed using XHTML

entries.heading: Primary cover copy
entries.note: Primary descriptive blurb usually taken from the back cover or jacket, or occasionally from the cover / jacket flaps. See also code 27

entries.heading: Review quote
entries.note: A quote taken from a review of the product or of the work in question where there is no need to take account of different editions

entries.heading: Review quote: previous edition
entries.note: A quote taken from a review of a previous edition of the work

entries.heading: Review quote: previous work
entries.note: A quote taken from a review of a previous work by the same author(s) or in the same series

entries.heading: Endorsement
entries.note: A quote usually provided by a celebrity or another author to promote a new book, not from a review

entries.heading: Promotional headline
entries.note: A promotional phrase which is intended to headline a description of the product

entries.heading: Feature
entries.note: Text describing a feature of a product to which the publisher wishes to draw attention for promotional purposes. Each separate feature should be described by a separate repeat, so that formatting can be applied at the discretion of the receiver of the ONIX record, or multiple features can be described using appropriate XHTML markup

entries.heading: Biographical note
entries.note: A note referring to all contributors to a product – NOT linked to a single contributor

entries.heading: Publisher’s notice
entries.note: A statement included by a publisher in fulfillment of contractual obligations, such as a disclaimer, sponsor statement, or legal notice of any sort. Note that the inclusion of such a notice cannot and does not imply that a user of the ONIX record is obliged to reproduce it

entries.heading: Excerpt
entries.note: A short excerpt from the main text of the work

entries.heading: Index
entries.note: Used for an index sent as a single text field, which may be structured using XHTML

entries.heading: Short description / annotation for collection
entries.note: (of which the product is a part.) Limited to a maximum of 350 characters

entries.heading: Description for collection
entries.note: (of which the product is a part.) Length unrestricted

entries.heading: New feature
entries.note: As code 11 but used for a new feature of this edition or version

entries.heading: Open access statement
entries.note: Short summary statement of open access status and any related conditions (eg ‘Open access – no commercial use’), primarily for marketing purposes. Should always be accompanied by a link to the complete license (see <EpubLicense> or code 99 in List 158)

entries.heading: Digital exclusivity statement
entries.note: Short summary statement that the product is available only in digital formats (eg ‘Digital exclusive’). If a non-digital version is planned, <ContentDate> should be used to specify the date when exclusivity will end (use content date role code 15). If a non-digital version is available, the statement should not be included

entries.heading: Official recommendation
entries.note: For example a recommendation or approval provided by a ministry of education or other official body. Use <Text> to provide details and ideally use <TextSourceCorporate> to name the approver

entries.heading: JBPA description
entries.note: Short description in format specified by Japanese Book Publishers Association

entries.heading: schema.org snippet
entries.note: JSON-LD snippet suitable for use within an HTML <script type="application/ld+json"> tag, containing structured metadata suitable for use with schema.org

entries.heading: Introduction
entries.note: Introduction, preface or the text of other preliminary material, sent as a single text field, which may be structured using XHTML

entries.heading: Secondary cover copy
entries.note: Secondary descriptive blurb taken from the cover / jacket flaps, or occasionally from the back cover or jacket, used only when there are two separate texts and the primary text is included using code 05

entries.heading: Full cast and credit list
entries.note: For use with dramatized audiobooks, filmed entertainment etc, for a cast list sent as a single text field, which may or may not carry structure expressed using XHTML

entries.heading: Bibliography
entries.note: Complete list of books by the author(s), supplied as a single text field, which may be structured using (X)HTML

entries.heading: Abstract
entries.note: Formal summary of content (normally used with academic and scholarly content only)

entries.heading: Rules or instructions
entries.note: Eg for a game or kit – as supplied with the product

entries.heading: List of contents
entries.note: Eg for a game, kit. Note: use code 04 for a Table of Contents of a book

entries.heading: Short description / annotation for imprint
entries.note: Length limited to a maximum of 350 characters

entries.heading: Description for imprint
entries.note: Length unrestricted

entries.heading: Short description / annotation for publisher
entries.note: Length limited to a maximum of 350 characters

entries.heading: Description for publisher
entries.note: Length unrestricted

entries.heading: Cover line
entries.note: (US) Reading line – line of usually explanatory copy on cover, somewhat like a subtitle but not on the title page and added by the publisher, eg ‘with 125 illustrated recipes’

entries.heading: Special cover statement
entries.note: Short summary description of special nature of cover or jacket, for use with special editions (use with Edition type SPE), or with variant covers, when there is also a ‘standard’ cover

entries.heading: List of bonus contents
entries.note: Short summary description of bonus content (when there is also a ‘standard’ set of contents). Bonus material may include a new or extra foreword, additional illustrations, previously-unpublished bonus chapters (for these use with Edition type ENL), or for teaser chapters, author interview etc (do not use ENL)

entries.heading: Unrestricted
entries.note: Any audience. Use when there is only a single version of the promotional text or other marketing collateral. Avoid when there are differentiated versions (eg for end customers, for educators, for children) available

entries.heading: Restricted
entries.note: Distribution by agreement between the parties to the ONIX exchange (this value is provided to cover applications where ONIX content includes material which is not for general distribution)

entries.heading: Booktrade
entries.note: Distributors, bookstores, publisher’s own staff etc

entries.heading: End customers
entries.note: Potential purchasers, typically adults, who may or may not also be the audience for the book itself, particularly in the case of children’s books or books for younger teens

entries.heading: Teachers
entries.note: Including other educators

entries.heading: Students
entries.note: Content aimed at learners who are specified in <Audience> (including any relevant <AudienceRange>)

entries.heading: Press
entries.note: Press or other (traditional) media

entries.heading: Shopping comparison service
entries.note: Where a specially formatted description is required for this audience

entries.heading: Search engine index
entries.note: Text not intended for display, but may be used (in addition to any less restricted text) for indexing and search

entries.heading: Social media
entries.note: (Including bloggers, vloggers, influencers etc) Where this is distinct from end customers or the Press

entries.heading: Children
entries.note: Content aimed at children who are specified in <Audience> (including any relevant <AudienceRange>)

entries.heading: Teens
entries.note: Content aimed at teens who are specified in <Audience> (including any relevant <AudienceRange>)

entries.heading: Publication date
entries.note: Nominal date of publication (of the content item or supporting resource)

entries.heading: Broadcast date
entries.note: Date when a TV or radio program was / will be broadcast

entries.heading: From date
entries.note: Date from which a content item or supporting resource may be referenced or used. The content is embargoed until this date

entries.heading: Until date
entries.note: Date until which a content item or supporting resource may be referenced or used

entries.heading: Last updated
entries.note: Date when a resource was last changed or updated

entries.heading: From… until date
entries.note: Combines From date and Until date to define a period (both dates are inclusive). Use for example with dateformat 06

entries.heading: Available from
entries.note: Date from which a supporting resource is available for download. Note that this date also implies that it can be immediately displayed to the intended audience, unless a From date (code 14) is also supplied and is later than the Available from date

entries.heading: Available until
entries.note: Date until which a supporting resource is available for download. Note that this date does not imply it must be removed from display to the intended audience on this date – for this, use Until date (code 15)

entries.heading: Associated start date
entries.note: Start date referenced by the supporting resource, for example, the ‘earliest exam date’ for an official recommendation

entries.heading: Associated end date
entries.note: End date referenced by the supporting resource, for example, the ‘latest exam date’ for an official recommendation

entries.heading: Review
entries.note: The full text of a review in a third-party publication in any medium

entries.heading: Media mention
entries.note: Other than a review

entries.heading: ‘One locality, one book’ program
entries.note: Inclusion in a program such as ‘Chicago Reads’, ‘Seattle Reads’, ‘Canada Reads’, ‘One Dublin, one book’

entries.heading: Curated list
entries.note: For example a ‘best books of the year’ or ‘25 books you should have read’ list, without regard to their bestseller status

entries.heading: Commentary / discussion
entries.note: For example a third party podcast episode, social media message, newsletter issue, other commentary (see also code 03 for very brief items)

entries.heading: Interview
entries.note: Interview, for example with a contributor, in a third-party publication in any medium

entries.heading: Soundtrack
entries.note: For example a curated music playlist to accompany the product, environmental sounds etc

entries.heading: TV
entries.note: Including streaming video services (‘TV on demand’) as well as broadcast TV

entries.heading: Front cover
entries.note: 2D

entries.heading: Back cover
entries.note: 2D

entries.heading: Spine image
entries.note: 2D, portrait orientation

entries.heading: Spine panorama image
entries.note: 2D, image spans multiple upright spines

entries.heading: Cover / pack
entries.note: Not limited to front or back, including 3D perspective

entries.heading: Contributor picture
entries.note: Photograph or portrait of contributor(s)

entries.heading: Product image / artwork
entries.note: For example, an isolated image from the front cover (without text), image of a completed jigsaw

entries.heading: Contributor presentation
entries.note: Contributor presentation and/or commentary

entries.heading: Contributor event schedule
entries.note: Link to a schedule in iCalendar format

entries.heading: Sample content
entries.note: For example: a short excerpt, sample text or a complete sample chapter, page images, screenshots etc

entries.heading: Widget
entries.note: A ‘look inside’ feature presented as a small embeddable application

entries.heading: Review
entries.note: Review text held in a separate downloadable file, not in the ONIX record. Equivalent of code 06 in List 153. Use the <TextContent> composite for review quotes carried in the ONIX record. Use the <CitedContent> composite for a third-party review which is referenced from the ONIX record. Use <SupportingResource> for review text offered as a separate file resource for reproduction as part of promotional material for the product

entries.heading: Commentary / discussion
entries.note: For example a publisher’s podcast episode, social media message, newsletter issue, other commentary

entries.heading: Teacher’s guide
entries.note: Including associated teacher / instructor resources

entries.heading: Feature article
entries.note: Feature article provided by publisher

entries.heading: Character ‘interview’
entries.note: Fictional character ‘interview’

entries.heading: Table of contents
entries.note: A table of contents held in a separate downloadable file, not in the ONIX record. Equivalent of code 04 in List 153. Use the <TextContent> composite for a table of contents carried in the ONIX record. Use <SupportingResource> for text offered as a separate file resource

entries.heading: Trailer
entries.note: A promotional video (or audio), similar to a movie trailer (sometimes referred to as a ‘book trailer’)

entries.heading: Cover thumbnail
entries.note: Intended ONLY for transitional use, where ONIX 2.1 records referencing existing thumbnail assets of unknown pixel size are being re-expressed in ONIX 3.0. Use code 01 for all new cover assets, and where the pixel size of older assets is known

entries.heading: Full content
entries.note: The full content of the product (or the product itself), supplied for example to support full-text search or indexing

entries.heading: Full cover
entries.note: Includes cover, back cover, spine and – where appropriate – any flaps

entries.heading: Description
entries.note: Descriptive text in a separate downloadable file, not in the ONIX record. Equivalent of code 03 in List 153. Use the <TextContent> composite for descriptions carried in the ONIX record. Use <SupportingResource> for text offered as a separate file resource for reproduction as part of promotional material for the product

entries.heading: Index
entries.note: Index text held in a separate downloadable file, not in the ONIX record. Equivalent of code 15 in List 153. Use the <TextContent> composite for index text carried in the ONIX record. Use <SupportingResource> for an index offered as a separate file resource

entries.heading: Student’s guide
entries.note: Including associated student / learner resources

entries.heading: Publisher’s catalogue
entries.note: For example a PDF or other digital representation of a publisher’s ‘new titles’ or range catalog

entries.heading: Online advertisement panel
entries.note: For example a banner ad for the product. Pixel dimensions should typically be included in <ResourceVersionFeature>

entries.heading: Online advertisement page
entries.note: (de: ‘Búhnenbild’)

entries.heading: Promotional event material
entries.note: For example, posters, logos, banners, advertising templates for use in connection with a promotional event

entries.heading: Digital review copy
entries.note: Availability of a digital review, evaluation or sample copy, or a digital proof copy, which may be limited to authorized users or account holders, but should otherwise be fully readable and functional

entries.heading: Instructional material
entries.note: For example, a video, PDF, web page or app showing how to assemble, use or maintain the product, that is separate from the product itself

entries.heading: Introduction
entries.note: Introduction, preface or other preliminary material in a separate resource file

entries.heading: Collection description
entries.note: Descriptive material in a separate resource file, not in the ONIX record. Equivalent of code 17 in List 153. Use the <TextContent> composite for collection descriptions carried in the ONIX record. Use <SupportingResource> for material (which need not be solely only) offered as a separate file resource for reproduction as part of promotional material for the product and collection

entries.heading: Bibliography
entries.note: Complete list of books by the author(s), supplied as a separate resource file

entries.heading: Abstract
entries.note: Formal summary of content (normally used with academic and scholarly content only)

entries.heading: Cover holding image
entries.note: Image that may be used for promotional purposes in place of a front cover, ONLY where the front cover itself cannot be provided or used for any reason. Typically, holding images may comprise logos, artwork or an unfinished front cover image. Senders should ensure removal of the holding image from the record as soon as a cover image is available. Recipients must ensure replacement of the holding image with the cover image when it is supplied

entries.heading: Rules or instructions
entries.note: Eg for a game or kit – as supplied with the product

entries.heading: Transcript
entries.note: Full transcript of audio or video content of the product

entries.heading: Full cast and credit list
entries.note: For use with dramatized audiobooks, filmed entertainment etc, for a cast list sent as a separate resource file, not in the ONIX record. Equivalent of code 28 in List 153

entries.heading: Image for social media
entries.note: Image – not specifically a cover image or artwork, contributor image, or logo – explicitly intended for use in social media

entries.heading: Supplementary learning resources
entries.note: Eg downloadable worksheets, home learning materials

entries.heading: Cover flap image
entries.note: 2D, front or back flap image

entries.heading: Warning label
entries.note: Image of any warning label or hazard warning text on product or packaging, eg as required for EU General or Toy Safety, or for battery safety purposes

entries.heading: Product safety contacts
entries.note: Document giving full contact detail, including postal addresses, for product safety contacts at publisher or supplier. Deprecated, except for use in ONIX 3.0

entries.heading: Page edge deco image
entries.note: 2D image of edge decoration (see also List 79 code 02)

entries.heading: Endpaper deco image
entries.note: 2D image of endpaper (or inside front and back cover) decoration (see also List 79 code 55)

entries.heading: License
entries.note: Link to a license covering permitted usage of the product content. Deprecated in favor of <EpubLicense>. This was a temporary workaround in ONIX 3.0, and use of <EpubLicense> is strongly preferred. Not for use in ONIX 3.1 or later

entries.heading: Application
entries.note: An executable together with data on which it operates

entries.heading: Audio
entries.note: A sound recording

entries.heading: Image
entries.note: A still image

entries.heading: Text
entries.note: Readable text, with or without associated images etc

entries.heading: Video
entries.note: Moving images, with or without accompanying sound

entries.heading: Multi-mode
entries.note: A website or other supporting resource delivering content in a variety of modes

entries.heading: Required credit
entries.note: Credit that must be displayed when a resource is used (eg ‘Photo Jerry Bauer’ or ‘© Magnum Photo’). Credit text should be carried in <FeatureNote>

entries.heading: Caption
entries.note: Explanatory caption that may accompany a resource (eg use to identify an author in a photograph). Caption text should be carried in <FeatureNote>

entries.heading: Copyright holder
entries.note: Copyright holder of resource (indicative only, as the resource can be used without consultation). Copyright text should be carried in <FeatureNote>

entries.heading: Length in minutes
entries.note: Approximate length in minutes of an audio or video resource. <FeatureValue> should contain the length of time as an integer number of minutes

entries.heading: ISNI of resource contributor
entries.note: Use to link resource such as a contributor image to a contributor unambiguously. Use for example with Resource Content types 04, 11–14 from List 158, particularly where the product has more than a single contributor. <FeatureValue> contains the 16-digit ISNI, which must match an ISNI given in an instance of <Contributor>

entries.heading: Proprietary ID of resource contributor
entries.note: Use to link resource such as a contributor image to a contributor unambiguously. Use for example with Resource Content types 04, 11–14 from List 158, particularly where the product has more than a single contributor. <FeatureValue> contains the proprietary ID, which must match a proprietary ID given in an instance of <Contributor>

entries.heading: Resource alternative text
entries.note: <FeatureNote> is Alternative text for the resource, which might be presented to visually-impaired readers

entries.heading: Background color of image resource
entries.note: <FeatureValue> is a 24-bit RGB or 32-bit RBGA color in hexadecimal, eg fff2de for an opaque warm cream. Used when the resource – for example a 3D image of the product – includes a background, or if used with an alpha channel, when the image is irregularly shaped or contains a semi-transparent shadow thrown against a background

entries.heading: Attribute of product image resource
entries.note: <FeatureValue> is an ONIX code from List 256 that describes an attribute of a product image resource (eg perspective of 3D view, content)

entries.heading: Background color of page
entries.note: <FeatureValue> is a 24-bit RGB color in hexadecimal, eg ffc300 for a rich yellow-orange, used when the resource supplier requests a specific background color be displayed behind the resource on a web page

entries.heading: ORCID of resource contributor
entries.note: Use to link resource such as a contributor image to a contributor unambiguously, for example with Resource Content types 04, 11–14 from List 158, particularly where the product has more than a single contributor. <FeatureValue> contains the 16-digit ISNI, which must match an ORCID given in an instance of <Contributor>

entries.heading: Linkable resource
entries.note: A resource that may be accessed by a hyperlink. The current host (eg the ONIX sender, who may be the publisher) will provide ongoing hosting services for the resource for the active life of the product (or at least until the Until Date specified in ). The ONIX recipient may embed the URL in a consumer facing-website (eg as the src attribute in an link), and need not host an independent copy of the resource

entries.heading: Downloadable file
entries.note: A file that may be downloaded on demand for third-party use. The ONIX sender will host a copy of the resource until the specified Until Date, but only for the ONIX recipient’s direct use. The ONIX recipient should download a copy of the resource, and must host an independent copy of the resource if it is used on a consumer-facing website. Special attention should be paid to the ‘Last Updated’ <ContentDate> to ensure the independent copy of the resource is kept up to date

entries.heading: Embeddable application
entries.note: An application which is supplied in a form which can be embedded into a third-party webpage. As type 02, except the resource contains active content such as JavaScript, Flash, etc

entries.heading: File format
entries.note: Resource Version Feature Value carries a code from List 178

entries.heading: Image height in pixels
entries.note: Resource Version Feature Value carries an integer

entries.heading: Image width in pixels
entries.note: Resource Version Feature Value carries an integer

entries.heading: Filename
entries.note: Resource Version Feature Value carries the filename of the supporting resource, necessary only when it is different from the last part of the path provided in <ResourceLink>

entries.heading: Approximate download file size in megabytes
entries.note: Resource Version Feature Value carries a decimal number only, suggested no more than 2 or 3 significant digits (eg 1.7, not 1.7462 or 1.75MB)

entries.heading: MD5 hash value
entries.note: MD5 hash value of the resource file. <ResourceVersionFeatureValue> should contain the 128-bit digest value (as 32 hexadecimal digits). Can be used as a cryptographic check on the integrity of a resource after it has been retrieved

entries.heading: Exact download file size in bytes
entries.note: Resource Version Feature Value carries a integer number only (eg 1831023)

entries.heading: SHA-256 hash value
entries.note: SHA-256 hash value of the resource file. <ResourceVersionFeatureValue> should contain the 256-bit digest value (as 64 hexadecimal digits). Can be used as a cryptographic check on the integrity of a resource after it has been retrieved

entries.heading: ISCC
entries.note: International Standard Content Code, a ‘similarity hash’ derived algorithmically from the resource content itself (see https://iscc.codes). <IDValue> is the ISCC-CODE generated from a digital manifestation of the work, as a variable-length case-insensitive alphanumeric string (or 55 characters including three hyphens if using ISCC v1.0, but this is deprecated). Note alphabetic characters in v1.x ISCCs use Base32 encoding and are conventionally upper case. The ‘ISCC:’ prefix is omitted

entries.heading: Previous filename
entries.note: <ResourceVersionFeatureValue> carries the previous filename of the supporting resource, necessary only when it is different from the last part of the path provided in <ResourceLink> and from the filename provided using <ResourceVersionFeatureType> code 04, and when the data sender suggests the recipient delete this old file. Note that the ‘trigger’ to update the resource and delete the old file is provided by the Resource version’s <ContentDate>

entries.heading: Publication date
entries.note: Nominal date of publication. This date is primarily used for planning, promotion and other business process purposes, and is not necessarily the first date for retail sales or fulfillment of pre-orders. In the absence of a sales embargo date, retail sales and pre-order fulfillment may begin as soon as stock is available to the retailer

entries.heading: Sales embargo date
entries.note: If there is an embargo on retail sales (in the market) before a certain date, the date from which the embargo is lifted and retail sales and fulfillment of pre-orders are permitted. (In some markets, this may be termed a ‘strict on-sale date’.) In the absence of an embargo date, retail sales and pre-order fulfillment may begin as soon as stock is available to the retailer

entries.heading: Public announcement date
entries.note: Date when a new product may be announced to the general public. Prior to the announcement date, the product data is intended for internal use by the recipient and supply chain partners only. After the announcement date, or in the absence of an announcement date, the planned product may be announced to the public as soon as metadata is available

entries.heading: Trade announcement date
entries.note: Date when a new product may be announced to the book trade only. Prior to the announcement date, the product information is intended for internal use by the recipient only. After the announcement date, or in the absence of a trade announcement date, the planned product may be announced to supply chain partners (but not necessarily made public – see the Public announcement date) as soon as metadata is available

entries.heading: Date of first publication
entries.note: Date when the work incorporated in a product was first published. For works in translation, see also Date of first publication in original language (code 20)

entries.heading: Latest reprint date
entries.note: Date when a product was most recently reprinted

entries.heading: Out-of-print / permanently withdrawn date
entries.note: Date when a product was (or will be) declared out-of-print, permanently withdrawn from sale or deleted

entries.heading: Latest reissue date
entries.note: Date when a product was most recently reissued

entries.heading: Publication date of print counterpart
entries.note: Date of publication of a printed book which is the direct print counterpart to a digital product. The counterpart product may be included in <RelatedProduct> using code 13

entries.heading: Date of first publication in original language
entries.note: Date when the original language version of the work incorporated in a product was first published (note, use only on works in translation – and also see code 11 for the first publication date of the translation)

entries.heading: Forthcoming reissue date
entries.note: Date when a product will be reissued

entries.heading: Expected availability date after temporary withdrawal
entries.note: Date when a product that has been temporary withdrawn from sale or recalled for any reason is expected to become available again, eg after correction of quality or technical issues

entries.heading: Review embargo date
entries.note: Date from which reviews of a product may be published eg in newspapers and magazines or online. Provided to the book trade for information only: newspapers and magazines are not expected to be recipients of ONIX metadata

entries.heading: Publisher’s reservation order deadline
entries.note: Latest date on which an order may be placed with the publisher for guaranteed delivery prior to the publication date. May or may not be linked to a special reservation or pre-publication price

entries.heading: Forthcoming reprint date
entries.note: Date when a product will be reprinted

entries.heading: Preorder embargo date
entries.note: Earliest date a retail ‘preorder’ can be placed (in the market), where this is distinct from the public announcement date. In the absence of a preorder embargo, advance orders can be placed as soon as metadata is available to the consumer (this would be the public announcement date, or in the absence of a public announcement date, the earliest date metadata is available to the retailer)

entries.heading: Transfer date
entries.note: Date of acquisition of product by new publisher (use with publishing roles 09 and 13)

entries.heading: Date of production
entries.note: For an audiovisual work (eg on DVD)

entries.heading: Streaming embargo date
entries.note: For digital products that are available to end customers both as a download and streamed, the earliest date the product can be made available on a stream, where the streamed version becomes available later than the download. For the download, see code 02 if it is embargoed or code 01 if there is no embargo

entries.heading: Subscription embargo date
entries.note: For digital products that are available to end customers both as purchases and as part of a subscription package, the earliest date the product can be made available by subscription, where the product may not be included in a subscription package until some while after publication. For ordinary sales, see code 02 if there is a sales embargo or code 01 if there is no embargo

entries.heading: Download embargo date
entries.note: For digital products that are available to end customers both as a download and streamed, the earliest date the product can be made available via download, where the download version becomes available later than the stream. For any embargo on the stream, see code 02

entries.heading: Purchase embargo date
entries.note: For digital products that are available to end customers both as purchases and as part of a subscription package, the earliest date the product can be made available to purchase, where the product may not be purchased until some while after it becomes available via the subscription. For any embargo on the subscription, see code 02

entries.heading: CIP date
entries.note: Date by which CIP copy is required for inclusion in the product

entries.heading: Date of first unabridged publication
entries.note: Date when the unabridged version of the work incorporated in a product was first published (note, use only on abridged works – and also see code 11 for the first publication date of the abridgement)

entries.heading: Year of publication
entries.note: Where this is managed separately from the date of publication (code 01), for example for library use. Note, requires an explicit dateformat="05" attribute (YYYY)

entries.heading: Preview embargo date
entries.note: Date from which previews of a product may be made available, where the embargo is managed separately from any Sales embargo date. Applies to all previews (previews in <TextContent> or <SupportingResource>, previews covered by <EpubUsageConstraint> and external preview ‘widgets’) UNLESS overridden by a Valid from date for a specific preview

entries.heading: Library embargo date
entries.note: For digital products that are available to end customers both via retail sale and sales to libraries, the earliest date the product can be made available to purchase by libraries, or made available by a library to patrons. For any embargo on non-library sales, see code 02

entries.heading: Manifestation of
entries.note: Product A is or includes a manifestation of work X. (There is a direct parent–child relation between work X and the product). The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work X

entries.heading: Derived from
entries.note: Product A is or includes a manifestation of a work X which is derived (directly) from related work W in one or more of the ways specified in the former ISTC rules. (There is a relationship between a grandparent work W and a parent work X, and between that parent work and the product.) This relation type is intended to enable products with a common ‘grandparent’ work to be linked without specifying the precise nature of their derivation, and without necessarily assigning an identifier to the product’s parent work X. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work W. Codes 20–30 may be used instead to provide details of the derivation of work X from work W

entries.heading: Related work is derived from this
entries.note: Product A is a manifestation of a work X from which related work Y is (directly) derived in one or more of the ways specified in the former ISTC rules. (There is a relationship between a parent work X and a child work Y, and between the parent work X and the product.) The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work Y. Codes 40–50 may be used instead to provide details of the derivation of work Y from work X

entries.heading: Other work in same (bibliographic) collection
entries.note: Product A is a manifestation of a work X in the same (bibliographic) collection as related work Z. (There is a relationship between the parent work X and a ‘same collection’ work Z, and between the parent work X and the product.) The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work Z

entries.heading: Other work by same contributor
entries.note: Product A is a manifestation of a work X by the same contributor(s) as related work Z. (There is a relationship between the parent work X and a work Z where X and Z have at least one contributor in common, and between the parent work X and the product.) The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work Z

entries.heading: Manifestation of original work
entries.note: Product A is or includes a manifestation of work X. (There is a direct parent–child relation between work X and the product, and work X is original, ie not a derived work of any kind – there is no work W.) The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work X. See code 01 if the originality of X is unspecified or unknown

entries.heading: Derived from by abridgement
entries.note: Product A is or includes a manifestation of a work X which is derived directly from related work W by abridgement. (There is a relationship between the grandparent [unabridged] work W and the parent [abridged] work X, and between the parent work X and the product.) The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [unabridged] work W. <EditionType> of product A would normally be ABR. See code 02 if the method of derivation of X from W is unknown or unstated. The [abridged] parent work X may be identified using a separate instance of <RelatedWork> with relation code 01

entries.heading: Derived from by annotation
entries.note: Product A is or includes a manifestation of a work X which is derived directly from related work W by annotation. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [unannotated] work W. <EditionType> of product X would normally be ANN, VAR etc. See code 02 if the method of derivation of X from W is unknown or unstated. The [annotated] parent work X may be identified using a separate instance of <RelatedWork> with relation code 01

entries.heading: Derived from by compilation
entries.note: The content of the work X has been formed by compilation of work W and another work Z. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work W. <EditionType> of product A may be CMB. Work Z may be identified using a separate instance of <RelatedWork> with code 23. The compiled parent work X may be identified using a separate instance of <RelatedWork> with relation code 01

entries.heading: Derived from by criticism
entries.note: The content of the work W has been augmented by the addition of critical commentary to form work X. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work W. <EditionType> of Product A would normally be CRI

entries.heading: Derived from by excerption
entries.note: The content of the work X is an excerpt from work W. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [complete] work W

entries.heading: Derived from by expurgation
entries.note: Offensive or unsuitable text material has been removed from work W to form work X. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [unsuitable] work W. <EditionType> of Product A would normally be EXP

entries.heading: Derived from by addition (of non-text material)
entries.note: The content of work W has been augmented by the addition of significant non-textual elements to form work X. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [unaugmented] work W. <EditionType> of product A may be ILL, ENH etc

entries.heading: Derived from by revision
entries.note: The content of work W has been revised and/or expanded or enlarged to form work X [including addition, deletion or replacement of text material]. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [unrevised] work W. <EditionType> of product A may be REV, NED, etc, or A may be numbered

entries.heading: Derived from via translation
entries.note: The content of work W has been translated into another language to form work X. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [untranslated] work W

entries.heading: Derived from via adaptation
entries.note: The content of work W has been adapted [into a different literary form] to form work X. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for [unadapted] work W. <EditionType> of product A would normally be ADP, ACT etc

entries.heading: Derived from by subtraction (of non-text material)
entries.note: The content of work W has been modified by the removal of significant non-textual elements to form work X. The instance of <RelatedWork> must include an identifier for work W

entries.heading: Related work is derived from this by abridgement
entries.note: Product A is a manifestation of a work X from which the related work Y is (directly) derived by abridgement. (There is a relationship between the parent [unabridged] work X and the child [abridged] work Y, and between parent work X and the product.) The instance of <RelatedWork> must include the identifier for [abridged] work Y. See code 03 if the method of derivation of Y from X is unknown or unstated. The [unabridged] parent work X may be identified using a separate instance of <RelatedWork> with relation code 01 or 06

entries.heading: Related work is derived from this by annotation
Related work is derived from this by compilation
Related work is derived from this by criticism
Related work is derived from this by excerption
Related work is derived from this by expurgation
Related work is derived from this by addition (of non-text material)
Related work is derived from this by revision
Related work is derived from this via translation
Related work is derived from this via adaptation
Derived from this by subtraction (of non-text material)
Manifestation of LRM work
entries.note: Product A is or includes a manifestation of an expression of LRM work X. Do not use, except as a workaround for differences between LRM works and expressions, and ONIX works in LRM library practice, and always also include a relationship to an ONIX work using code 01

entries.heading: Manifestation of LRM expression
entries.note: Product A is or includes a manifestation of an LRM expression with the same content, same agents and in the same modality (text, audio, video etc) as work X. Do not use, except as a workaround for differences between LRM expressions and ONIX works in LRM library practice, and always also include a relationship to an ONIX work using code 01

entries.heading: Supplier’s sales classification
entries.note: A rating applied by a supplier (typically a wholesaler) to indicate its assessment of the expected or actual sales performance of a product

entries.heading: Supplier’s bonus eligibility
entries.note: A supplier’s coding of the eligibility of a product for a bonus scheme on overall sales

entries.heading: Publisher’s sales classification
entries.note: A rating applied by the publisher to indicate a sales category (eg backlist / frontlist, core stock etc). Use only when the publisher is not the ‘supplier’

entries.heading: Supplier’s pricing restriction classification
entries.note: A classification applied by a supplier to a product sold on Agency terms, to indicate that retail price restrictions are applicable

entries.heading: Supplier’s sales expectation
entries.note: Code is the ISBN of another book that had sales (both in terms of copy numbers and customer profile) comparable to that the distributor or supplier estimates for the product. <SupplierCodeValue> must be an ISBN-13 or GTIN-13

entries.heading: Publisher’s sales expectation
entries.note: Code is the ISBN of another book that had sales (both in terms of copy numbers and customer profile) comparable to that the publisher estimates for the product. <SupplierCodeValue> must be an ISBN-13 or GTIN-13

entries.heading: Supplier’s order routing eligibility
