entries.note: Code indicates whether an order can be placed with the supplier indirectly via an intermediary system. The code name type indicates the specific intermediate order aggregation / routing platform and the code indicates the eligibility

entries.heading: Sales embargo date
entries.note: If there is an embargo on retail sales (of copies from the supplier) before a certain date and this is later than any general or market-wide embargo date, the date from which the embargo is lifted and retail sales and fulfillment of pre-orders are permitted. Use code 02 here ONLY in the exceptional case when the embargo is supplier-specific. More general market-wide or global sales embargos should be specified in <MarketDate> or <PublishingDate> codes. In the absence of any supplier-specific, market-wide or general embargo date, retail sales and pre-order fulfillment may begin as soon as stock is available to the retailer

entries.heading: Expected availability date
entries.note: The date on which physical stock is expected to be available to be shipped from the supplier to retailers, or a digital product is expected to be released by the publisher or digital asset distributor to retailers or their retail platform providers

entries.heading: Last date for returns
entries.note: Last date when returns will be accepted, generally for a product which is being remaindered or put out of print

entries.heading: Reservation order deadline
entries.note: Latest date on which an order may be placed for guaranteed delivery prior to the publication date. May or may not be linked to a special reservation or pre-publication price

entries.heading: Last redownload date
entries.note: Latest date on which existing owners or licensees may download or re-download a copy of the product. Existing users may continue to use their local copy of the product

entries.heading: Last TPM date
entries.note: Date on which any required technical protection measures (DRM) support will be withdrawn. DRM-protected products may not be usable after this date

entries.heading: Expected warehouse date
entries.note: The date on which physical stock is expected to be delivered to the supplier from the manufacturer or from a primary distributor. For the distributor or wholesaler (the supplier) this is the ‘goods in’ date, as contrasted with the Expected availability date, code 08, which is the ‘goods out’ date

entries.heading: New supplier start date
entries.note: First date on which the supplier specified in <NewSupplier> will accept orders. Note the first date would typically be the day after the old supplier end date, but they may overlap if there is an agreement to forward any orders between old and new supplier for fulfillment

entries.heading: Supplier end date
entries.note: Last date on which the supplier specified in <Supplier> will accept orders. New supplier should be specified where available. Note last date would typically be the day before the new supplier start date, but they may overlap if there is an agreement to forward any orders between old and new supplier for fulfillment

entries.heading: No conditions
entries.note: Allows positive indication that there are no conditions (the default if <PriceCondition> is omitted)

entries.heading: Includes updates
entries.note: Purchase at this price includes specified updates

entries.heading: Must also purchase updates
entries.note: Purchase at this price requires commitment to purchase specified updates, not included in price

entries.heading: Updates available
entries.note: Updates may be purchased separately, no minimum commitment required

entries.heading: Linked subsequent purchase price
entries.note: Use with <PriceConditionQuantity> and <ProductIdentifier>. Purchase at this price requires commitment to purchase the specified linked product, which is not included in the price

entries.heading: Linked prior purchase price
entries.note: Use with <PriceConditionQuantity> and <ProductIdentifier>. Purchase at this price requires prior purchase of the specified linked product

entries.heading: Linked price
entries.note: Use with <PriceConditionQuantity> and <ProductIdentifier>. Purchase at this price requires simultaneous purchase of the specified linked product, which is not included in the price

entries.heading: Auto-renewing
entries.note: The rental or subscription will automatically renew at the end of the period unless actively cancelled

entries.heading: Combined price
entries.note: Purchase at this price includes the price of the specified other product

entries.heading: Rental duration
entries.note: The duration of the rental to which the price applies. Deprecated, use <PriceConstraint> instead

entries.heading: Rental to purchase
entries.note: Purchase at this price requires prior rental of the product. <PriceConditionQuantity> gives minimum prior rental period, and <ProductIdentifier> may be used if rental uses a different product identifier

entries.heading: Rental extension
entries.note: Upgrade to longer rental duration. <PriceConditionQuantity> gives minimum prior rental duration, and <ProductIdentifier> may be used if rental uses a different product identifier. Separate price constraint with time limited license duration (code 07) specifies the new combined rental duration

entries.heading: Time period
entries.note: The price condition quantity represents a time period

entries.heading: Number of updates
entries.note: The price condition quantity is a number of updates

entries.heading: Number of linked products
entries.note: Use with Price condition type 06 and a Quantity of units. Price is valid when purchased with a specific number of products from a list of product identifiers provided in the associated <ProductIdentifier> composites. Use for example when describing a price for this product which is valid if it is purchased along with any two from a list of other products

entries.heading: Number of copies of this product
entries.note: Use with Price condition type 06 and a Quantity of units. Meeting the Price condition qualifies for purchase of a specified number of copies of this product at this price. Use for example when describing a price that applies to the specified number of units of this product which is valid if they are purchased along with a number of copies of another product

entries.heading: Minimum number of linked products
entries.note: Use with Price condition type 06 and a Quantity of units. Price is valid when purchased with at least a specific number of products from a list of product identifiers provided in the associated <ProductIdentifier> composites. Use for example when describing a price for this product which is valid if it is purchased along with any two from a list of other products

entries.heading: Maximum number of copies of this product
entries.note: (at this price). Use with Price condition type 06 and a Quantity of units. Meeting the Price condition qualifies for purchase of up to the specified number of copies of this product at this price. Use for example when describing a price that applies to the specified number of units of this product which is valid if they are purchased along with a number of copies of another product

entries.heading: Units
entries.note: The quantity refers to a unit implied by the quantity type

entries.heading: Classes
entries.note: Multiple copies or units suitable for a class. A ‘class’ is a group of learners attending a specific course or lesson and generally taught as a group

entries.heading: Rising discount
entries.note: Discount applied to all units in a qualifying order. The default if no <DiscountType> is specified

entries.heading: Rising discount (cumulative)
entries.note: Additional discount may be applied retrospectively, based on number of units ordered over a specific period

entries.heading: Progressive discount
entries.note: Discount applied to marginal units in a qualifying order

entries.heading: Progressive discount (cumulative)
entries.note: Previous orders within a specific time period are counted when calculating a progressive discount

entries.heading: Value-added tax
entries.note: VAT, TVA, IVA, MwSt, GST etc, levied incrementally at all parts of the supply chain

entries.heading: Sales tax
entries.note: General sales tax, levied on retail sales only

entries.heading: ECO
entries.note: ‘Green’ or eco-tax, levied to encourage responsible production or disposal, used only where this is identified separately from value-added or sales taxes

entries.heading: Eurozone
entries.note: Countries that at the time being have the Euro as their national currency. Deprecated

entries.heading: From date
entries.note: Date on which a price becomes effective

entries.heading: Until date
entries.note: Date on which a price ceases to be effective

entries.heading: From… until date
entries.note: Combines From date and Until date to define a period (both dates are inclusive). Use for example with dateformat 06

entries.heading: No
entries.note: Price not printed on product

entries.heading: Yes
entries.note: Price printed on product

entries.heading: CD standard audio format
entries.note: CD ‘red book’ format

entries.heading: MP3 format
entries.note: MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III file

entries.heading: WMA
entries.note: Windows Media Audio format

entries.heading: AAC
entries.note: Advanced Audio Coding format

entries.heading: Ogg/Vorbis
entries.note: Vorbis audio format in the Ogg container

entries.heading: Audible
entries.note: Audio format proprietary to Audible.com

entries.heading: FLAC
entries.note: Free lossless audio codec

entries.heading: AIFF
entries.note: Audio Interchangeable File Format

entries.heading: ALAC
entries.note: Apple Lossless Audio Codec

entries.heading: W3C Audiobook format
entries.note: Audiobook package format

entries.heading: DAISY 2: full audio with title only (no navigation)
entries.note: Deprecated, as does not meet DAISY 2 standard. Use conventional audiobook codes instead

entries.heading: DAISY 2: full audio with navigation (no text)
DAISY 2: full audio with navigation and partial text
DAISY 2: full audio with navigation and full text
DAISY 2: full text with navigation and partial audio
entries.note: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

entries.heading: DAISY 2: full text with navigation and no audio
entries.note: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

entries.heading: DAISY 3: full audio with title only (no navigation)
entries.note: Deprecated, as does not meet DAISY 3 standard. Use conventional audiobook codes instead

entries.heading: DAISY 3: full audio with navigation (no text)
DAISY 3: full audio with navigation and partial text
DAISY 3: full audio with navigation and full text
DAISY 3: full text with navigation and partial audio
entries.note: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

entries.heading: DAISY 3: full text with navigation and no audio
entries.note: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

entries.heading: Readalong audio
entries.note: Audio intended exclusively for use alongside a printed copy of the book. Most often a children’s product. Normally contains instructions such as ‘turn the page now’ and other references to the printed item, and is usually sold packaged together with a printed copy

entries.heading: Playalong audio
entries.note: Audio intended for musical accompaniment, eg ‘Music minus one’, etc, often used for music learning. Includes singalong backing audio for musical learning or for Karaoke-style entertainment

entries.heading: Speakalong audio
entries.note: Audio intended for language learning, which includes speech plus gaps intended to be filled by the listener

entries.heading: Synchronized audio
entries.note: Audio synchronized to text within an e-publication, for example an EPUB3 with audio overlay. Synchronization at least at paragraph level, and covering the full content

entries.heading: Sound effects
entries.note: Incidental sounds added to the audiobook narration (eg background environmental sounds)

entries.heading: Background music
entries.note: Incidental music added to the audiobook narration (eg to heighten atmosphere). Do not use where the music is a primary part of the audio

entries.heading: Without background sounds
entries.note: Pre-recorded audiobook narration does not contain any background sounds, including music, sound effects, etc, though music and effects may be present if isolated from the speech (ie the sounds do not overlap)

entries.heading: 64kbits/s
entries.note: Constant or average bit rate (eg of an mp3 or AAC audio file) 64kbits/second or more. Note the bit rate is the total across all channels, not a per channel rate

entries.heading: 128kbits/s
entries.note: Constant or average bit rate 128bbits/second or more

entries.heading: Mono
entries.note: Includes ‘stereo’ where channels are identical

entries.heading: Stereo
entries.note: Includes ‘joint stereo’

entries.heading: Stereo 2.1
entries.note: Stereo plus low-frequency channel

entries.heading: Surround 4.1
entries.note: Five-channel audio (including low-frequency channel)

entries.heading: Surround 5.1
entries.note: Six-channel audio (including low-frequency channel)

entries.heading: Dolby Atmos
entries.note: Multi-channel ‘spatial’ audio (eg for 7.1.4 speaker arrangements or processed for headphone delivery)

entries.heading: Mass market (rack) paperback
entries.note: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (typically from 6¾ up to 7⅛ x 4¼ inches) and partly by target market and terms of trade. Use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: Trade paperback (US)
entries.note: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (larger than rack-sized) and partly by target market and terms of trade. AKA ‘quality paperback’, and including textbooks. Most paperback books sold in North America except ‘mass-market’ (B101) and ‘tall rack’ (B107) are correctly described with this code. Use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: Digest format paperback
entries.note: In North America, a category of paperback characterized by page size (typically 7 x 5 inches) and generally used for children’s books; use with Product Form code BC. Note: was wrongly shown as B102 (duplicate entry) in Issue 3

entries.heading: A-format paperback
entries.note: In UK and IE, a category of paperback characterized by page size (normally 178 x 111 mm approx); use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: B-format paperback
entries.note: In UK and IE, a category of paperback characterized by page size (normally 198 x 129 mm approx); use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: Trade paperback (UK)
entries.note: In UK and IE, a category of paperback characterized largely by size (usually in traditional hardback dimensions), and often used for paperback originals or retailer / travel / export-exclusives; use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: Tall rack paperback (US)
entries.note: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (typically 7½ x 4¼ inches) and partly by target market and terms of trade; use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: A5 size Tankobon
entries.note: Japanese A-series size, 210 x 148mm. A tankobon is a complete collected story originally published in serialized form (eg in a magazine)

entries.heading: JIS B5 size Tankobon
entries.note: Japanese B-series size, 257 x 182mm

entries.heading: JIS B6 size Tankobon
entries.note: Japanese B-series size, 182 x 128mm

entries.heading: A6 size Bunko
entries.note: Japanese A-series size, 148 x 105mm

entries.heading: B40-dori Shinsho
entries.note: Japanese format, 182x103mm or 173x105mm

entries.heading: Pocket (Sweden, Norway, France)
entries.note: A Swedish, Norwegian, French paperback format, of no particular fixed size. Use with Product Form Code BC

entries.heading: Storpocket (Sweden)
entries.note: A Swedish paperback format, use with Product Form Code BC. In Finnish, Jättipokkari

entries.heading: Kartonnage (Sweden)
entries.note: A Swedish hardback format, use with Product Form Code BB

entries.heading: Flexband (Sweden)
entries.note: A Swedish softback format, use with Product Form Code BC

entries.heading: Mook / Bookazine
entries.note: A softback book in the format of a magazine, usually sold like a book. Use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: Dwarsligger
entries.note: Also called ‘Flipback’. A softback book in a specially compact proprietary format with pages printed in landscape on very thin paper and bound along the long (top) edge (ie parallel with the lines of text). Use with Product Form code BC – see www.dwarsligger.com

entries.heading: 46 size
entries.note: Japanese format, 188 x 127mm

entries.heading: 46-Henkei size
entries.note: Japanese format, approximately 188 x 127mm

entries.heading: A4-Henkei size
entries.note: Japanese format, approximately 297 x 210mm

entries.heading: A5-Henkei size
entries.note: Japanese format, approximately 210 x 146mm

entries.heading: B5-Henkei size
entries.note: Japanese format, approximately 257 x 182mm

entries.heading: B6-Henkei size
entries.note: Japanese format, approximately 182 x 128mm

entries.heading: JIS B7 size
entries.note: Japanese B-series size, 128 x 91mm

entries.heading: Kiku size
entries.note: Japanese format, 218 x 152mm or 227 x 152mm

entries.heading: Kiku-Henkei size
entries.note: Japanese format

entries.heading: JIS B4 size
entries.note: Japanese B-series size, 364 x 257 mm

entries.heading: Paperback (DE)
entries.note: German large paperback format, greater than about 205mm high, with flaps. Use with Product form code BC

entries.heading: Libro de bolsillo
entries.note: Spanish pocket paperback. Use with Product form code BC

entries.heading: Pocket-sized
entries.note: Pocket-sized format, usually less than about 205mm high, without necessarily implying a particular trade category (de: ,Taschenbuch‘; it: «Tascabile / Supertascabile»; es: «libro de bolsillo»; fr: « livre de poche » etc). Use with Product form code BB or BC. See also List 12 code 04

entries.heading: Mass market max paperback
entries.note: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (typically 7⅛ x 4¾ inches) and partly by target market and terms of trade. Use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: Comic book size (US)
entries.note: Standard 10.25 x 6.625in size approx (260 x 170mm)

entries.heading: Comic album size (Euro)
entries.note: Standard 240 x 320mm size approx

entries.heading: B4-Henkei size
entries.note: Japanese format, approximately 364 x 257 mm

entries.heading: Touch-and-feel book
entries.note: Sensory book. A book whose pages have a variety of textured inserts designed to stimulate tactile exploration: see also B214 and B215

entries.heading: Die-cut book
entries.note: A book which is cut into a distinctive non-rectilinear shape and/or in which holes or shapes have been cut internally. (‘Die-cut’ is used here as a convenient shorthand, and does not imply strict limitation to a particular production process)

entries.heading: Book-as-toy
entries.note: A book which is also a toy, or which incorporates a toy as an integral part. (Do not, however, use B213 for a multiple-item product which includes a book and a toy as separate items)

entries.heading: Soft-to-touch book
entries.note: A book whose cover has a soft textured finish, typically over board

entries.heading: Fuzzy-felt book
entries.note: A book with detachable felt pieces and textured pages on which they can be arranged

entries.heading: Press-out pieces
entries.note: A book containing pages with die-cut or press-out pieces that can be used as a jigsaw, as puzzle or game pieces, play pieces (eg paper dolls) etc

entries.heading: Picture book
entries.note: Picture book, generally for children though also occasionally for teens or adults, with few words per illustration: use with applicable Product form code

entries.heading: ‘Carousel’ book
entries.note: (aka ‘Star’ book). Tax treatment of products may differ from that of products with similar codes such as Book as toy or Pop-up book)

entries.heading: Pull-the-tab book
entries.note: A book with movable card ‘tabs’ within the pages. Pull a tab to reveal or animate part of a picture (distinct from a ‘lift-the-flap’ book, where flaps simply reveal hidden pictures, and not specifically a ‘pop-up’ book with 3D paper engineering – though when combined with code B206 indicates a pop-up book with tabs for moveable parts of 3D ‘scenes’)

entries.heading: ‘Wordless’ book
entries.note: Picture book, generally for children though also used in augmentative and alternative education, or for teens and adults, without text in the body of the book. Also ‘silent books’, wordless graphic novels and comic books: use with applicable Product Form code

entries.heading: Cut-out pieces
entries.note: A book containing pages with pieces intended to be cut out (not pre-cut or press-out – see B216) that can be used as puzzle or game pieces, play pieces etc, but which may not be suitable for young children

entries.heading: Loose leaf or partwork – sheets / parts and binder / wallet
entries.note: Use with Product Form code BD, BN or PM

entries.heading: Loose leaf or partwork – binder / wallet only
entries.note: Use with Product Form code BD, BN or PM

entries.heading: Loose leaf or partwork – sheets / parts only
entries.note: Use with Product Form code BD, BN or PM

entries.heading: Sewn
entries.note: AKA stitched; for ‘saddle-sewn’, prefer code B310

entries.heading: Unsewn / adhesive bound
entries.note: Including ‘perfect bound’, ‘glued’

entries.heading: Library binding
entries.note: Strengthened cloth-over-boards binding intended for libraries: use with Product form code BB

entries.heading: Reinforced binding
entries.note: Strengthened binding, not specifically intended for libraries: use with Product form code BB or BC

entries.heading: Half bound
entries.note: Highest quality material used on spine and corners only. Must be accompanied by a code specifying a material, eg ‘half-bound real leather’

entries.heading: Quarter bound
entries.note: Highest quality material used on spine only. Must be accompanied by a code specifying a material, eg ‘quarter bound real leather’

entries.heading: Saddle-sewn
entries.note: AKA ‘saddle-stitched’ or ‘wire-stitched’

entries.heading: Comb bound
entries.note: Round or oval plastic forms in a clamp-like configuration: use with Product Form code BE

entries.heading: Wire-O
entries.note: Twin loop metal wire spine: use with Product Form code BE

entries.heading: Concealed wire
entries.note: Cased over Coiled or Wire-O binding: use with Product Form code BE and Product Form Detail code B312 or B314

entries.heading: Coiled wire bound
entries.note: Spiral wire bound. Use with product form code BE. The default if a spiral binding type is not stated. Cf. Comb and Wire-O binding

entries.heading: Trade binding
entries.note: Hardcover binding intended for general consumers rather than libraries, use with Product form code BB. The default if a hardcover binding detail is not stated. cf. Library binding

entries.heading: Swiss binding
entries.note: Cover is attached to the book block along only one edge of the spine, allowing the cover to lay flat

entries.heading: Notched binding
entries.note: Refinement of perfect binding, with notches cut in the spine of the book block prior to glueing, to improve adhesion and durability

entries.heading: Lay-flat binding
entries.note: Hardcover or softcover where interior spreads lay flat across the spine

entries.heading: Flush cut binding
entries.note: Hardcover where the cover boards are trimmed flush with the trimmed book block

entries.heading: Rounded spine
entries.note: Hardcover where the spine is rounded during binding

entries.heading: Square spine
entries.note: Hardcover where the spine is straight

entries.heading: Self-covered
entries.note: Covers do not use a distinctive stock, but are the same as the body pages. Use for example with Product form BF, to indicate a pamphlet does not use a card or distinct paper cover. See also B416 (for card covers) and B418 (for distinct paper covers)

entries.heading: Cloth over boards
entries.note: Cotton, linen or other woven fabric over boards. Use with <ProductForm> BB

entries.heading: Paper over boards
entries.note: Cellulose-based or similar non-woven material, which may be printed and may be embossed with an artificial cloth or leather-like texture, over boards. Use with <ProductForm> BB

entries.heading: Leather, real
entries.note: Covered with leather created by tanning animal hide. May be ‘full-grain’ using the entire thickness of the hide, ‘top grain’ using the outer layer of the hide, or ‘split’ using the inner layers of the hide. Split leather may be embossed with an artificial grain or texture. Use with <ProductForm> BG, and if appropriate with codes B308 or B309 (otherwise ‘full-bound’ is implied)

entries.heading: Leather, imitation
entries.note: Covered with synthetic leather-like material – polymer or non-animal fibre over a textile backing, usually coated and embossed with an artificial grain or texture. Leatherette, pleather etc. Use with <ProductForm> BB (or BG if particularly high-quality), and if appropriate with codes B308 or B309 (otherwise ‘full-bound’ is implied)

entries.heading: Leather, bonded
entries.note: Covered with leather reconstituted from a pulp made from shredded animal hide, layered on a fibre or textile backing, coated and usually embossed with an artificial grain or texture. Use with <ProductForm> BG, and if appropriate with codes B308 or B309 (otherwise ‘full-bound’ is implied)

entries.heading: Vellum
entries.note: Pages made with prepared but untanned animal skin (usually calf, occasionally goat or sheep). Includes parchment, a thicker and less refined form of animal skin, but not ‘paper vellum’ or vegetable parchment made from synthetic or plant fibres

entries.heading: Head and tail bands
entries.note: Capital bands, either decorative or functional. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color

entries.heading: Decorated page edges
entries.note: Colored, stained, gilded, patterned, abstract or illustrated sprayed edges. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color, and optionally, use <SupportingResource> to provide an image of the decoration

entries.heading: Decorated endpapers
entries.note: Colored, patterned, printed, abstract or illustrated endpapers or of inside front and back covers. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color, and optionally, use <SupportingResource> to provide an image of the decoration

entries.heading: Cloth
entries.note: Cloth, not necessarily over boards – cf B401

entries.heading: Imitation cloth
entries.note: Spanish ‘simil-tela’

entries.heading: Flexible plastic / vinyl cover
entries.note: AKA ‘flexibound’: use with Product Form code BC

entries.heading: Plastic-covered
entries.note: Separate outer plastic cover, often transparent and allowing the cover to show through. Typically has pockets into which the cover tucks. See also B412, where the cover itself is plastic or vinyl

entries.heading: Vinyl-covered
entries.note: Separate outer vinyl cover. See also B412, where the cover itself is plastic or vinyl

entries.heading: Laminated cover
entries.note: Book, laminating material unspecified, often termed PLC or PPC (printed laminated case, printed paper case) when used with Product form BB. Use L101 for ‘whole product laminated’, eg a laminated sheet map or wallchart

entries.heading: Card cover
entries.note: With card cover (like a typical paperback). As distinct from a self-cover or more elaborate binding. Use for example with Product form BF, to indicate a pamphlet is bound within a card cover. See also B400 (for self-covers) and B418 (for distinct paper covers)

entries.heading: Duplex-printed cover
entries.note: Printed both inside and outside the front and/or back cover

entries.heading: Paper cover
entries.note: Cover uses a distinct, usually heavier (thicker) paper than the interior pages. Use for example with Product form BF, to indicate a pamphlet is bound within a paper cover. See also B400 (for self-covers) and B416 (for card covers)

entries.heading: Delicate cover / jacket finish
entries.note: Cover or jacket finish may merit special handling or packaging during distribution and fulfilment, for example because of gloss varnish which may hold fingerprints or matt laminate liable to scuffing

entries.heading: Embossed cover
entries.note: Embossing (or debossing) used on cover or jacket

entries.heading: Temporary stickers on cover or jacket
entries.note: All types of promotional stickers, applied on behalf of the publisher, but easily removable by the reader without damage to the cover or jacket

entries.heading: Permanent stickers on cover or jacket
entries.note: All types of promotional stickers, applied on behalf of the publisher, but not capable of being removed easily without damage to the cover or jacket

entries.heading: Spine panorama
entries.note: Spine illustration combines with spines of other products in a collection to form a panoramic image. Sometimes termed a ‘spinescape’

entries.heading: Belly band
entries.note: Obi. Paper band around the middle of a book (typically tucked inside the front and back cover rather than extending around the whole book)

entries.heading: With dust jacket
entries.note: Type unspecified

entries.heading: With printed dust jacket
entries.note: Used to distinguish from B503

entries.heading: With translucent dust cover
entries.note: With translucent paper or plastic protective cover

entries.heading: With flaps
entries.note: For paperback with flaps – sometimes known as gatefolds or French flaps (extensions of the cover that fold inside the front and back cover)

entries.heading: With ribbon marker(s)
entries.note: If the number of markers is significant, it can be stated as free text in <ProductFormDescription>. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color

entries.heading: With leather edge lining
entries.note: AKA yapp edge?

entries.heading: Rough front
entries.note: With edge trimming such that the front edge is ragged, not neatly and squarely trimmed: AKA deckle edge, feather edge, uncut edge, rough cut

entries.heading: Foldout
entries.note: With one or more gatefold or foldout sections bound into the book block

entries.heading: Wide margin
entries.note: Pages include extra-wide margin specifically intended for hand-written annotations

entries.heading: With fastening strap
entries.note: Book with attached loop for fixing to baby stroller, cot, chair etc

entries.heading: With perforated pages
entries.note: With one or more pages perforated and intended to be torn out for use

entries.heading: Acid-free paper
entries.note: Printed on acid-free or alkaline buffered paper conforming with ISO 9706

entries.heading: Archival paper
entries.note: Printed on acid-free or alkaline buffered paper with a high cotton content, conforming with ISO 11108

entries.heading: With elasticated strap
entries.note: Strap acts as closure or as page marker

entries.heading: With serialized authenticity token
entries.note: For example, holographic sticker such as the banderol used in the Turkish book trade

entries.heading: With dust jacket poster
entries.note: Jacket in the form of a pamphlet or poster, specifically intended to be removed and read or used separately from the book

entries.heading: Rounded corners
entries.note: Usually die-cut rounding to foredge corners of cover (and/or to foredge page corners). See B212 for elaborate die-cutting

entries.heading: Splashproof
entries.note: Water-resistant or ‘waterproof’ cover and pages

entries.heading: Mineral paper
entries.note: Pages composed of ‘mineral paper’ comprised of HDPE plastic and ground calcium carbonate, eg Stonepaper

entries.heading: With accessibility claim ticket
entries.note: For example, cut-out claim form such as the ‘text data request ticket’ used in the Japanese book trade

entries.heading: Plastic paper
entries.note: Pages composed of microporous sheets comprised of non-woven HDPE or HDPP fibers, or of non-porous HDPP film, eg Tyvek or Yupo

entries.heading: With wraparound foredge flap
entries.note: For paperback with flaps (an extension of the cover that folds outside the front or back cover, covering the foredge). The other flap may be absent, conventional or may also wrap around the foredge

entries.heading: Turn-around book
entries.note: A book in which half the content is printed upside-down, to be read the other way round. Also known as a ‘flip-book’ or ‘tête-bêche’ (Fr) binding, it has two front covers and a single spine. Usually an omnibus of two works

entries.heading: Unflipped manga format
entries.note: Manga with pages and panels in the sequence of (right-to-left flowing) Japanese-style design

entries.heading: Back-to-back book
entries.note: A book in which half the content is printed so as to be read from the other cover. All content is printed the same way up. Also known as ‘dos-à-dos’ (Fr) binding, it has two front covers and two spines. Usually an omnibus of two works

entries.heading: Flipped manga format
entries.note: Manga with pages and panels in the sequence mirrored from Japanese-style design (thus flowing left-to-right)

entries.heading: Variant turn-around book
entries.note: A book in which half the content is read the other way round from ‘back’ to ‘front’. A variant on ‘flip-book’ or ‘tête-bêche’ (fr) binding where the text is in two languages with different page progression (eg English and Arabic) and neither needs to be upside down, it has two front covers and a single spine. Usually an omnibus of a work and a derived translated work

entries.heading: Page progression LTR
entries.note: Pages are ordered left to right (the left page in a spread is read before the right). Note this does not specifically mean text on the page is also read left to right

entries.heading: Page progression RTL
entries.note: Pages are ordered right to left

entries.heading: Page progression TTB
entries.note: Pages are ordered top to bottom, with the spine oriented horizontally. See also Dwarsligger (code B118), a proprietary variation of this format

entries.heading: Page progression other
entries.note: Pages are ordered bottom to top, with the spine oriented horizontally, or in a way for which there is no other code

entries.heading: Syllabification
entries.note: Text shows syllable breaks

entries.heading: Upper case only
entries.note: For bicameral scripts, body text is upper case only

entries.heading: UK Uncontracted Braille
entries.note: Single letters only. Was formerly identified as UK Braille Grade 1

entries.heading: UK Contracted Braille
entries.note: With some letter combinations. Was formerly identified as UK Braille Grade 2

entries.heading: US Braille
entries.note: For US Braille, prefer codes B704 and B705 as appropriate

entries.heading: Unified English Braille
entries.note: For UEB, prefer codes B708 and B709 as appropriate

entries.heading: Moon
entries.note: Moon embossed alphabet, used by some print-impaired readers who have difficulties with Braille

entries.heading: Tactile images
entries.note: Eg charts, diagrams, maps, or other tactile graphics or illustrations that are embossed or textured for accessibility purposes

entries.heading: Lenticular images
entries.note: Image-changing effect, ‘3D’ images, ‘tilt cards’, printed with tiny lenses

entries.heading: Anaglyph images

heading: EU General Product Safety Regulation and Toy Safety Directive hazard warning type

entries.heading: No warning
entries.note: Use to provide positive indication that no warnings are applicable

entries.heading: Carries minimum age warning
entries.note: Use to specify age (in years, or years and months). Provide specific wording in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>

entries.heading: Carries EU Toy Safety Directive ‘Unsuitable for children ages 0–3’ warning logo
entries.note: Carries logo, and must be accompanied by the default warning ‘Not suitable for children under 36 months’ (or its approved equivalent in a language other than English, as appropriate), unless specific wording is provided in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. If specific alternative wording is carried in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>, this must be used in place of the default text

entries.heading: Carries EU Toy Safety Directive hazard warning
entries.note: Exact text of warning must be included in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>

entries.heading: Carries other text associated with toy safety
entries.note: Exact text (not in itself a warning) must be included in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. May be used either without any warning, or as text additional to a warning. Note that if no warnings apply, code 00 can provide positive indication of this. Example uses: ‘Suitable for all ages’ or ‘Adult supervision required’

entries.heading: Material Safety Data Sheet available
entries.note: Material Safety Data Sheet (a document required by the EU Toy Safety Directive) available online, typically as a PDF file or similar. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> must carry the URL of the document

entries.heading: Declaration of Conformity available
entries.note: Declaration of Conformity (the document that backs up the CE or CA mark) available online, typically as a PDF file or similar. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> must carry the URL of the document

entries.heading: Carries EN71 conformity statement
entries.note: If specific alternative wording is carried in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>, this must be used in place of the default ‘Conforms to EN71’ text

entries.heading: Carries ‘UKCA’ logo
entries.note: UK Conformity Assessment mark. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Accessibility summary
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> contains a short explanatory summary of the accessibility of the product, or the URL of a web page comprising such a summary, consistent with the more specific conformance, feature and certification details provided. The summary should note both the accessibility features provided and any potential deficiencies. The summary does not remove the requirement for full structured accessibility data, but should be considered a fallback option if more structured detail cannot be provided or used. Use code 92 for a shorter accessibility summary that does NOT repeat information that is sent using codes. Both 00 and 92 can be included. Further detailed information may be provided in an external file using codes 94–96. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: LIA Compliance Scheme
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of the LIA accessibility certification scheme. See https://www.fondazionelia.org/en/services/certification/

entries.heading: EPUB Accessibility Specification 1.0 A
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of EPUB Accessibility Specification 1.0 and WCAG level A. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry a URL linking to a compliance report or certification provided by an independent third party certifier. In the absence of a URL, conformance with the requirements of the Accessibility Specification is self-certified by the publisher. Alternatively, use codes 88–99 to provide extra details about certification

entries.heading: EPUB Accessibility Specification 1.0 AA
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of EPUB Accessibility Specification 1.0 and WCAG level AA. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry a URL linking to a compliance report or certification provided by an independent third party certifier. In the absence of a URL, conformance with the requirements of the Accessibility Specification is self-certified by the publisher. Alternatively, use codes 88–99 to provide extra details about certification

entries.heading: EPUB Accessibility Specification 1.1
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of EPUB Accessibility Specification v1.1 – see https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-a11y-11/. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry a URL linking to a compliance report or certification provided by an independent third-party certifier. In the absence of a URL, conformance with the requirements of the Accessibility Specification is self- certified by the publisher. Alternatively, use codes 88–99 to provide extra details about certification. Use with other List 196 codes to indicate WCAG version and level, ARIA inclusion. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: PDF/UA-1
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of ISO 32000-1:2008 plus ISO 14289-1:2014 – Portable Document Format for Universal Accessibility, including for example, ensuring all content is tagged in logical reading order and correctly represents the document’s semantic structure. See https://pdfa.org/accessibility/. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: PDF/UA-2
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of ISO 32000-2:2020 (PDF 2.0) plus ISO 14289-2:2024 – Portable Document Format for Universal Accessibility v2, including for example, the revised semantic tagging, MathML, Unicode support and associated documents from PDF 2.0. See https://pdfa.org/accessibility/. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unknown accessibility
entries.note: Product has not yet been assessed for accessibility, or no or insufficient accessibility information is provided. It should be treated as likely to be inaccessible (and also may not have been checked for hazards). <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry details of why the accessibility of the title is unknown, or an Accessibility summary using code 00 may give further details. Include code 92 with latest Accessibility assessment date, where available, and code 99 (or <ProductContact>) for an accessibility contact. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Inaccessible, or known limited accessibility
entries.note: Known to lack significant features required for broad accessibility. Details of and reasons for limitations on accessibility can be given in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>, or an Accessibility summary using code 00 may give further details. Include code 92 with latest accessibility assessment date, and code 99 for an accessibility contact, if available. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: No reading system accessibility options actively disabled (except)
entries.note: No accessibility features or content rendering options offered by the reading system, device or reading software (including but not limited to the ability to modify or choose text size or typeface, word and line spacing, zoom level, text or background color, or use of text-to-speech) are limited, disabled, overridden or otherwise unusable with the product EXCEPT – in ONIX 3 messages only – those specifically noted as subject to restriction or prohibition in <EpubUsageConstraint>. Note that provision of any significant part of the textual content as images (ie as pictures of text, rather than as ‘text-as-text’, and without any textual equivalent) or the application of some technical protection measures (DRM), inevitably prevents full use of these accessibility options. Code 10 means ‘this e-publication is accessible to the full extent that the file format and types of content allow, on a specific reading device, by default, without necessarily including any additions such as textual descriptions of images or enhanced navigation. Note that for reflowable e-books, this means code 36 also applies, although code 10 can also be used with accessible non-reflowable (fixed-format) e-publications and with audio material. Should be used with other codes that describe any additions to enhance the level of accessibility

entries.heading: Table of contents navigation
entries.note: Table of contents allows direct (eg hyperlinked) access to all levels of text organization above individual paragraphs (ie to all chapters, sections and subsections that exist within the text), and to all tables, figures, illustrations etc (non-textual items such as illustrations, tables, audio or video content may be directly accessible from the Table of contents, or from a similar List of illustrations, List of tables, etc). For audio and audiovisual content, chapter, section and sub-section timings are provided in <AVItem>

entries.heading: Index navigation
entries.note: Index provides direct (eg hyperlinked) access to uses of the index terms in the document body

entries.heading: Single logical reading order
entries.note: All or substantially all textual matter is arranged in a single logical reading order (including text that is visually presented as separate from the main text flow, eg in boxouts, captions, tables, footnotes, endnotes, citations, etc). Non-textual content is also linked from within this logical reading order. (Purely decorative non-text content can be ignored). All or substantially all audio content should also have a single logical ‘reading order’, which is the order the content should be presented to the listener

entries.heading: Short alternative textual descriptions
entries.note: All or substantially all non-text content has short alternative (textual) descriptions, usually provided via alt attributes, so that they can be presented in the form the reader needs – large text on screen, Braille, speech, simplified language or symbols. Note this applies to normal images (eg photographs, charts and diagrams) and also to any embedded audio, video etc. Audio and video content should include alternative descriptions suitable for hearing-impaired as well as for visually-impaired readers. (Purely decorative non-text content can be ignored, but the accessibility of resources delivered via a network connection rather than delivered as part of the e-publication package must be included). Should be used in association with relevant codes from list 81 or list 175, so it is clear what kind of non-text content is included in the product. In general, short alternative descriptions are intended as brief textual substitutes for images. The short alternative description should not repeat the image’s caption, title or legend

entries.heading: Full alternative textual descriptions
entries.note: Extended descriptions. All or substantially all non-text content has full alternative (textual) extended descriptions, so that they can be presented in the form the reader needs – large text on screen, Braille, speech, simplified language or symbols. Note this applies to normal images (eg photographs, charts and diagrams) and also to any embedded audio, video etc. Audio and video content should include full alternative descriptions (eg audio-described video) and transcript, subtitles or captions (whether closed or open) suitable for hearing-impaired as well as for visually-impaired readers. (Purely decorative non-text content can be ignored, but the accessibility of resources delivered via a network connection rather than delivered as part of the e-publication package must be included). Should be used in association with relevant codes from lists 81 or 175, so it is clear what kind of non-text content is included in the product. In general, full alternative descriptions are intended to describe the image and explain the editorial points that it illustrates in detail. The full extended description should not repeat the image’s caption, title or legend, but should elaborate upon any provided short alt description

entries.heading: Visualized data also available as non-graphical data
entries.note: Where data visualizations are provided (eg graphs and charts), the underlying data is also available in non-graphical (usually tabular or textual) form. Tabular form involves organizing data into rows and columns, making it easier to compare and analyse different items. Textual form uses words and sentences to describe information, alongside or instead of a tabular presentation. Use with relevant codes from list 81

entries.heading: Accessible math content as MathML
entries.note: Mathematical content such as equations is usable with assistive technology, through use of MathML. Semantic MathML is preferred but Presentational MathML is acceptable. Use with code 48 from list 81

entries.heading: Accessible chemistry content as ChemML
entries.note: Chemistry content such as chemical formulae is usable with assistive technology, through use of ChemML. Use with code 47 from list 81

entries.heading: Print-equivalent page numbering
entries.note: For a reflowable e-publication, contains references to the page numbering of an equivalent printed product, page number navigation based on print-equivalent page numbers or digital-only static page breaks, such as the doc-pagebreak role in ARIA or other page break markers. Use <RelatedProduct> with relation code 13 to specify an identifier for the product that is the source of the page numbers

entries.heading: Synchronized pre-recorded audio
entries.note: Text-synchronized pre-recorded audio narration (natural or synthesized voice) is included for substantially all textual matter, including all alternative descriptions, eg via a SMIL media overlay. The product includes both text and audio renditions, and it includes sync information that allows them to be used simultaneously

entries.heading: Text-to-speech hinting provided
entries.note: Text-to-speech has been optimized through provision of PLS (Pronunciation Lexicon Specification) lexicons, SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) or CSS Speech synthesis hints, or other speech synthesis markup languages or hinting

entries.heading: Language tagging provided
entries.note: The language of the text has been specified (eg via the HTML or XML lang attribute) to optimize text-to-speech (and other alternative renderings), both at whole document level and, where appropriate, for individual words, phrases or passages in a different language. Language(s) used in the product should be specified using <Language>

entries.heading: Dyslexia readability
entries.note: Specialized font, character and/or line spacing, justification and paragraph spacing, coloring and other options provided specifically to improve readability for dyslexic readers. Details, including the name of the font if relevant, should be listed in <ProductFormFeatureDescription>. Use with <EditionType> code HRE as appropriate

entries.heading: Use of color is not sole means of conveying information
entries.note: For readers with color vision deficiency, use of color (eg in diagrams, graphs and charts, in prompts or on buttons inviting a response) is not the sole means of graphical distinction or of conveying information, which means that color perception is not necessary to understand the content, and the content is not color-dependent. Use <PrimaryContent> and <ProductContent>, and relevant codes from list 81, to specify the types of content included in the product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Use of high contrast between text and background color
entries.note: Body text is presented with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large / heading text), so the text can be read more easily by people with impaired vision. Use <PrimaryContent> and <ProductContent>, and relevant codes from list 81, to specify the types of content included in the product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Use of high contrast between foreground and background audio
entries.note: Foreground audio content (eg voice) is presented with no or low background noise (eg ambient sounds, music), at least 20dB below the level of the foreground, or background noise can be switched off (eg via an alternative audio track). Brief and occasional sound effects may be as loud as foreground voice so long as they are isolated (or isolatable) from the foreground, to ensure any speech is not disrupted. Detailed description of how the audio meets this requirement can be included in an accessibility addendum (see code 92). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Full alternative audio descriptions
entries.note: All or substantially all video or moving image content has full description as pre-recorded audio. Video content should include full alternative descriptions (eg audio-described video) and transcript, subtitles or captions (whether closed or open) suitable for hearing-impaired as well as for visually-impaired readers. (Purely decorative non-text content can be ignored, but the accessibility of resources delivered via a network connection rather than delivered as part of the e-publication package must be included). For products that are primarily video, see Product form detail code V215. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Next / Previous structural navigation
entries.note: All levels of heading and other structural elements of the content are correctly marked up and (if applicable) numbered, to enable fast next heading / previous heading, next chapter / previous chapter navigation without returning to the table of contents. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: ARIA roles provided
entries.note: Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA) roles (including associated states and properties) are used to organize and improve the structural or landmark navigation of the publication (eg to identify key sections of the content and the purpose of hyperlinks). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Accessible controls provided
entries.note: Where interactive content is included in the product, timing controls are provided (eg for speed, pause and resume, reset) and labelled to make their use clear. All activities that have a timed interaction are adjustable so that all users have adequate time to complete tasks. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Landmark navigation
entries.note: E-publication includes basic landmark navigation (usually less detailed than TOC-based navigation). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Accessible chemistry content (as MathML)
entries.note: Chemistry content such as chemical formulae is usable with assistive technology, through use of MathML. Use with code 47 from list 81. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Accessible math content (as LaTeX)
entries.note: Mathematical content such as equations is usable with assistive technology, through use of LaTeX. Use with code 48 from list 81. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Appearance of all textual content can be modified
entries.note: E-publication does not restrict the ability of users to modify and reflow the display of any textual content to the full extent allowed by the reading system (eg to change the text size or typeface, line height and word spacing, colors). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. Compare with code 10 which applies to a broader range of content types

entries.heading: Use of ultra-high contrast between text foreground and background
entries.note: Body text is presented with a contrast ratio of at least 7:1 (or 4.5:1 for large / heading text). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Unusual words or abbreviations explained
entries.note: E-publication provides explanations for unusual words, abbreviations, acronyms, idioms, jargon in an accessible form, such as glossaries, scripted pop-ups. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Supplementary material to an audiobook is accessible
entries.note: All supplementary visual or textual material necessary for understanding of an audiobook, is available as pre-recorded audio, or has full alternative text that can be read via text-to- speech. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Link purposes clear
entries.note: Where links, controls or buttons are included in the product, the purpose or functionality of each link, control or button is apparent from the associated text alone – or where it is unclear, separate link, control or button descriptions are provided. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Page list navigation
entries.note: E-publication includes page number navigation, based on print-equivalent page numbers (see code 19) or digital-only static page breaks. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: All non-decorative content supports reading via pre-recorded audio
entries.note: All contents of the digital publication necessary to use and understanding, including any text, images (via alternative descriptions), video (via audio description) is fully accessible via suitable audio reproduction. The entire publication can be navigated and ‘read’ using only pre-recorded sound, and does not require visual or tactile perception. NB this implies that all <ProductContent> types listed can be accessed without sight. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: All non-decorative content supports reading without sight
entries.note: Sometimes termed ‘screen reader-friendly’, and fully supports multiple forms of non-visual reading. All contents of the digital publication necessary to use and understanding, including text, images (via their alternative descriptions), audio and video material (via their transcripts, descriptions, captions or subtitles) are fully accessible via suitable reading devices, for example text-to-speech screen readers or tactile reading devices (‘Braille displays’), and nothing in the digital publication prevents or blocks the use of alternative reading modes. The entire publication can be navigated and ‘read’ using only text rendered via sound or touch, and does not require visual perception. NB this implies that all <ProductContent> types listed can be accessed without sight. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Described math content
entries.note: Textual description of mathematical content, either as an alternative description attached to an image of the content, or in addition to MathML or LaTeX. Use with code 48 from list 81. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Accessible chemistry content (as LaTeX)
entries.note: Chemistry content such as chemical formulae is usable with assistive technology, through use of laTeX. Use with code 47 from list 81. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EAA exception 1 – Micro-enterprises
entries.note: Digital product falls under European Accessibility Act exception for Micro-enterprises (as defined by current regulations). The product may not have to comply fully with requirements of the EAA if the publisher is a micro-enterprise. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry details justifying the exception claim. Use for example with code 09, if product is considered of limited accessibility, but include codes for other relevant features of the product that make it accessible to some, and include an Accessibility summary describing the accessibility features and limitations of the product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EAA exception 2 – Disproportionate burden
entries.note: Digital product falls under European Accessibility Act exception for Disproportionate burden (as defined by current regulations). The product may not have to comply fully with requirements of the EAA if doing so would financially overburden the publisher. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry details justifying the exception claim. Use for example with code 09, if product is considered of limited accessibility, but include codes for other relevant features of the product that make it accessible to some, and include an Accessibility summary describing the accessibility features and limitations of the product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: EAA exception 3 – Fundamental alteration
entries.note: Digital product falls under European Accessibility Act exception for Fundamental alteration (as defined by current regulations). The product may not have to comply fully with requirements of the EAA if doing so requires a fundamental modification of the nature of the product or service. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry details justifying the exception claim. Use for examp with code 09, if product is considered of limited accessibility, but include codes for other relevant features of the product that make it accessible to some, and include an Accessibility summary describing the accessibility features and limitations of the product. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WCAG v2.0
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of WCAG version 2.0 – see https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry a URL linking to a compliance report or certification provided by an independent third-party certifier. In the absence of a URL, conformance with the requirements of the Specification is self-certified by the publisher. Should be used in combination with code 04. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WCAG v2.1
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WCAG v2.2
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WCAG level A
entries.note: Conforms with the requirements of WCAG level A. <ProductFormFeatureDescription> may carry a URL linking to a compliance report or certification provided by an independent third-party certifier. In the absence of a URL, conformance with the requirements of the Specification is self-certified by the publisher. Should be used in combination with code 04. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WCAG level AA
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: WCAG level AAA
entries.note: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Certifier credentialled by (name)
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the name of the organization responsible for credentialling the certifier named as certifying the compliance of the product (see code 90) – ie ‘who certifies the certifier?’ Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Certifier credentialled by (URL)
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the URL of a web page belonging to an organization responsible for credentialling the certifier identified (via URL) as certifying the compliance of the product (see code 93) – ie ‘who certifies the certifier?’ Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Compliance certification by (name)
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the name of the organization responsible for compliance testing and certification of the product. See code 93 for the URL of the organization, which should also be provided. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Latest accessibility assessment date
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> contains a date in the YYYYMMDD format of the latest assessment or re-assessment of the accessibility of the product. (Note that changes to or re-confirmation of individual accessibility features, standards conformance or certification may be highlighted with a timestamp attribute on the relevant repeat of <ProductFormFeature>). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Accessibility addendum
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> contains a short addendum to the accessibility detail of the product, or the URL of a web page comprising such an addendum, providing further details of the specific conformance and features details provided. The addendum should be considered additional to the more structured data. A complete Accessibility summary (including information that is duplicated in the structured data) should be provided using code 00. Further detailed information may be provided in an external file using codes 94–96. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Compliance certification by (URL)
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the URL of a web page belonging to an organization responsible for compliance testing and certification of the product – typically a ‘home page’ or a page describing the certification scheme itself. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Compliance web page for detailed accessibility information
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the URL of a web page giving further detailed description of the accessibility features, compatibility, testing, certification etc relevant to this product. The web page should be maintained by an independent compliance scheme or testing organization. Note the web page may include information about specific national requirements or voluntary conformance reports

entries.heading: Trusted intermediary’s web page for detailed accessibility information
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the URL of a web page giving further detailed description of the accessibility features, compatibility, testing etc relevant to this product. The web page should be provided by a trusted intermediary or third party nominated by the publisher. Note the web page can include information about specific national requirements or voluntary conformance reports

entries.heading: Publisher’s web page for detailed accessibility information
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the URL of a web page giving further detailed description of the accessibility features, compatibility, testing etc relevant to this product. The web page should be provided by the publisher. Note the web page can include information about specific national requirements or voluntary conformance reports

entries.heading: Compatibility tested
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the URL of a web page giving a short description of compatibility testing carried out for this product, including detailed compatibility with various assistive technology such as third-party screen-reading software. See also code 00 for a summary of the accessibility features of the product itself

entries.heading: Trusted Intermediary contact
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the e-mail address for a contact at a ‘trusted intermediary’, to whom detailed questions about accessibility for this product may be directed. This information is recommended where a title has some limitations to its accessibility or may present difficulties for some complex accessibility needs. This information can also be included using <ProductContactRole> and code 01 from list 198, where the publisher delegates all responsibility for accessibility queries to the trusted intermediary

entries.heading: Publisher contact for further accessibility information
entries.note: <ProductFormFeatureDescription> carries the e-mail address for a contact at the publisher to whom detailed questions about accessibility of this product may be directed. This information is recommended where a title has some limitations to its accessibility or may present difficulties for some complex accessibility needs. This information can also be included using <ProductContactRole> and code 01 from list 198, particularly if the publisher does not delegate responsibility to a trusted intermediary

entries.heading: Proprietary collection sequence type
entries.note: A short explanatory label for the sequence should be provided in <CollectionSequenceTypeName>

entries.heading: Title order
entries.note: Order as specified by the title, eg by volume or part number sequence, provided for confirmation

entries.heading: Publication order
entries.note: Order of publication of products within the collection

entries.heading: Temporal / narrative order
entries.note: Order defined by a continuing narrative or temporal sequence within products in the collection. Applicable to either fiction or to non-fiction (eg within a collection of history textbooks)

entries.heading: Original publication order
entries.note: Original publication order, for a republished collection or collected works originally published outside a collection

entries.heading: Suggested reading order
entries.note: Where it is different from the title order, publication order, narrative order etc

entries.heading: Suggested display order
entries.note: Where it is different from the title order, publication order, narrative order, reading order etc

entries.heading: Metadata contact
entries.note: For queries and feedback concerning the metadata record itself

entries.heading: Accessibility request contact
entries.note: Eg for requests for supply of mutable digital files for conversion to other formats

entries.heading: Promotional contact
entries.note: Eg for requests relating to interviews, author events

entries.heading: Advertising contact
entries.note: Eg for co-op advertising

entries.heading: Review copy contact
entries.note: Eg for requests for review copies

entries.heading: Evaluation copy contact
entries.note: Eg for requests for approval or evaluation copies (particularly within education)

entries.heading: Permissions contact
entries.note: Eg for requests to reproduce or repurpose parts of the publication

entries.heading: Return authorization contact
entries.note: Eg for use where authorization must be gained from the publisher rather than the distributor or wholesaler

entries.heading: CIP / Legal deposit contact
entries.note: Eg for legal deposit or long-term preservation

entries.heading: Rights and licensing contact
entries.note: Eg for subrights licensing, collective licensing

entries.heading: Product safety contact
entries.note: Eg for EU General product safety regulation (GPSR) compliance. See https://commission.europa.eu/business-economy-euro/product-safety-and-requirements/product-safety/general-product-safety-regulation_en

entries.heading: Product raw materials contact
entries.note: Eg for EU Deforestation regulation (EUDR) compliance. See https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115&qid=1687867231461

entries.heading: Customer services contact
entries.note: For general enquiries

entries.heading: Any adult audience
entries.note: The publisher states that the product is suitable for any adult audience

entries.heading: Content advice
entries.note: The publisher advises the content may offend or distress parts of the adult audience (for any reason)

entries.heading: Content advice (sex)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content of an explicit sexual nature

entries.heading: Content advice (violence)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content of an extreme violent nature

entries.heading: Content advice (drugs)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content involving severe misuse of drugs or alcohol

entries.heading: Content advice (language)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes extreme / offensive / explicit language

entries.heading: Content advice (intolerance)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content involving severe intolerance or abuse of particular groups (eg religious, ethnic, racial, gendered and other social groups)

entries.heading: Content advice (abuse)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content involving sexual or extreme domestic abuse (including both mental and physical abuse)

entries.heading: Content advice (self-harm)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content involving severe self-harm (including serious eating disorders)

entries.heading: Content advice (animal cruelty)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content involving extreme cruelty to animals

entries.heading: Content advice (illness)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content involving serious chronic or acute illness (mental or physical)

entries.heading: Content advice (death and grief)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content relating to severe emotional distress resulting from death and grief

entries.heading: Content advice (suicide)
entries.note: The publisher advises the product includes content relating to suicide

entries.heading: Unspecified
entries.note: Unspecified, contact supplier for details

entries.heading: Consignment
entries.note: The retailer pays for goods only after they are sold by the retailer to an end consumer, and may return excess unsold inventory to the supplier at any time. The goods remain the property of the supplier until they are paid for, even while they are physically located at the retailer

entries.heading: Firm sale
entries.note: The retailer is invoiced for the goods immediately (or upon dispatch) and pays within the specified credit period, as in the sale or return model, but any excess unsold inventory cannot be returned to the supplier

entries.heading: Sale or return
entries.note: Contact supplier for applicable returns authorization process. The retailer is invoiced for the goods immediately (or upon dispatch) and pays within the specified credit period, but can return excess unsold inventory to the supplier for full credit at a later date. Some kind of returns authorization process is normally required. Returns must be in saleable condition, except when return of stripped covers or proof of destruction may be allowed instead. For more detail, use codes 05, 06 or 07

entries.heading: Direct fulfillment
entries.note: The retailer pays for goods only after they are sold by the retailer to an end consumer, but all inventory remains physically located at the supplier (thus there can be no retailer returns of unsold inventory). When ordered by the retailer, the goods are delivered direct to the end consumer

entries.heading: Sale or return of saleable copies
entries.note: Contact supplier for applicable returns authorization process. As for code 03, but only returns of saleable copies will be accepted. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Sale or return of stripped covers
entries.note: Contact supplier for applicable cover returns authorization process. As for code 03, but only returns of stripped covers will be accepted. An additional barcode will likely be required on cover 2 (inside front cover) to facilitate scanning of returned covers. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Sale or certified destruction
entries.note: Contact supplier for applicable destruction certification process. As for code 03, but only certified destruction will be accepted. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

entries.heading: Exactly
entries.note: The supplier’s true figure, or at least a best estimate expected to be within 10% of the true figure (ie a quoted figure of 100 could in fact be anything between 91 and 111)

entries.heading: Approximately
entries.note: Generally interpreted as within 25% of the true figure (ie a quoted figure of 100 could in fact be anything between 80 and 133). The supplier may introduce a deliberate approximation to reduce the commercial sensitivity of the figure

entries.heading: About
entries.note: Generally interpreted as within a factor of two of the true figure (ie a quoted figure of 100 could in fact be anything between 50 and 200). The supplier may introduce a deliberate approximation to reduce the commercial sensitivity of the figure

entries.heading: Mean daily sale

entries.heading: Maximum daily sale

entries.heading: Minimum weekly sale

entries.heading: Proprietary price identifier scheme
entries.note: Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required for proprietary price identifiers

entries.heading: Proprietary price point identifier scheme
entries.note: Proprietary identifier uniquely identifies price amount and currency. Two unrelated products with the same price amount carry the same identifier, though their price types may be different. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required for proprietary price identifiers

entries.heading: Proprietary price type identifier scheme
entries.note: Proprietary identifier uniquely identifies price type, qualifier and any constraints and conditions. Two unrelated products with the same price type carry the same identifier, though their price points may be different. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required for proprietary price identifiers

entries.heading: Proprietary price point and type identifier scheme
entries.note: Proprietary identifier identifies a unique combination of price point and type, though two unrelated products may carry the same identifier if all details of their prices are identical. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required for proprietary price identifiers

entries.heading: Proprietary unique price identifier scheme
entries.note: Proprietary identifier is unique to a single price point, price type and product. No two products can carry the same identifier, even if all details of their prices are identical. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required for proprietary price identifiers

entries.heading: Proprietary product price point identifier scheme
entries.note: Proprietary identifier uniquely identifies a specific combination of product, price amount and currency, independent of the price type. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required for proprietary price identifiers

entries.heading: Proprietary product price type identifier scheme
entries.note: Proprietary identifier uniquely identifies a specific combination of product, price type, qualifier and any constraints and conditions, independent of the price amount and currency. A product with the same product price type identifier may carry differing price amounts, currencies at different points in time. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required for proprietary price identifiers

entries.heading: Human readable
entries.note: Document (eg Word file, PDF or web page) intended for the lay reader

entries.heading: Professional readable
entries.note: Document (eg Word file, PDF or web page) intended for the legal specialist reader

entries.heading: Human readable additional license
entries.note: Document (eg Word file, PDF or web page) intended for the lay reader, expressing an additional license that may be separately obtained covering uses of the content that are not granted by the intrinsic product license (the license expressed by code 01)

entries.heading: Professional readable additional license
entries.note: Document (eg Word file, PDF or web page) intended for the legal specialist reader, expressing an additional license that may be separately obtained covering uses of the content that are not granted by the intrinsic product license (the license expressed by code 02)

entries.heading: ODRL
entries.note: Open Digital Rights Language (ODRL) in JSON-LD format. Used for example to express TDM licenses using the W3C TDM Reservation Protocol

entries.heading: ODRL additional license
entries.note: Open Digital Rights Language (ODRL) in JSON-LD format. Used for example to express additional TDM licenses that may be separately obtained covering uses of the content that are not granted by the intrinsic product license (the license expressed by code 20), using the W3C TDM Reservation Protocol

entries.heading: Copyright
entries.note: Text or image copyright (normally indicated by the © symbol). The default if no <CopyrightType> is specified

entries.heading: Phonogram right
entries.note: Phonogram copyright or neighboring right (normally indicated by the ℗ symbol)

entries.heading: Database right
entries.note: Sui generis database right
